  • Representation variant where required

ETags must not leak secrets.

docs.title: If-Match
docs.text:
Update or delete commands may require:

If-Match: "resource-version"

Missing required precondition may return a precondition-required error.

docs.title: Concurrency Failure
docs.text:
When the version changed:

  • Do not apply partial mutation.
  • Return current version or ETag where safe.
  • Provide conflict code.
  • Allow client reload and comparison.

docs.title: Immutable Resources
docs.text: Immutable resources may use ETag for caching but do not require mutation preconditions because mutation is not allowed.

docs.title: Conditional Reads
docs.text:
Read endpoints may support:

  • If-None-Match
  • If-Modified-Since

A matching condition returns 304 without a body.

docs.title: Create Resource Convention
docs.text:
Create endpoints use:

POST /resources

On success:

  • Return 201
  • Return resource representation
  • Include Location
  • Include ETag if mutable

docs.title: Replace Convention
docs.text:
Full replacement may use:

PUT /resources/{id}

Version 1 should use PUT sparingly because many domain resources are not safely replaceable as whole documents.

docs.title: Partial Update Convention
docs.text:
Partial updates may use:

PATCH /resources/{id}

The API must choose and document one patch format.

For domain-heavy mutations, explicit command routes are preferred.

docs.title: Delete Convention
docs.text:
Deletion uses:

DELETE /resources/{id}

Most ChannelForge entities archive rather than hard-delete.

The route contract must state whether DELETE means:

  • Archive
  • Revoke
  • Remove child relationship
  • Hard delete

Hard deletion should require an explicit administrative command.

docs.title: Archive Command
docs.text:
Explicit archive may use:

POST /resources/{id}/archive

This is clearer where DELETE semantics would be misleading.

docs.title: Restore Command
docs.text:
Restore from archive may use:

POST /resources/{id}/restore

docs.title: Domain Command Routes
docs.text:
Domain actions use explicit subresources or commands.

Examples:

POST /schedule-plans/{planId}/validate
POST /schedule-plans/{planId}/approve
POST /schedule-plans/{planId}/reject
POST /channels/{channelId}/publish
POST /channels/{channelId}/restart
POST /media-sources/{mediaSourceId}/synchronize

docs.title: Command Response
docs.text:
An immediate command may return:

  • Updated resource
  • Command result
  • 204

A long-running command returns:

  • 202
  • Background Job representation
  • Location to job
  • Optional target resource link

docs.title: Safe Methods
docs.text:
GET and HEAD must not perform domain mutations.

A cache refresh or health observation caused incidentally by GET must not alter editorial state.

docs.title: Search
docs.text:
Search may use:

GET /catalog-items?search=...

Search behavior must define:

  • Normalization
  • Fields searched
  • Ranking
  • Maximum query length
  • Stable tie-break
  • Archived inclusion
  • Availability filters

docs.title: Filtering
docs.text:
Filters use query parameters.

Examples:

?mediaKind=MOVIE
?availability=AVAILABLE
?networkId=net_...
?state=DRAFT

Repeated fields or comma-separated values must follow one consistent convention.

docs.title: Filter Operators
docs.text:
Version 1 should use a bounded documented set.

Potential operators:

  • Equal
  • Not equal
  • Greater than
  • Greater than or equal
  • Less than
  • Less than or equal
  • In
  • Contains
  • Exists
  • Date range

Avoid exposing arbitrary SQL-like expressions.

docs.title: Nested Filters
docs.text: Complex selector authoring may use typed JSON command bodies rather than unbounded query-string expressions.

docs.title: Sorting
docs.text:
Sort may use:

?sort=displayName
?sort=-createdAt

A leading minus may indicate descending order.

Every sort includes a stable final ID tie-break.

docs.title: Default Sorting
docs.text: Every collection endpoint declares a deterministic default sort.

docs.title: Unsupported Sort
docs.text: Unsupported sort fields return a validation error.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text: Cursor-based pagination is preferred for large mutable collections.

docs.title: Cursor Properties
docs.text:
A cursor must be:

  • Opaque
  • Signed or integrity-protected where needed
  • Bound to filter and sort
  • Bounded in size
  • Expiring only when documented
  • Safe to log only if it contains no secrets

docs.title: Cursor Request
docs.text:
Example:

?limit=50&cursor=...

docs.title: Page Limit
docs.text:
Each endpoint defines:

  • Default limit
  • Maximum limit

Requests above maximum are rejected or clamped according to documented policy.

Rejecting is clearer for automation.

docs.title: Total Counts
docs.text:
Total counts may be omitted for expensive queries.

When provided, the response states whether count is exact or estimated.

docs.title: Stable Pagination
docs.text: Pagination must not depend on unspecified database order.

docs.title: Offset Pagination
docs.text:
Offset pagination may be used for:

  • Small administrative lists
  • Static snapshots
  • Audit export pages

It should not be the default for large mutable catalogs.

docs.title: Field Selection
docs.text: Version 1 may support limited field expansion rather than arbitrary sparse fieldsets.

docs.title: Expansion
docs.text:
Example:

?include=sourceBindings,playbackVariants

Expansion must be bounded to avoid enormous responses.

docs.title: Default Representation
docs.text:
Default list representations should be summaries.

Detailed child collections use dedicated routes or explicit inclusion.

docs.title: Maximum Response Size
docs.text:
Endpoints must bound response size through:

  • Pagination
  • Expansion limits
  • Field limits
  • Streaming export
  • Compression where appropriate

docs.title: Compression
docs.text:
JSON and artifact responses may use HTTP compression.

Live MPEG-TS and already-compressed media should not be recompressed by the web server.

docs.title: Long-Running Operations
docs.text:
Long-running work returns a Background Job.

Examples:

  • Full synchronization
  • Schedule generation
  • Artifact generation
  • Backup
  • Restore preparation
  • Projection rebuild
  • Integrity check
  • Large import
  • Diagnostic export

docs.title: Background Job Resource
docs.text:
Suggested representation:

{
  "id": "job_...",
  "jobType": "GENERATE_SCHEDULE",
  "state": "RUNNING",
  "progress": {
    "current": 420,
    "total": 1000,
    "unit": "entries"
  },
  "requestedAt": "2026-07-27T18:42:31.123Z",
  "startedAt": "2026-07-27T18:42:32.001Z",
  "completedAt": null,
  "result": null,
  "error": null
}

docs.title: Job Polling
docs.text:
Clients may poll:

GET /background-jobs/{jobId}

Polling guidance may be included through:

  • Retry-After
  • Progress state
  • Suggested poll interval

docs.title: Job Cancellation
docs.text:
Cancellation may use:

POST /background-jobs/{jobId}/cancel

Cancellation is a request, not guaranteed immediate termination.

docs.title: Job Result
docs.text:
On success, result may contain links to:

  • Schedule Plan
  • Synchronization Run
  • Backup
  • Artifact
  • Diagnostic bundle

Large results are not embedded in the job representation.

docs.title: Job Failure
docs.text: A failed job contains structured error data and diagnostic link where authorized.

docs.title: Job Events
docs.text:
Version 1 may optionally expose Server-Sent Events for Background Job updates.

Polling remains the required baseline.

docs.title: Server-Sent Events
docs.text:
Potential use:

  • Job progress
  • Runtime state
  • Source synchronization status
  • Health changes

SSE is deferred unless implementation cost is justified.

docs.title: WebSocket
docs.text: WebSocket is not required for version 1.

docs.title: Bulk Operations
docs.text:
Bulk operations are explicit and bounded.

Examples:

  • Apply label to Catalog Items
  • Archive multiple Catalog Items
  • Validate multiple Plans
  • Delete multiple stale jobs
  • Reorder Channel list

docs.title: Bulk Request
docs.text:
A bulk request includes:

  • Item IDs
  • Command parameters
  • Atomicity mode
  • Idempotency Key where applicable

docs.title: Bulk Atomicity Modes
docs.text:
Suggested modes:

  • ALL_OR_NOTHING
  • BEST_EFFORT

The endpoint declares supported modes.

docs.title: Bulk Response
docs.text:
Best-effort response includes per-item results.

Example:

{
  "results": [
    {
      "id": "cat_1",
      "status": "SUCCEEDED"
    },
    {
      "id": "cat_2",
      "status": "FAILED",
      "error": {
        "code": "NOT_FOUND"
      }
    }
  ]
}

docs.title: Bulk Limits
docs.text:
Every bulk endpoint has a maximum item count.

Large work becomes a Background Job.

docs.title: File Uploads
docs.text:
Uploads may use:

  • Multipart form data
  • Preflight resource followed by upload
  • Direct managed upload endpoint

Version 1 should prefer a simple bounded multipart flow for local deployments.

docs.title: Upload Lifecycle
docs.text:
Suggested flow:

  1. Authorize.
  2. Validate request metadata.
  3. Stream to temporary storage.
  4. Enforce size limit.
  5. Validate file signature.
  6. Calculate checksum.
  7. Validate dimensions or media metadata.
  8. Move to managed storage.
  9. Create resource.
  10. Return representation.

docs.title: Upload Error Cleanup
docs.text: Failed uploads must remove temporary files.

docs.title: File Downloads
docs.text:
Downloads should:

  • Authorize
  • Set safe content type
  • Set safe filename
  • Support conditional requests where useful
  • Avoid path exposure
  • Stream without loading entire file into memory
  • Record audit for sensitive downloads

docs.title: Content-Disposition
docs.text:
User-downloadable files may use attachment disposition.

Filenames are sanitized.

docs.title: Range Requests for Files
docs.text:
Static artifacts may support byte ranges where useful.

Live Channel streams follow stream-specific behavior.

docs.title: Import APIs
docs.text:
Imports should use:

  1. Upload or source selection.
  2. Parse and validate.
  3. Produce preview.
  4. Resolve conflicts.
  5. Apply through Background Job.
  6. Return result report.

Imports must not apply destructive changes without explicit confirmation.

docs.title: Export APIs
docs.text:
Exports may be synchronous when small or asynchronous when large.

Exports include a schema version.

docs.title: OpenAPI
docs.text:
The Management API must have an OpenAPI description.

The description includes:

  • Routes
  • Methods
  • Parameters
  • Request schemas
  • Response schemas
  • Error schemas
  • Authentication
  • Permissions where possible
  • Examples
  • Deprecation
  • Enumeration values

docs.title: OpenAPI Source of Truth
docs.text:
The implementation must choose one approach:

  • Code-first generation
  • Contract-first generation
  • Hybrid with validation

Drift between runtime and specification must fail CI.

docs.title: Schema Reuse
docs.text:
Common schemas include:

  • Error
  • Validation violation
  • Page
  • Link
  • Background Job
  • Audit metadata
  • Timestamp
  • Duration
  • Resource version

docs.title: OpenAPI Security
docs.text: Examples must not contain real credentials or internal URLs.

docs.title: API Documentation
docs.text:
Documentation should include:

  • Getting started
  • Authentication
  • Common workflows
  • Error handling
  • Pagination
  • Idempotency
  • Concurrency
  • Webhooks
  • Output endpoints
  • Deprecation

docs.title: Client Generation
docs.text:
OpenAPI may support generated clients.

Generated clients are secondary to contract clarity.

The API must not contort domain semantics solely for one generator.

docs.title: Resource Links
docs.text:
Representations may include links.

Example:

{
  "links": {
    "self": "/api/v1/channels/chn_...",
    "network": "/api/v1/networks/net_...",
    "schedulePlans": "/api/v1/channels/chn_.../schedule-plans"
  }
}

Links are additive and optional for clients.

  • Read instance settings
  • Update mutable settings
  • Read feature flags
  • Read supported capabilities

Suggested operations:

  • Sign out

docs.title: Media Source Secrets
docs.text:
Create or rotate responses never return stored secret values.

A response may return:

docs.title: Catalog Endpoints

docs.title: Catalog Item Summary
docs.text:
List responses should include enough information for programming selection:

  • ID
  • Media kind
  • Title
  • Series context
  • Year
  • Duration
  • Availability
  • Artwork summary
  • Source count
  • Conflict state

docs.title: Source Binding Representation
docs.text:
A Source Binding representation may expose:

  • Provider type
  • Media Source ID
  • External item ID
  • Library
  • State
  • Last seen
  • Match state
  • Availability

It must not expose provider credentials or signed access URLs.

docs.title: Playback Variant Representation
docs.text: A Playback Variant representation may expose technical metadata but not restricted runtime access descriptors.

docs.title: Conflict Resolution Commands
docs.text:
Conflict resolution commands require:

  • Expected conflict version
  • Resolution type
  • Target IDs
  • Operator note where required
  • Preview where destructive

docs.title: Network Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested operations:

  • List Networks
  • Create Network
  • Read Network
  • Update mutable identity
  • Archive Network

  • Read programming revisions
  • Create programming draft
  • Update programming draft

docs.title: Revision Endpoints
docs.text:
Revision routes should preserve immutability.

Example:

POST /channels/{channelId}/programming-revisions
PATCH /programming-revisions/{revisionId}
POST /programming-revisions/{revisionId}/validate
POST /programming-revisions/{revisionId}/approve
POST /channels/{channelId}/activate-programming-revision

Approved revisions do not accept PATCH.

docs.title: Schedule Generation Endpoint
docs.text:
A schedule generation request may include:

  • Horizon
  • Mode
  • Configuration revision
  • Existing plan
  • Regeneration range
  • Seed
  • Approval policy
  • Diagnostic verbosity
  • Idempotency Key

The endpoint returns a Background Job.

docs.title: Schedule Plan Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested operations:

  • Read Schedule Plan

  • Compare plans
  • Read generation explanation
  • Regenerate range
  • Lock entry
  • Unlock entry

docs.title: Schedule Entry Pagination
docs.text:
Timeline reads may paginate by time range rather than generic cursor.

Parameters may include:

  • start
  • end
  • limit
  • cursor

The result remains ordered by start and sequence.

docs.title: Schedule Plan Approval
docs.text:
Approval requires:

  • If-Match or expected plan state
  • Validation Result ID
  • Warning acknowledgments
  • Optional note
  • Permission

Approval is idempotent only with an Idempotency Key.

docs.title: Publication Endpoints

  • Schedule future publication
  • Roll back to prior publication

docs.title: Publish Command
docs.text:
A publish request includes:

  • Effective time

docs.title: Runtime Endpoints
docs.text:

docs.title: Runtime Command Safety
docs.text:
Runtime commands must distinguish:

  • Editorial changes
  • Operational recovery
  • Diagnostic test

A runtime restart must not mutate the Schedule Plan.

docs.title: Background Job Endpoints

  • Cancel job

Audit search supports:

Audit details require elevated permission.

docs.title: Liveness
docs.text:
Liveness indicates whether the process can respond.

It should not perform expensive dependency checks.

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
Readiness indicates whether the instance can serve normal management traffic.

It may consider:

  • Database
  • Migrations
  • Storage
  • Startup reconciliation
  • Critical configuration

docs.title: Detailed Health
docs.text:
Authenticated detailed health may include:

  • Database
  • Managed storage
  • Media Sources
  • Artifact freshness
  • Job queue
  • Playout
  • Clock
  • Backup freshness

docs.title: Backup Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested operations:

  • List backups
  • Start backup
  • Read backup
  • Verify backup
  • Download backup
  • Delete backup
  • Prepare restore
  • Confirm restore
  • Read restore status

Restore requires a multi-step confirmation flow.

docs.title: Restore Confirmation
docs.text:
Restore should require:

  • Backup verification
  • Explicit confirmation token
  • Current administrator authentication
  • Maintenance acknowledgment
  • Optional typed instance name
  • Idempotency Key

docs.title: Template Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested operations:

  • List Templates
  • Create Template
  • Read Template
  • Create revision
  • Update draft revision
  • Validate
  • Approve
  • Apply to Network or Channel
  • Archive

docs.title: Programming Pack Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested operations:

  • List installed Packs
  • Import Pack
  • Preview Pack
  • Read Pack
  • Apply Pack
  • Update Pack
  • Disable Pack
  • Uninstall Pack where safe

Pack import is treated as untrusted data.

docs.title: Output Artifact Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested routes:

/xmltv/{instanceOrProfile}.xml
/playlist/{instanceOrProfile}.m3u
/api/v1/output-artifacts/{artifactId}
/api/v1/channels/{channelId}/logo

Exact public aliases are configurable.

docs.title: XMLTV Endpoint
docs.text:
The XMLTV endpoint:

  • Serves last valid active artifact
  • Uses correct content type
  • Supports ETag
  • Supports Last-Modified
  • May require access token
  • Does not generate synchronously on every request
  • Returns controlled error when no valid artifact exists

docs.title: M3U Endpoint
docs.text:
The M3U endpoint:

  • Serves last valid playlist
  • Uses correct content type
  • Uses configured public base URL
  • Does not expose provider tokens
  • May embed ChannelForge stream access tokens according to policy
  • Supports ETag

docs.title: Logo Endpoint
docs.text:
Logo responses:

  • Use managed or proxied artwork
  • Hide provider credentials
  • Validate MIME type
  • Support caching
  • Use stable Channel identity

docs.title: Streaming Endpoint
docs.text:
Suggested route:

/stream/channels/{channelId}

Possible protocol variants may use:

/stream/channels/{channelId}.ts
/stream/channels/{channelId}/index.m3u8

Exact route design is implementation-specific.

docs.title: Stream Authentication
docs.text:
Stream authentication may use:

  • Browser session
  • API token
  • Signed stream token
  • Local-network policy
  • Reverse-proxy authentication

docs.title: Stream Errors
docs.text:
Before output starts, the endpoint may return an HTTP error.

After output starts, failures are represented through stream termination, recovery content, or protocol-specific behavior.

A JSON error body must not be inserted into a media stream.

docs.title: Stream Response Headers
docs.text:
Headers may include:

  • Content type
  • Cache control
  • Connection behavior
  • Request ID
  • Optional Channel identity
  • CORS policy

docs.title: HDHomeRun-Compatible Endpoints
docs.text:
Potential endpoints include:

  • Discovery document
  • Device description
  • Lineup
  • Lineup status
  • Channel stream URLs

These endpoints follow expected compatibility shapes rather than the standard Management API error envelope where protocol compatibility requires it.

docs.title: Protocol Compatibility Boundary
docs.text: HDHomeRun-compatible shapes must be isolated from canonical domain models.

docs.title: Webhook Endpoints
docs.text:
Suggested route:

/webhooks/media-sources/{mediaSourceId}/{provider}

Webhook endpoints:

  • Use provider-specific verification
  • Return quickly
  • Queue targeted synchronization
  • Deduplicate
  • Apply rate limits
  • Never expose management resources

docs.title: Webhook Response
docs.text:
A valid accepted webhook usually returns:

  • 202 Accepted, or
  • Provider-required success response

Invalid authentication returns a provider-compatible error without excess detail.

docs.title: Outbound Webhooks
docs.text:
Future outbound webhooks may notify external systems.

Version 1 may defer outbound webhooks.

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Rate limiting protects:

  • Authentication
  • Setup
  • Expensive searches
  • Synchronization commands
  • Backup commands
  • Diagnostics
  • Streaming token creation
  • Webhook ingress

docs.title: Rate Limit Dimensions
docs.text:
Limits may apply by:

  • IP classification
  • User
  • API token
  • Route
  • Resource
  • Media Source
  • Instance

docs.title: Rate Limit Response
docs.text:
A limited request returns:

  • 429
  • Stable error code
  • Retry-After where known
  • Request ID

docs.title: Capacity Limits
docs.text:
Resource exhaustion may return 503 rather than 429.

Example:

  • No transcode capacity
  • Database maintenance
  • Restore in progress
  • Instance shutting down

docs.title: Abuse Protection
docs.text:
Controls include:

  • Request body limits
  • Header limits
  • Query length limits
  • Pagination limits
  • Bulk limits
  • Upload limits
  • Authentication throttling
  • Webhook limits
  • Background Job deduplication
  • Stream session limits

docs.title: Timeouts
docs.text:
Management requests have bounded timeouts.

Long work becomes a Background Job.

Stream responses use stream-specific timeout policy.

docs.title: Cancellation on Disconnect
docs.text:
For ordinary reads, server work may be cancelled when the client disconnects.

For accepted Background Jobs, client disconnect does not cancel the job.

docs.title: Maintenance Mode
docs.text:
During maintenance or restore:

  • Liveness remains available.
  • Readiness may fail.
  • Management writes return controlled 503.
  • Existing artifacts may remain available.
  • Streaming behavior follows maintenance policy.
  • Restore endpoints remain restricted.

docs.title: Deprecation
docs.text:
Deprecated routes or fields are:

  • Marked in OpenAPI
  • Documented
  • Logged for usage
  • Given replacement
  • Assigned removal target
  • Not silently removed

docs.title: Deprecation Headers
docs.text:
Responses may include:

  • Deprecation indicator
  • Sunset date
  • Documentation link

Exact header names follow implementation standards.

docs.title: Compatibility Aliases
docs.text:
Temporary aliases may preserve inherited Tunarr endpoints.

Compatibility aliases must:

  • Be isolated
  • Be documented
  • Use translation adapters
  • Avoid becoming canonical
  • Emit deprecation metadata
  • Have removal criteria

docs.title: Tunarr API Compatibility
docs.text:
Inherited Tunarr API routes may remain operational during migration.

New ChannelForge UI and services should target ChannelForge v1 routes.

Compatibility behavior must not leak legacy database shapes into new contracts.

docs.title: Legacy Identifier Resolution
docs.text:
Compatibility routes may accept legacy IDs and resolve them through mapping.

Canonical responses use ChannelForge IDs.

docs.title: API Gateway Boundary
docs.text:
Version 1 does not require a separate API gateway.

The application server may provide:

  • Routing
  • Authentication
  • Rate limiting
  • Request IDs
  • Compression
  • CORS
  • OpenAPI

A reverse proxy may provide TLS and connection management.

docs.title: Reverse Proxy Headers
docs.text:
Forwarded headers are trusted only from configured proxy addresses.

The application must prevent host-header and scheme spoofing.

docs.title: Public URL Construction
docs.text:
Public links derive from:

  1. Explicit configured public base URL
  2. Trusted reverse-proxy headers
  3. Safe request origin
  4. Local fallback

docs.title: Security Headers
docs.text:
Management responses should use appropriate headers for:

  • Content type
  • Clickjacking protection
  • MIME sniffing protection
  • Referrer policy
  • Content Security Policy for HTML surfaces
  • HSTS where TLS termination and deployment policy permit

docs.title: Management Resources
docs.text: Authenticated management responses are generally private or no-store where sensitive.

docs.title: Immutable Resources
docs.text: Approved Plans, revision snapshots, and artifacts may use ETag and longer private caching.

docs.title: Public Artifacts
docs.text: XMLTV, M3U, and logos may use conditional caching according to access policy.

docs.title: Stream Responses
docs.text: Live streams generally prevent intermediary caching.

docs.title: Sensitive Response Fields
docs.text:
Sensitive fields include:

  • Credential values
  • Token hashes
  • Signed source URLs
  • Cookies
  • Secret headers
  • Local paths where restricted
  • Password state details
  • Encryption keys
  • Raw provider payloads

They are omitted or redacted.

docs.title: Administrative Diagnostics
docs.text:
Detailed diagnostics may expose:

  • Redacted FFmpeg command
  • Source failure
  • Provider response metadata
  • Database health
  • Job traces

Diagnostics require permission and are audited.

docs.title: Logging
docs.text:
Request logs should include:

  • Request ID
  • Actor ID
  • Token ID prefix where appropriate
  • Route template
  • Method
  • Status
  • Duration
  • Response size
  • Error code
  • Correlation ID
  • Client address classification

Logs should not include:

  • Authorization header
  • Cookies
  • Request bodies by default
  • Signed URLs
  • Secrets
  • Uploaded binary content

docs.title: Metrics
docs.text:
Suggested API metrics:

  • Request count
  • Status count
  • Latency
  • Active requests
  • Request size
  • Response size
  • Authentication failures
  • Authorization failures
  • Validation failures
  • Concurrency conflicts
  • Idempotency replays
  • Rate-limit events
  • Background Job acceptance
  • Stream connections
  • Webhook receipts

docs.title: Tracing
docs.text:
Potential spans:

  • Authenticate
  • Authorize
  • Validate request
  • Load aggregate
  • Execute command
  • Persist transaction
  • Queue Background Job
  • Serialize response
  • Resolve stream session
  • Serve artifact

docs.title: Privacy
docs.text:
API logs and audit must minimize personal data.

Remote addresses may be:

  • Truncated
  • Classified
  • Retained for bounded periods
  • Restricted to security diagnostics

docs.title: Localization
docs.text:
Version 1 API error codes are language-neutral.

Human-readable messages may initially be English.

Clients should rely on error codes, not message text.

docs.title: Date and Time Localization
docs.text:
The API returns canonical UTC timestamps and explicit time-zone identifiers.

Formatting for local display is a client concern.

docs.title: Contract Tests
docs.text:
Every route requires tests for:

  • Authentication
  • Authorization
  • Valid request
  • Invalid request
  • Not found
  • Conflict
  • Concurrency
  • Idempotency
  • Response schema
  • Error schema
  • Request ID
  • Sensitive field omission

docs.title: OpenAPI Tests
docs.text:
Tests should verify:

  • Every implemented Management route appears in OpenAPI.
  • Every documented route exists.
  • Request schemas match runtime validation.
  • Response schemas match runtime output.
  • Error responses use common schema.
  • Security declarations match runtime.
  • Deprecated routes are marked.
  • Examples validate.

docs.title: Authentication Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Valid session
  • Expired session
  • Revoked session
  • Valid API token
  • Expired API token
  • Revoked API token
  • Missing scope
  • Setup token lifecycle
  • Reverse-proxy spoof attempt
  • CSRF failure

docs.title: Authorization Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover every permission boundary.

A route must not rely only on hidden UI controls.

docs.title: Validation Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Missing field
  • Unknown field
  • Wrong type
  • Oversized string
  • Invalid enumeration
  • Invalid timestamp
  • Invalid time zone
  • Invalid URL
  • Excessive array
  • Malformed JSON
  • Unsupported media type

docs.title: Idempotency Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Same key and request
  • Same key and different request
  • Concurrent duplicate requests
  • Job creation replay
  • Expired key
  • Actor scope
  • Failure replay policy

docs.title: Concurrency Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Correct ETag
  • Stale ETag
  • Missing required If-Match
  • Concurrent update
  • Archive conflict
  • Approval race
  • Publication race

docs.title: Pagination Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • First page
  • Next page
  • Stable ordering
  • Filter-bound cursor
  • Sort-bound cursor
  • Invalid cursor
  • Maximum limit
  • Mutation between pages
  • Archived inclusion

docs.title: Error Tests
docs.text:
Tests should verify:

  • Stable code
  • Correct status
  • Request ID
  • No stack trace
  • No secrets
  • Validation violations
  • Retry metadata
  • Conflict details

docs.title: Upload Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Valid image
  • Oversized image
  • Wrong MIME
  • Wrong file signature
  • Path-like filename
  • Interrupted upload
  • Duplicate checksum
  • Temporary cleanup
  • Unauthorized upload

docs.title: Stream Endpoint Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Authorization
  • First client
  • Shared client
  • Late join
  • Client disconnect
  • No publication
  • No source
  • Recovery
  • Correct content type
  • No JSON after stream start
  • Token expiration behavior

docs.title: Artifact Endpoint Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Valid XMLTV
  • Valid M3U
  • ETag
  • 304
  • Missing artifact
  • Prior valid artifact
  • Authenticated and public policy
  • Logo caching
  • Public base URL

docs.title: HDHomeRun Compatibility Tests
docs.text:
Tests should validate expected:

  • Discovery shape
  • Device identity
  • Lineup shape
  • Channel URLs
  • Tuner limits
  • Error behavior
  • Stable Channel identity

docs.title: Webhook Tests
docs.text:
Tests should cover:

  • Valid signature
  • Invalid signature
  • Replay
  • Duplicate event
  • Oversized payload
  • Unknown source
  • Rate limit
  • Fast acceptance
  • Background Job enqueue
  • No direct catalog mutation

docs.title: Performance Tests
docs.text:
Performance tests should measure:

  • Catalog list
  • Catalog search
  • Schedule timeline
  • Background Job polling
  • XMLTV download
  • M3U download
  • Concurrent runtime status
  • Stream attachment
  • Authentication throughput
  • Large audit query
  • OpenAPI generation

docs.title: Reference Create Channel Request
docs.text:
POST /api/v1/channels
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Content-Type: application/json
Idempotency-Key: 8fd763c8-9f2d-46cb-9c59-64756d2bbf93

{
  "networkId": "net_...",
  "displayName": "Night Signal",
  "channelNumber": {
    "major": 107,
    "minor": null
  },
  "timeZone": "America/Los_Angeles"
}

Successful response:

201 Created
Location: /api/v1/channels/chn_...
ETag: "chn-1"

docs.title: Reference Concurrency Failure
docs.text:
Request:

PATCH /api/v1/channels/chn_...
If-Match: "chn-4"
Content-Type: application/json

Current server version is 5.

Response:

412 Precondition Failed

{
  "error": {
    "code": "PRECONDITION_FAILED",
    "message": "The Channel changed after it was loaded.",
    "status": 412,
    "requestId": "req_...",
    "details": {
      "currentEtag": "\"chn-5\""
    },
    "violations": []
  }
}

docs.text:
Request:

POST /api/v1/channels/chn_.../schedule-generations
Authorization: Bearer <token>
Idempotency-Key: 487f137d-6112-4cf9-b787-11c130d51239
Content-Type: application/json

{
  "mode": "FULL",
  "horizon": {
    "start": "2026-08-01T07:00:00Z",
    "end": "2026-08-08T07:00:00Z"
  },
  "programmingRevisionId": "pgr_...",
