docs.title: Milestone 03: Identity, Persistence, and Migrations
docs.text:
• Roadmap version: 0.1
  • Milestone status: Complete
  • Last updated: 2026-08-18
  • Risk classification: Persistence / Critical
  • Implementation authority: Additive ChannelForge persistence scaffolding

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This milestone introduces the first ChannelForge-owned persistence and identity foundation.

It defines:

  • ChannelForge identifier policy
  • Identifier types
  • Revision identifiers
  • External identifier qualification
  • Legacy identifier mapping
  • SQLite schema additions
  • Migration metadata
  • Migration runner behavior
  • Repository contracts
  • Repository implementations
  • Query services
  • Transaction coordination
  • Unit-of-work semantics
  • Optimistic concurrency
  • Write serialization
  • Busy handling
  • WAL and connection initialization
  • Integrity enforcement
  • Audit foundations
  • Backup preflight
  • Restore compatibility
  • Restart-safe migration
  • Rollback boundaries
  • Compatibility reads
  • Migration evidence
  • Pull-request sequence
  • Entry and completion gates
  • Risks
  • Deferred decisions

This milestone does not yet make ChannelForge persistence authoritative for every domain.

It creates additive foundations that later milestones can adopt safely.

docs.title: Governing Specifications
docs.text:
This milestone is governed by:

  • docs/architecture/spec/01-terminology.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/02-system-context.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/03-domain-model.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/05-media-catalog.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/06-playout-and-output.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/07-integrations.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/08-persistence.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/09-api.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/11-security.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/12-deployment.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/13-testing.md
  • docs/architecture/spec/14-migration.md
  • docs/implementation/README.md
  • docs/implementation/01-baseline-and-change-control.md
  • docs/implementation/02-module-boundaries.md

docs.title: Milestone Mission
docs.text:
ChannelForge must establish stable internal identity before domain migration.

The persistence milestone must:

  • Introduce ChannelForge-owned opaque identifiers
  • Preserve legacy identifiers through explicit mappings
  • Keep inherited data readable
  • Avoid destructive schema conversion
  • Keep schema evolution ordered and auditable
  • Ensure migrations are restart-safe
  • Ensure migrations are backup-aware
  • Keep provider calls outside write transactions
  • Keep FFmpeg outside write transactions
  • Keep transactions short
  • Enforce foreign keys
  • Enforce explicit deterministic ordering
  • Support optimistic concurrency
  • Support immutable revisions
  • Support immutable Schedule Plans
  • Support one primary SQLite writer
  • Support concurrent reads
  • Preserve historical references
  • Preserve rollback until cutover gates close
  • Make repository ownership align with module ownership
  • Prevent new domain code from depending on raw tables
  • Record every migration decision and result

docs.title: Product Principle
docs.text:
The governing product principle remains:

Build television networks, not playlists.

Stable ChannelForge identity allows Networks, Channels, Catalog Items, Programming Revisions, and Schedule Plans to exist independently of inherited playlist-oriented data structures.

docs.title: Current Persistence Baseline
docs.text:
The inherited runtime currently uses SQLite and includes multiple persistence libraries.

Known server dependencies include:

  • Better SQLite3
  • Kysely
  • Drizzle ORM
  • LowDB

Milestone 01 must identify actual ownership and use.

Milestone 03 must not assume every listed dependency remains necessary.

docs.title: Version 1 Persistence Decision
docs.text:
SQLite remains the authoritative version 1 database.

Version 1 does not require:

  • PostgreSQL
  • MySQL
  • Redis
  • Distributed transactions
  • Distributed locks
  • Multi-primary writes
  • Horizontal application scaling
  • External message queue
  • Event sourcing as the primary persistence model

docs.title: Persistence Principles
docs.text:
1. Domain services depend on repositories.
  2. Repositories do not expose raw database rows.
  3. SQLite remains implementation detail.
  4. Transactions align with application use cases.
  5. External network calls do not occur in write transactions.
  6. FFmpeg does not execute in write transactions.
  7. Immutable revisions remain immutable.
  8. Approved Schedule Plans remain immutable.
  9. Migrations are ordered.
  10. Migrations are tracked.
  11. Migrations are restart-safe.
  12. Migrations are observable.
  13. Backups precede critical conversion.
  14. Rollback is explicit.
  15. Historical references survive archival.
  16. Derived projections can be rebuilt.
  17. Read ordering is deterministic.
  18. Foreign keys are enabled.
  19. Database connections are bounded.
  20. Write lock duration is minimized.
  21. Legacy data remains preserved until retirement approval.
  22. Provider identifiers never become unqualified ChannelForge identity.
  23. Human-readable keys are not primary keys.
  24. Audit references survive lifecycle changes.
  25. Secret material is not stored in ordinary domain tables.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Milestone 03 covers:

  • Additive schema
  • Identifier scaffolding
  • Migration metadata
  • Legacy identity mappings
  • Repository infrastructure
  • Transaction coordination
  • Concurrency
  • Integrity
  • Backup preflight
  • Migration execution
  • Persistence testing
  • Compatibility support

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Milestone 03 does not require:

  • Final Media Source schema
  • Final Catalog schema
  • Final Network schema
  • Final Channel schema
  • Final Scheduling schema
  • Final Publication schema
  • Final Playout schema
  • Legacy write freeze
  • Legacy table deletion
  • Full provider migration
  • Full API migration
  • Full UI migration
  • PostgreSQL abstraction completion
  • Distributed outbox
  • Multi-process worker
  • Public release migration

docs.title: Identity Foundation
docs.text: Every persistent entity owned by ChannelForge must have a ChannelForge-owned identifier.

docs.title: Identifier Properties
docs.text:
A ChannelForge identifier must be:

  • Opaque
  • Stable
  • Collision resistant
  • Independent of row order
  • Independent of provider identity
  • Independent of legacy Tunarr identity
  • Safe to expose where authorization permits
  • Serializable
  • Comparable for equality
  • Preservable through export and import where supported
  • Validatable without database access

docs.title: Identifier Non-Properties
docs.text:
A ChannelForge identifier must not be assumed to be:

  • Sequential
  • Numeric
  • Time sortable
  • Human meaningful
  • Provider meaningful
  • Globally unique outside documented scope
  • Reusable after deletion
  • Mutable

docs.title: Identifier Format Decision
docs.text:
Recommended initial format:

UUID

Acceptable UUID variants include:

  • UUIDv4
  • UUIDv7

The exact variant requires one implementation decision.

docs.title: Identifier Variant Criteria
docs.text:
Choose based on:

  • Collision safety
  • Library support
  • SQLite indexing behavior
  • API compatibility
  • Export compatibility
  • Test determinism
  • Operational readability
  • Future migration

docs.title: UUIDv4 Considerations
docs.text:
Advantages:

  • Broad library support
  • Opaque
  • Mature
  • No embedded time
  • Easy generation

Tradeoffs:

  • Random insertion order
  • Larger B-tree locality cost
  • No natural creation ordering

docs.title: UUIDv7 Considerations
docs.text:
Advantages:

  • Time-ordered insertion
  • Better index locality
  • Broadening ecosystem support
  • Still opaque enough for API use

Tradeoffs:

  • Timestamp information
  • Newer library ecosystem
  • Potential accidental ordering assumptions

docs.title: Identifier ADR Threshold
docs.text: An ADR is required when selecting a non-UUID identifier format.

docs.title: Identifier Type Safety
docs.text:
Identifiers should use branded TypeScript types.

Example:

declare const networkIdBrand: unique symbol;

export type NetworkId = string & {
  readonly [networkIdBrand]: true;
};

docs.title: Identifier Constructors
docs.text:
Each identifier type should expose:

  • generate
  • parse
  • tryParse
  • toString
  • Optional test fixture constructor

docs.title: Identifier Constructor Rule
docs.text:
Parsing validates syntax.

Parsing does not verify database existence.

docs.title: Identifier Examples
docs.text:
Initial identifier types include:

  • InstanceId
  • UserId
  • ApiCredentialId
  • MediaSourceId
  • LibraryBindingId
  • CatalogItemId
  • SourceBindingId
  • PlaybackVariantId
  • NetworkId
  • NetworkProfileRevisionId
  • ChannelId
  • ChannelProfileRevisionId
  • BrandingProfileId
  • BrandingRevisionId
  • ProgrammingConfigurationId
  • ProgrammingConfigurationRevisionId
  • SchedulePlanId
  • ScheduleEntryId
  • SchedulePublicationId
  • PlayoutSessionId
  • BackgroundJobId
  • HealthSnapshotId
  • TemplateId
  • TemplateRevisionId
  • ProgrammingPackId
  • PluginInstallationId
  • MigrationRunId
  • MigrationConflictId
  • AuditRecordId
  • ArtifactId

docs.title: Identifier Ownership
docs.text:
The owning module defines its identifier type.

The shared kernel may define generic identifier primitives.

The shared kernel must not own every feature-specific identifier.

docs.title: Identifier Storage
docs.text:
Recommended SQLite representation:

TEXT

The exact representation must be consistent.

docs.title: Identifier Storage Invariants
docs.text:
• Non-null for owned persistent entities
  • Unique where entity identity requires it
  • Never silently regenerated
  • Never derived from mutable fields
  • Never reused
  • Foreign keys reference the exact stored value
  • Case normalization is explicit

docs.title: Case Policy
docs.text:
Canonical identifiers should use one case representation.

For UUIDs:

lowercase canonical text

is recommended.

docs.title: Identifier Validation
docs.text:
Database constraints should reject malformed identifiers where practical.

Application parsing remains mandatory.

docs.title: Human-Readable Keys
docs.text:
Human-readable keys include:

  • Network slug
  • Channel number
  • Call sign
  • Display name
  • Template name
  • Artifact file name

They are not primary identifiers.

docs.title: Human-Key Uniqueness
docs.text:
Uniqueness is scope-specific.

Examples:

  • Active Channel number unique within an instance
  • Network slug unique among non-archived Networks
  • Template name may repeat across publishers
  • Artifact file name may repeat across generations

docs.title: External Identifiers
docs.text: External identifiers must be qualified.

docs.title: External Identifier Components
docs.text:
A qualified external identity includes:

  • Provider type
  • Configured Media Source instance
  • External entity type
  • External identifier value
  • Optional external parent identity
  • Optional external version token

docs.title: External Identifier Value Object
docs.text:
Example:

export type QualifiedExternalId = {
  mediaSourceId: MediaSourceId;
  providerType: MediaProviderType;
  entityType: ExternalEntityType;
  value: string;
};

docs.title: External Identifier Invariants
docs.text:
• Value cannot be interpreted without source instance
  • Provider type must match Media Source
  • Empty values are invalid
  • Normalization is provider-specific
  • Case sensitivity is provider-specific
  • Same value may exist on multiple sources
  • Provider reinstall behavior is explicit
  • External value never replaces ChannelForge identity

docs.title: Legacy Identifiers
docs.text:
Legacy identifiers are compatibility references.

They remain necessary during migration.

docs.title: Legacy Identifier Components
docs.text:
A legacy mapping includes:

  • Legacy namespace
  • Legacy entity type
  • Legacy identifier value
  • ChannelForge entity type
  • ChannelForge identifier
  • Mapping status
  • Source migration run
  • Created timestamp
  • Verified timestamp
  • Conflict reference
  • Notes or evidence reference

docs.title: Legacy Namespace
docs.text:
Initial namespace:

tunarr

Future namespaces may include:

  • Import pack
  • External backup
  • Earlier ChannelForge version
  • Third-party migration tool

docs.title: Legacy Mapping Table
docs.text:
Suggested conceptual table:

legacy_identity_mapping

docs.title: Legacy Mapping Fields
docs.text:
mapping_id
legacy_namespace
legacy_entity_type
legacy_identifier
channelforge_entity_type
channelforge_identifier
mapping_status
migration_run_id
created_at
verified_at
conflict_id
metadata_json

docs.title: Mapping Unique Constraints
docs.text:
Recommended constraints:

UNIQUE (
  legacy_namespace,
  legacy_entity_type,
  legacy_identifier
)

and:

UNIQUE (
  legacy_namespace,
  legacy_entity_type,
  channelforge_entity_type,
  channelforge_identifier
)

The second constraint may require refinement for split or merge mappings.

docs.title: Mapping Cardinality
docs.text:
Supported mapping cardinalities must be explicit:

  • One legacy to one ChannelForge
  • Many legacy to one ChannelForge
  • One legacy to many ChannelForge
  • Unmapped
  • Conflict
  • Ignored

docs.title: Mapping Status
docs.text:
Suggested values:

  • PENDING
  • MAPPED
  • VERIFIED
  • CONFLICT
  • IGNORED
  • SUPERSEDED
  • ROLLED_BACK

docs.title: Mapping Conflict
docs.text:
A conflict occurs when:

  • One legacy ID maps to multiple active targets unexpectedly
  • One target receives incompatible legacy identities
  • Entity type does not match
  • Legacy data is incomplete
  • Required parent mapping is missing
  • Uniqueness constraint would be violated
  • Existing verified mapping disagrees

docs.title: Mapping Immutability
docs.text:
Verified mappings should not be edited in place casually.

Correction should record:

  • Prior mapping
  • New mapping
  • Reason
  • Actor
  • Migration run
  • Timestamp

docs.title: Revision Identity
docs.text: Mutable configuration uses immutable revisions.

docs.title: Revision Concepts
docs.text:
Revisioned concepts include:

  • Network Profile
  • Channel Profile
  • Branding Profile
  • Programming Configuration
  • Output Profile where applicable

docs.title: Revision Fields
docs.text:
Recommended common fields:

revision_id
owner_id
revision_number
status
created_at
created_by
activated_at
supersedes_revision_id
content_hash

docs.title: Revision Number
docs.text:
Revision number may be sequential within one owner.

It is not the primary identifier.

docs.title: Revision Status
docs.text:
Suggested values:

  • DRAFT
  • ACTIVE
  • SUPERSEDED
  • ARCHIVED
  • INVALID

docs.title: Revision Immutability
docs.text:
After activation:

  • Content cannot change
  • Hash cannot change
  • Parent reference cannot change
  • Created timestamp cannot change

Status metadata may transition according to lifecycle policy.

docs.title: Revision Hash
docs.text:
A deterministic content hash supports:

  • Change detection
  • Generation evidence
  • Duplicate detection
  • Audit
  • Migration verification

docs.title: Canonical Serialization
docs.text:
Hashing requires canonical serialization.

Canonical serialization must define:

  • Property ordering
  • Array ordering
  • Number formatting
  • Time formatting
  • Null handling
  • Omitted fields
  • Identifier case
  • Unicode normalization

docs.title: Revision Concurrency
docs.text: Creating a new revision should require the caller's expected active revision.

docs.title: Optimistic Concurrency
docs.text: ChannelForge uses optimistic concurrency for mutable aggregates.

docs.title: Concurrency Token
docs.text:
A mutable aggregate should expose:

  • Revision number
  • Version integer
  • Updated timestamp
  • ETag
  • Or equivalent token

docs.title: Recommended Token
docs.text:
Recommended persistence token:

version INTEGER NOT NULL

docs.title: Update Pattern
docs.text:
Example:

UPDATE network
SET
  display_name = ?,
  version = version + 1,
  updated_at = ?
WHERE
  network_id = ?
  AND version = ?;

docs.title: Concurrency Result
docs.text:
If affected rows equal zero:

  • Resource may be missing
  • Expected version may be stale
  • Authorization may have changed
  • Lifecycle state may reject update

The repository must distinguish outcomes where practical.

docs.title: ETag Mapping
docs.text:
API ETags may derive from:

  • Version integer
  • Revision identifier
  • Content hash
  • Stable combination

The mapping must be documented.

docs.title: Immutable Entity Concurrency
docs.text:
Immutable entities do not use update concurrency.

Creation uniqueness and idempotency protect them.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text: Critical creation commands should support idempotency.

docs.title: Idempotency Record
docs.text:
Suggested conceptual table:

idempotency_record

docs.title: Idempotency Fields
docs.text:
idempotency_key
scope
actor_id
request_hash
result_reference
status
created_at
expires_at

docs.title: Idempotency Scope
docs.text:
Examples:

  • API credential creation
  • Network creation
  • Schedule generation request
  • Publication request
  • Migration start
  • Backup request

docs.title: Idempotency Collision
docs.text: Same key with different request hash returns conflict.

docs.title: Persistence Architecture
docs.text:
The target persistence flow is:

flowchart TB
    Transport["Transport"]
    Application["Application Service"]
    Domain["Domain Aggregate"]
    Unit["Transaction Coordinator"]
    Repository["Repository Interface"]
    Query["Query Service"]
    Adapter["SQLite Adapter"]
    Database[("SQLite")]
    Files["Managed File Storage"]
    Audit["Audit Sink"]

    Transport --> Application
    Application --> Domain
    Application --> Unit
    Application --> Repository
    Application --> Query
    Application --> Audit
    Repository --> Adapter
    Query --> Adapter
    Unit --> Adapter
    Adapter --> Database
    Adapter --> Files

docs.title: Persistence Module Placement
docs.text:
Recommended infrastructure paths:

server/src/infrastructure/database/
├── connection/
├── migrations/
├── transactions/
├── integrity/
├── backup/
├── query/
└── testing/

Module-owned repositories may live under:

server/src/modules/<module>/adapters/persistence/sqlite/

docs.title: Repository Interface Placement
docs.text:
Repository interfaces live in the owning module.

Example:

server/src/modules/networks/ports/network-repository.ts

docs.title: Repository Implementation Placement
docs.text:
Repository implementation may live:

server/src/modules/networks/adapters/persistence/sqlite-network-repository.ts

or:

server/src/infrastructure/database/repositories/sqlite-network-repository.ts

The implementation must satisfy the module-owned port.

docs.title: Repository Contract
docs.text:
A repository contract should define:

  • Get by ID
  • Require by ID where appropriate
  • Save new aggregate
  • Update mutable aggregate with expected version
  • Archive or lifecycle operation
  • Existence check
  • Pagination only when aggregate listing is part of ownership

docs.title: Repository Non-Responsibilities
docs.text:
Repositories do not:

  • Authorize requests
  • Call providers
  • Generate schedules
  • Start FFmpeg
  • Serialize HTTP responses
  • Compose XMLTV
  • Publish domain events before commit
  • Hide long-running transactions

docs.title: Query Services
docs.text: Read-heavy workflows may use query services.

docs.title: Query Service Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Projection reads
  • Joined reads
  • Search
  • Pagination
  • Reporting
  • Guide read models
  • Operational diagnostics
  • Migration verification

docs.title: Query Service Restrictions
docs.text:
Query services are read-only.

They do not mutate through query-builder side effects.

docs.title: Domain Mapping
docs.text:
Persistence adapters map:

  • Database record to domain
  • Domain to database write
  • Database error to persistence error

docs.title: Mapping Rule
docs.text:
Database nullability does not automatically define domain optionality.

Domain invariants remain authoritative.

docs.title: Record Naming
docs.text:
Persistence records use explicit suffixes:

  • NetworkRecord
  • ChannelRecord
  • CatalogItemRecord
  • SchedulePlanRecord
  • MigrationRunRecord

docs.title: SQL Naming
docs.text:
Recommended table naming:

snake_case

Recommended column naming:

snake_case

docs.title: Timestamp Storage
docs.text:
Persisted instants use UTC.

Recommended representation:

ISO 8601 UTC text

or:

integer epoch milliseconds

The exact format must be consistent.

docs.title: Timestamp Decision Criteria
docs.text:
• Ordering
  • Precision
  • Human inspection
  • SQLite functions
  • JavaScript safety
  • Migration compatibility
  • Time-zone neutrality

docs.title: Duration Storage
docs.text: Durations should use integer milliseconds unless stronger precision is required.

docs.title: Boolean Storage
docs.text:
SQLite boolean values use integer constraints.

Example:

enabled INTEGER NOT NULL CHECK (enabled IN (0, 1))

docs.title: Enum Storage
docs.text:
Enums use text with validation.

Possible enforcement:

  • CHECK
  • Application validation
  • Both

docs.title: JSON Storage
docs.text:
JSON may be used for:

  • Immutable snapshots
  • Provenance payload
  • Migration metadata
  • Adapter-specific capability observations
  • Diagnostics

JSON must not replace queryable relational structure without justification.

docs.title: JSON Invariants
docs.text:
• Schema version required where long-lived
  • Canonical serialization where hashed
  • Size bounded
  • Secrets excluded
  • Validation required on read
  • Migration strategy defined

docs.title: Table Categories
docs.text:
ChannelForge tables fall into:

  • Authoritative aggregate tables
  • Immutable revision tables
  • Immutable plan tables
  • Mapping tables
  • Job tables
  • Audit tables
  • Migration tables
  • Derived projection tables
  • Idempotency tables
  • Operational lease tables

docs.title: Initial Additive Tables
docs.text:
Milestone 03 may introduce:

  • cf_instance
  • cf_schema_migration
  • cf_migration_run
  • cf_migration_step
  • cf_migration_checkpoint
  • cf_migration_conflict
  • cf_legacy_identity_mapping
  • cf_idempotency_record
  • cf_audit_record
  • cf_outbox_event only if approved
  • cf_integrity_check
  • cf_backup_record

The cf_ prefix is an implementation option during coexistence.

docs.title: Prefix Decision
docs.text:
A temporary prefix helps distinguish ChannelForge-owned tables from inherited tables.

The exact prefix must be documented.

docs.title: Prefix Tradeoffs
docs.text:
Advantages:

  • Clear coexistence
  • Easier inventory
  • Easier rollback
  • Easier accidental query detection

Tradeoffs:

  • Naming cleanup later
  • Longer SQL
  • Potential permanent temporary naming

docs.title: Prefix Removal
docs.text: Prefix removal is not required for version 1.

docs.title: Schema Ownership
docs.text: Every ChannelForge table has one owning module.

docs.title: Schema Ownership Registry
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/persistence/schema-ownership.md

Suggested columns:

Table Owning module Authoritative Mutable Migration owner Retention

docs.title: Migration Metadata Tables
docs.text: Migration execution must be durable.

docs.text:
Suggested values:

  • PENDING
  • RUNNING
  • APPLIED
  • FAILED
  • ROLLED_BACK
  • SKIPPED

docs.title: Migration Checksum
docs.text: Migration source checksum detects modified applied migrations.

docs.title: Applied Migration Immutability
docs.text:
An applied migration file must not be edited.

Corrections require a new migration.

docs.title: Migration Run
docs.text: A Migration Run tracks one higher-level data transition.

docs.title: Migration Run Status
docs.text:
Suggested values:

  • PLANNED
  • PREFLIGHT
  • READY
  • RUNNING
  • PAUSED
  • FAILED
  • ROLLING_BACK
  • ROLLED_BACK
  • COMPLETED
  • COMPLETED_WITH_WARNINGS
  • ABORTED

docs.title: Migration Step
docs.text: A Migration Run consists of steps.

docs.title: Migration Step Fields
docs.text:

migration_run_id

status

docs.title: Migration Step Status
docs.text:
• PENDING
  • RUNNING
  • PAUSED
  • FAILED
  • COMPLETED
  • SKIPPED
  • ROLLED_BACK

docs.title: Migration Checkpoint
docs.text: A checkpoint stores restart position.

docs.title: Checkpoint Fields
docs.text:
migration_run_id
step_key
cursor_type
cursor_value
last_source_identity
last_target_identity
processed_count
updated_at

docs.title: Checkpoint Rules
docs.text:
• Persist after bounded batch
  • Persist after each critical mapping
  • Persist before external side effect
  • Persist after transaction commit
  • Must be idempotent
  • Must not contain secrets
  • Must survive restart

docs.title: Migration Conflict
docs.text: A conflict is durable operator-review state.

docs.title: Conflict Fields
docs.text:
migration_conflict_id
migration_run_id
step_key
conflict_type
source_reference
candidate_targets_json
status
detected_at
resolved_at
resolved_by
resolution
evidence_json

docs.title: Conflict Status
docs.text:
• OPEN
  • AUTO_RESOLVED
  • OPERATOR_RESOLVED
  • IGNORED
  • SUPERSEDED
  • ROLLED_BACK

docs.title: Migration Statistics
docs.text:
Statistics should include:

  • Source rows inspected
  • Rows mapped
  • Rows created
  • Rows updated
  • Rows skipped
  • Conflicts
  • Warnings
  • Failures
  • Duration
  • Batch count
  • Checkpoint count

docs.title: Migration Runner
docs.text: The migration runner owns schema and controlled data migration execution.

docs.title: Migration Runner Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Discover migrations
  • Order migrations
  • Verify checksum
  • Acquire migration exclusivity
  • Run preflight
  • Verify backup requirement
  • Apply step
  • Record status
  • Record failure
  • Release exclusivity
  • Resume restart-safe work
  • Prevent downgrade
  • Expose diagnostics

docs.title: Migration Runner Non-Responsibilities
docs.text:
• Provider synchronization
  • Schedule generation
  • FFmpeg
  • HTTP route orchestration
  • Silent conflict resolution
  • Legacy deletion without approval

docs.title: Migration Exclusivity
docs.text: Only one schema migration process may run at a time.

docs.title: Exclusivity Mechanisms
docs.text:
Possible mechanisms:

  • SQLite exclusive transaction
  • Durable migration lease
  • Process-level lock plus database record
  • File lock plus database verification

Exact mechanism must be tested on:

  • Windows
  • Linux
  • Docker volume
  • Unraid storage

docs.title: Exclusivity Failure
docs.text:
If lock cannot be obtained:

  • Startup must not run migration concurrently
  • Readiness remains false
  • Diagnostics identify lock owner where possible
  • Operator action is clear

docs.title: Startup Migration Policy
docs.text:
Startup may apply safe schema migrations automatically.

Critical data migrations may require explicit operator approval.

docs.title: Automatic Migration Criteria
docs.text:
An automatic migration must be:

  • Additive
  • Bounded
  • Restart-safe
  • Tested
  • Backup-compatible
  • Non-destructive
  • Fast enough for startup policy
  • Observable

docs.title: Manual Migration Criteria
docs.text:
Manual approval required for:

  • Large data rewrite
  • Legacy write freeze
  • Identity remap
  • Secret migration
  • Destructive cleanup
  • Long-running backfill
  • Backup format change
  • Active publication cutover

docs.title: Migration Preflight
docs.text: Preflight checks occur before mutation.

docs.title: Preflight Checks
docs.text:
• Database exists
  • Database writable
  • Required free space
  • SQLite integrity
  • Foreign keys
  • Journal mode compatibility
  • Application version
  • Source schema version
  • Target schema version
  • Migration checksum
  • No conflicting migration
  • Backup availability
  • Backup verification
  • Required files accessible
  • Required permissions
  • No unsupported downgrade
  • No unresolved critical conflict
  • No active write freeze conflict

docs.title: Free-Space Policy
docs.text:
Preflight should estimate:

  • Database growth
  • WAL growth
  • Backup size
  • Temporary file use
  • Asset migration size

docs.title: Integrity Preflight
docs.text:
Recommended checks:

PRAGMA quick_check;
PRAGMA foreign_key_check;

A full integrity check may run based on risk.

docs.title: Backup Preflight
docs.text: Critical migrations require a backup record.

docs.title: Backup Record Fields
docs.text:
backup_id
created_at
created_by
application_version
schema_version
database_path
database_size
asset_manifest_hash
backup_path
backup_size
checksum
verification_status
retention_until
migration_run_id

docs.title: Backup Verification Status
docs.text:
• CREATING
  • CREATED
  • VERIFYING
  • VERIFIED
  • FAILED
  • EXPIRED
  • DELETED

docs.title: Backup Requirements
docs.text:
A migration backup must include:

  • SQLite database
  • WAL state handled consistently
  • Managed assets required by migrated state
  • Manifest
  • Checksums
  • Version metadata
  • Restore instructions

docs.title: SQLite Backup Mechanism
docs.text:
Preferred options:

  • SQLite online backup API
  • VACUUM INTO
  • Checkpoint plus safe copy where validated

Raw file copy while active is prohibited unless validated for the exact journal mode and checkpoint procedure.

docs.title: Backup Naming
docs.text:
Backup names should include:

  • Timestamp
  • Application version
  • Schema version
  • Migration Run ID

docs.title: Backup Retention
docs.text: Retention must preserve rollback through the supported window.

docs.title: Restore Compatibility
docs.text:
A backup manifest must declare:

  • Minimum restore application
  • Maximum tested restore application
  • Schema version
  • Required assets
  • Checksum algorithm
  • Encryption state

docs.title: Migration Batch Processing
docs.text: Large data migrations use bounded batches.

docs.title: Batch Criteria
docs.text:
Choose batch size based on:

  • Lock duration
  • Row size
  • WAL growth
  • Checkpoint cost
  • Test performance
  • Memory
  • Retry behavior

docs.title: Batch Transaction Rule
docs.text:
Each batch:

  1. Reads bounded source records.
  2. Translates outside write transaction where possible.
  3. Begins write transaction.
  4. Writes target records.
  5. Writes mappings.
  6. Writes checkpoint.
  7. Commits.
  8. Emits progress after commit.

docs.title: Provider Call Prohibition
docs.text: No provider call occurs during schema or data migration transaction.

docs.title: File Operation Rule
docs.text:
File copy or hash may occur outside database write transaction.

Database references become authoritative only after file verification.

docs.title: Idempotent Migration Step
docs.text:
A migration step is idempotent when re-execution:

  • Does not duplicate target entity
  • Does not duplicate mapping
  • Does not overwrite verified state incorrectly
  • Resumes from checkpoint
  • Produces same final state
  • Detects incompatible prior partial state

docs.title: Idempotency Strategies
docs.text:
• Unique constraints
  • Upsert with expected state
  • Mapping lookup
  • Content hash
  • Checkpoint
  • Deterministic target ID
  • Run-scoped work table

docs.title: Deterministic Target ID
docs.text:
A migration may generate target identifiers once and persist mappings.

It should not regenerate new IDs on retry.

docs.title: Deterministic ID Derivation
docs.text:
Deriving UUIDs from legacy identity may be considered.

Tradeoffs:

  • Stable retries
  • Reproducible mapping
  • Potential identity correlation
  • Namespace management
  • Collision policy

The default strategy should be generated ID plus durable mapping.

docs.title: Migration Resume
docs.text:
On startup:

  1. Detect incomplete run.
  2. Verify application compatibility.
  3. Verify migration checksum.
  4. Verify backup record.
  5. Verify last checkpoint.
  6. Reconcile last batch.
  7. Resume or require operator action.

docs.title: Last Batch Reconciliation
docs.text:
A crash may occur after commit but before checkpoint reporting.

The migration must distinguish:

  • Target committed
  • Mapping committed
  • Checkpoint committed
  • Progress event emitted

docs.title: Transaction Atomicity
docs.text: Target write, mapping write, and checkpoint update should share one transaction when they represent one batch.

docs.title: Migration Failure
docs.text:
On failure:

  • Record error summary
  • Preserve detailed sanitized diagnostics
  • Mark step failed
  • Mark run failed or paused
  • Keep backup
  • Keep mappings
  • Keep checkpoint
  • Do not continue silently
  • Do not delete source state

docs.title: Migration Pause
docs.text: Long migrations may support pause between batches.

docs.title: Migration Cancellation
docs.text:
Cancellation must be safe.

A cancellation request:

  • Stops after current transaction
  • Records checkpoint
  • Marks status
  • Preserves backup
  • Does not roll back committed batches automatically

docs.title: Migration Rollback
docs.text: Rollback must be defined per migration.

docs.title: Rollback Categories
docs.text:
• Metadata-only rollback
  • Target-table cleanup
  • Mapping rollback
  • Active-pointer rollback
  • Backup restore
  • Forward-fix only

docs.title: Forward-Fix Migration
docs.text:
Some migrations may be forward-fix only after cutover.

This requires:

  • Explicit declaration
  • Backup
  • Approval
  • Release note
  • Tested recovery

docs.title: Rollback Preconditions
docs.text:
• Supported rollback window open
  • Backup available
  • No incompatible new writes
  • Target state not externally depended upon
  • Operator authorized
  • Application version compatible

docs.title: Rollback Evidence
docs.text:
Record:

  • Requested by
  • Started at
  • Completed at
  • Restored backup
  • Rows removed
  • Mappings reverted
  • Conflicts
  • Verification result

docs.title: Schema Migration File Naming
docs.text:
Suggested pattern:

YYYYMMDDHHMMSS_description.ts

or:

0001_description.ts

The repository should use one ordered convention.

docs.title: Schema Migration Interface
docs.text:
Example:

export interface SchemaMigration {
  id: string;
  description: string;
  checksum: string;
  up(context: MigrationContext): Promise<void>;
  down?: (context: MigrationContext) => Promise<void>;
}

docs.title: Down Migration Policy
docs.text:
Production rollback should not assume every migration has a down.

A backup restore may be safer.

docs.title: Migration Checksum Generation
docs.text: Checksum includes canonical migration source or declared SQL content.

docs.title: Modified Applied Migration
docs.text:
If applied checksum differs:

  • Readiness fails
  • Migration does not proceed
  • Diagnostic names migration
  • Operator must restore original or apply documented repair

docs.title: Schema Version
docs.text:
The Instance aggregate records active schema version.

Migration metadata remains the authoritative history.

docs.title: Application Version Compatibility
docs.text:
Startup must verify:

  • Application supports current schema
  • Schema is not ahead beyond supported range
  • Required migrations are available
  • Downgrade is not implicit

docs.title: Database Naming
docs.text: During coexistence, ChannelForge-owned tables should use explicit naming.

docs.title: Database Connection Initialization
docs.text: Every connection must apply required pragmas.

docs.title: Required Pragmas
docs.text:
At minimum evaluate:

  • foreign_keys
  • journal_mode
  • busy_timeout
  • synchronous
  • temp_store
  • cache_size
  • wal_autocheckpoint

docs.title: Foreign Keys
docs.text: Foreign-key enforcement must be enabled for every connection.

docs.title: Foreign-Key Verification
docs.text:
Initialization should verify:

PRAGMA foreign_keys;

Expected:

1

docs.title: Foreign-Key Failure
docs.text:
If enforcement cannot be confirmed:

  • Writes must not proceed
  • Readiness remains false
  • Diagnostics identify cause

docs.title: Journal Mode
docs.text: WAL is preferred where deployment storage supports it.

docs.title: WAL Validation
docs.text:
Validate:

  • Local filesystem
  • Docker bind mount
  • Docker named volume
  • Unraid share
  • Network filesystem if supported
  • Windows development filesystem

docs.title: Unsupported WAL Storage
docs.text:
If storage does not support safe WAL behavior:

  • Use documented alternative
  • Warn operator
  • Adjust concurrency expectations
  • Test backup behavior
  • Record health finding

docs.title: Busy Timeout
docs.text: Every connection uses a bounded busy timeout.

docs.title: Busy Retry
docs.text:
Busy retry should be:

  • Bounded
  • Jittered where useful
  • Logged at debug or warning threshold
  • Classified
  • Not applied to every error
  • Not unbounded

docs.title: Write Serialization
docs.text:
Version 1 assumes one application instance.

Within the process, writes may be coordinated.

docs.title: Write Coordinator
docs.text:
A write coordinator may provide:

  • Queue
  • Priority
  • Cancellation
  • Timeout
  • Metrics
  • Shutdown drain

docs.title: Write Priority
docs.text:
Possible priorities:

  • Critical publication
  • Migration
  • User command
  • Background synchronization
  • Cleanup
  • Projection rebuild

Priority policy must avoid starvation.

docs.title: Read Connections
docs.text:
Read connections should:

  • Remain bounded
  • Use short transactions
  • Avoid blocking checkpoint indefinitely
  • Use stable ordering
  • Use indexes

docs.title: Write Connection
docs.text:
The write connection should:

  • Be owned by infrastructure
  • Apply required pragmas
  • Use explicit transactions
  • Close on shutdown
  • Avoid hidden nesting

docs.title: Connection Pool
docs.text:
SQLite may use:

  • Single shared connection
  • One write plus bounded reads
  • Connection-per-operation with strict initialization

Exact model requires testing.

docs.title: Transaction Coordinator
docs.text: The application layer requests transactions through a coordinator.

docs.title: Transaction Coordinator Interface
docs.text:
Example:

export interface TransactionCoordinator {
  run<T>(
    operation: (context: TransactionContext) => Promise<T>,
    options?: TransactionOptions,
  ): Promise<T>;
}

docs.title: Transaction Context
docs.text:
Contains:

  • Transaction-scoped repositories
  • Correlation ID
  • Optional actor reference
  • Start time
  • Deadline
  • Retry metadata

docs.title: Transaction Options
docs.text:
Possible fields:

  • Mode
  • Timeout
  • Retry policy
  • Name
  • Read-only
  • Priority

docs.title: Transaction Modes
docs.text:
SQLite modes may include:

  • Deferred
  • Immediate
  • Exclusive

Use must be explicit.

docs.title: Default Write Mode
docs.text:
IMMEDIATE may be appropriate for predictable write-lock acquisition.

The exact default requires testing.

docs.title: Nested Transactions
docs.text: Nested transactions are prohibited unless implemented through savepoints.

docs.title: Savepoints
docs.text:
Savepoints may support module-local composition.

They must not hide long transactions.

docs.title: External Call Guard
docs.text:
Transaction context should not expose provider clients.

Code review and architecture tests should enforce no provider calls during transactions.

docs.title: Transaction Duration
docs.text:
Set a target threshold.

Suggested initial warning threshold:

250 milliseconds

This is a planning target, not a universal failure threshold.

docs.title: Long Transaction Metrics
docs.text:
Record:

  • Operation
  • Duration
  • Lock wait
  • Rows affected
  • Retry count
  • Correlation ID

docs.title: Transaction Error Categories
docs.text:
• Busy
  • Constraint
  • Foreign key
  • Unique
  • Check
  • Not null
  • Corruption
  • I/O
  • Disk full
  • Permission
  • Interrupted
  • Unknown

docs.title: Persistence Error Translation
docs.text: Adapters translate SQLite errors into stable persistence errors.

docs.title: Constraint Translation
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Duplicate Channel number
  • Duplicate Network slug
  • Stale version
  • Missing parent
  • Invalid lifecycle state
  • Duplicate legacy mapping

docs.title: Query Ordering
docs.text: Every query that influences behavior must include explicit order.

docs.title: Behavioral Ordering
docs.text:
Behavioral queries include:

  • Scheduling candidates
  • Episode order
  • Channel lineup
  • Migration batches
  • Job queue
  • Publication selection
  • Fallback selection
  • Artifact listing

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Use stable pagination.

Recommended:

  • Cursor-based for large mutable collections
  • Offset only for bounded administrative lists

docs.title: Cursor Composition
docs.text:
Cursor should include:

  • Ordered field
  • Unique tie-breaker
  • Optional filter fingerprint

docs.title: Projection Tables
docs.text:
Derived projections may support:

  • Catalog search
  • Channel guide
  • Active publication lookup
  • Health metrics
  • Operational dashboard

docs.title: Projection Rebuild
docs.text:
A projection must define:

  • Source tables
  • Rebuild command
  • Rebuild status
  • Failure behavior
  • Cutover
  • Verification

docs.title: Projection Authority
docs.text: Projection is never authoritative unless explicitly specified.

docs.title: Audit Foundation
docs.text: Milestone 03 introduces audit persistence scaffolding.

docs.title: Audit Record Fields
docs.text:
audit_record_id
occurred_at
actor_type
actor_id
action
resource_type
resource_id
correlation_id
request_id
result
metadata_json

docs.title: Audit Exclusions
docs.text:
Do not store:

  • Raw credential
  • Provider token
  • Session secret
  • Plugin secret
  • Private key
  • Full media path unless policy permits

docs.title: Audit Immutability
docs.text: Audit records are append-only.

docs.title: Audit Retention
docs.text: Retention policy is configured and documented.

docs.title: Audit Failure
docs.text:
Critical security actions may fail closed when audit cannot be recorded.

Exact policy requires security milestone integration.

docs.title: Integrity Checks
docs.text:
Persistence infrastructure should support:

  • Quick check
  • Full integrity check
  • Foreign-key check
  • Orphan scan
  • Managed-file verification
  • Mapping consistency
  • Revision hash verification
  • Publication reference verification

docs.title: Integrity Check Record
docs.text:
Suggested table:

cf_integrity_check

docs.title: Integrity Check Fields
docs.text:
integrity_check_id
check_type
status
started_at
completed_at
database_version
finding_count
summary_json

docs.title: Integrity Status
docs.text:
• RUNNING
  • PASSED
  • PASSED_WITH_WARNINGS
  • FAILED
  • CANCELLED

docs.title: Integrity Finding
docs.text: Findings should be durable when they require action.

docs.title: Managed File References
docs.text: Database records may reference managed files.

docs.title: Managed File Fields
docs.text:
• Artifact ID
  • Logical type
  • Relative path
  • Checksum
  • Size
  • Created timestamp
  • Owner reference
  • Retention state
  • Encryption state

docs.title: Path Rule
docs.text: Store relative managed paths, not arbitrary host absolute paths, where possible.

docs.title: File Commit Protocol
docs.text:
For authoritative file publication:

  1. Write temporary file.
  2. Flush and close.
  3. Validate.
  4. Compute checksum.
  5. Move atomically into managed path.
  6. Commit database reference.
  7. Delete previous file only after retention policy permits.

docs.title: Database/File Atomicity
docs.text:
SQLite and filesystem cannot share one transaction.

Use staged state and reconciliation.

docs.title: File State
docs.text:
Suggested values:

  • STAGING
  • READY
  • ACTIVE
  • SUPERSEDED
  • MISSING
  • CORRUPT
  • DELETED

docs.title: Secret Storage Reference
docs.text:
Domain tables store secret references.

Secret material remains behind Secret Service.

docs.title: Secret Reference Fields
docs.text:
• Secret reference ID
  • Secret type
  • Owner module
  • Owner entity ID
  • Version
  • Created timestamp
  • Rotated timestamp
  • Archived timestamp

docs.title: Secret Migration
docs.text:
Secret migration requires:

  • Separate critical work item
  • Encryption verification
  • No plaintext logs
  • Backup policy
  • Rollback
  • Sentinel test

docs.title: Compatibility Reads
docs.text:
Milestone 03 may introduce repositories that read:

  • ChannelForge table first
  • Legacy table second
  • Mapping table to resolve identity

docs.title: Read Strategy
docs.text:
Possible strategies:

  • New-first fallback
  • Legacy-first shadow new
  • Dual read compare
  • Legacy-only adapter
  • New-only

Strategy must be explicit per concept.

docs.title: Write Strategy
docs.text:
Possible strategies:

  • Legacy authoritative
  • ChannelForge authoritative
  • Temporary dual write
  • ChannelForge write with legacy projection
  • Read-only migration

docs.title: Write Authority Matrix
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/persistence/write-authority.md

Suggested columns:

Concept Legacy writer ChannelForge writer Current authority Cutover gate Rollback

docs.title: Dual Write Policy
docs.text: Dual write is exceptional.

docs.title: Dual Write Requirements
docs.text:
• One authority identified
  • Idempotency
  • Reconciliation
  • Failure behavior
  • Metrics
  • Rollback
  • Removal milestone

docs.title: Partial Dual Write Failure
docs.text:
If one write succeeds and the other fails:

  • Record reconciliation finding
  • Return explicit outcome
  • Do not pretend atomicity
  • Retry safely
  • Preserve authoritative state

docs.title: Legacy Projection
docs.text:
A compatibility projection may translate ChannelForge state into legacy shape.

It must be derived and rebuildable.

docs.title: Shadow Read
docs.text: Shadow reads compare legacy and ChannelForge data.

docs.title: Shadow Read Finding
docs.text:
Record:

  • Concept
  • Legacy identity
  • ChannelForge identity
  • Legacy hash
  • ChannelForge hash
  • Difference category
  • Timestamp
  • Correlation ID

docs.title: Shadow Read Categories
docs.text:
• Equal
  • Formatting difference
  • Expected semantic difference
  • Missing legacy
  • Missing ChannelForge
  • Identity mismatch
  • Data mismatch
  • Error

docs.title: Migration Metadata API
docs.text:
Administrative APIs may expose:

  • Migration status
  • Step status
  • Progress
  • Conflict count
  • Backup status
  • Rollback eligibility

They must not expose secrets.

docs.title: Migration Authorization
docs.text:
Only authorized administrators may:

  • Start critical migration
  • Pause
  • Resume
  • Resolve conflict
  • Roll back
  • Complete cutover

docs.title: Migration Audit
docs.text: Every administrative migration action is audited.

docs.title: Persistence Observability
docs.text:
Required metrics include:

  • Connection count
  • Read latency
  • Write latency
  • Lock wait
  • Busy retries
  • Transaction duration
  • Transaction failures
  • Migration status
  • Migration throughput
  • Checkpoint age
  • WAL size
  • Checkpoint duration
  • Backup duration
  • Integrity findings
  • Query slow count

docs.title: Persistence Logs
docs.text:
Structured fields:

  • module
  • repository
  • operation
  • transactionName
  • durationMs
  • lockWaitMs
  • retryCount
  • rowsAffected
  • migrationRunId
  • migrationStep
  • correlationId

docs.title: SQL Logging
docs.text:
Production SQL logging must avoid:

  • Secret values
  • Tokens
  • Passwords
  • Full private paths
  • Large metadata payloads

docs.title: Slow Query Threshold
docs.text:
Initial threshold may be:

500 milliseconds

Exact threshold requires measurement.

docs.title: Backup Observability
docs.text:
Record:

  • Start
  • End
  • Source size
  • Backup size
  • Checksum
  • Verification
  • Failure
  • Retention

docs.title: Migration Progress
docs.text:
Progress should report:

  • Step
  • Batch
  • Processed
  • Remaining estimate
  • Warnings
  • Conflicts
  • Throughput

docs.title: Estimate Policy
docs.text: Progress estimates must be labeled estimates.

docs.title: SQLite Health
docs.text:
Health states:

  • HEALTHY
  • DEGRADED
  • READ_ONLY
  • MIGRATION_REQUIRED
  • MIGRATION_FAILED
  • CORRUPT
  • UNAVAILABLE

docs.title: Readiness
docs.text:
Readiness should fail when:

  • Required migration failed
  • Schema ahead unsupported
  • Foreign keys disabled
  • Database unavailable
  • Integrity critical failure
  • Migration lock conflict
  • Required backup preflight failed

docs.title: Liveness
docs.text: Liveness may remain true during recoverable migration failure if process is responsive.

docs.title: Persistence Testing
docs.text: Milestone 03 requires dedicated persistence test layers.

docs.title: Unit Tests
docs.text:
Unit tests cover:

  • Identifier parse
  • Identifier generation shape
  • Qualified external ID
  • Mapping rules
  • Revision hash
  • Concurrency token
  • Migration state transitions
  • Error translation
  • Canonical serialization

docs.title: Repository Contract Tests
docs.text: Every repository implementation runs shared contract tests.

docs.title: Repository Contract Cases
docs.text:
• Save
  • Get
  • Not found
  • Duplicate
  • Update
  • Stale version
  • Archive
  • Foreign key
  • Transaction rollback
  • Deterministic list order

docs.title: Transaction Tests
docs.text:
Test:

  • Commit
  • Rollback
  • Busy retry
  • Timeout
  • Constraint failure
  • Nested call
  • Savepoint if supported
  • Cancellation
  • Long transaction metric
  • Shutdown

docs.title: Migration Tests
docs.text:
Test:

  • Empty database
  • Current legacy fixture
  • Prior supported fixture
  • Interrupted migration
  • Resume
  • Modified checksum
  • Duplicate mapping
  • Conflict
  • Batch restart
  • Backup required
  • Backup failure
  • Disk full simulation
  • Read-only database
  • Foreign keys off
  • Schema ahead
  • Unsupported downgrade
  • Rollback

docs.title: Windows Migration Tests
docs.text:
Test:

  • File locking
  • Backup path
  • Rename
  • Temporary file cleanup
  • SQLite EBUSY
  • Drive-letter paths
  • Long paths where relevant

docs.title: Linux Migration Tests
docs.text:
Test:

  • Container volume
  • Signal interruption
  • User permissions
  • WAL
  • Backup
  • Atomic rename
  • Restart

docs.title: Failure Injection
docs.text:
Inject:

  • Crash after target write
  • Crash after mapping write
  • Crash before checkpoint
  • Crash after checkpoint
  • Busy database
  • Corrupt row
  • Missing parent mapping
  • Disk full
  • Permission denied
  • Checksum mismatch

docs.title: Golden Migration Fixtures
docs.text:
Maintain sanitized fixtures for:

  • Empty install
  • Minimal legacy install
  • Multiple Channels
  • Custom shows
  • Filler
  • Provider sources
  • Duplicate identifiers
  • Archived records
  • Invalid references
  • Partial migration
  • Completed migration

docs.title: Fixture Versioning
docs.text:
Fixture manifest includes:

  • Source application version
  • Source schema version
  • Expected migration target
  • Checksum
  • Sanitization statement
  • Expected findings

docs.title: Migration Determinism
docs.text:
The same fixture and migration version should produce equivalent canonical target state.

Generated identifiers may differ only when mapping is persisted and canonical comparison excludes allowed variance.

docs.title: Canonical Migration Comparison
docs.text:
Compare:

  • Entity counts
  • Mappings
  • Content hashes
  • Relationships
  • Lifecycle
  • Ordering
  • Conflict set
  • Publication references where included

docs.title: Performance Tests
docs.text:
Measure:

  • Migration throughput
  • Peak memory
  • WAL growth
  • Lock duration
  • Backup duration
  • Restore duration
  • Large mapping lookup
  • Repository query latency

docs.title: Performance Baselines
docs.text:
Record by fixture size:

  • Small
  • Medium
  • Large
  • Stress

docs.title: Data Volume Assumptions
docs.text: Do not hard-code home-server scale without measurement.

docs.title: Query Plans
docs.text:
Critical queries should inspect:

EXPLAIN QUERY PLAN

docs.title: Index Policy
docs.text:
Indexes support:

  • Primary lookup
  • Foreign key traversal
  • Unique constraints
  • Active records
  • Revision lookup
  • Migration batch cursor
  • Mapping lookup
  • Job queue
  • Publication lookup

docs.title: Index Review
docs.text:
Every index should state:

  • Query served
  • Selectivity
  • Write cost
  • Retention
  • Migration impact

docs.title: Partial Indexes
docs.text:
Use where beneficial for:

  • Active records
  • Open conflicts
  • Pending jobs
  • Current revisions
  • Unexpired idempotency

docs.title: Archive Semantics
docs.text: Archive preserves identity and history.

docs.title: Hard Delete
docs.text: Hard delete is restricted.

docs.title: Hard Delete Criteria
docs.text:
• Never referenced draft
  • Temporary artifact
  • Expired idempotency record
  • Explicit retention cleanup
  • Verified safe child ownership
  • User removal policy where permitted

docs.title: Historical Reference Rule
docs.text: Schedule, publication, migration, audit, and playout history must not disappear because an entity is archived.

docs.title: Cascades
docs.text: Cascade only for strictly owned child records.

docs.title: Default Foreign-Key Actions
docs.text:
• RESTRICT for historical references
  • CASCADE for owned children
  • SET NULL only where meaningful
  • No accidental orphan

docs.title: Retention
docs.text: Retention workers use bounded batches.

docs.title: Retention Audit
docs.text:
Critical deletion records:

  • Policy
  • Count
  • Cutoff
  • Actor or job
  • Timestamp
  • Verification

docs.title: Database Restore
docs.text: Restore is an operator workflow.

docs.title: Restore Steps
docs.text:
1. Stop writes.
  2. Validate backup manifest.
  3. Verify checksum.
  4. Preserve current failed state.
  5. Restore database and assets.
  6. Start compatible application version.
  7. Run integrity checks.
  8. Verify schema version.
  9. Verify mappings.
  10. Verify active publication.
  11. Resume service.

docs.title: Restore Rehearsal
docs.text: Critical migration cannot ship without tested restore.

docs.title: Restore Finding
docs.text: Any mismatch creates a durable finding.

docs.title: Database Export
docs.text:
Export may be added later.

Milestone 03 only defines identity preservation expectations.

docs.title: Import Identity
docs.text:
Import may preserve ChannelForge ID when:

  • Explicitly supported
  • No collision
  • Instance policy permits
  • References are complete
  • Audit records decision

Otherwise generate new ID and mapping.

docs.title: Multi-Instance Identity
docs.text:
ChannelForge IDs are unique within an instance.

Exports should include Instance ID and namespace.

docs.title: Instance Identity
docs.text: Exactly one active Instance exists per deployment.

docs.title: Instance Bootstrap
docs.text: Initial bootstrap must be idempotent.

docs.title: Instance Table
docs.text:
Suggested fields:

instance_id
display_name
default_time_zone
setup_state
schema_version
application_version
created_at
updated_at
version

docs.title: Instance Bootstrap Rule
docs.text:
If no instance exists:

  • Create one
  • Persist generated ID
  • Do not create second on retry

docs.title: Instance Duplicate
docs.text: More than one active instance is integrity failure.

docs.title: Schema Scaffold Implementation
docs.text: Milestone 03 should begin with infrastructure tables, not every domain table.

docs.title: Initial Migration Sequence
docs.text:
Suggested:

  1. Migration metadata
  2. Instance identity
  3. Legacy identity mappings
  4. Backup records
  5. Integrity records
  6. Audit foundation
  7. Idempotency
  8. Module repository support
  9. First representative aggregate table

docs.title: Representative Aggregate
docs.text:
Choose one low-risk aggregate to prove repository patterns.

Candidates:

  • Instance
  • Migration Run
  • Background Job metadata

Avoid using Network or Channel as first proof if it forces early cutover.

docs.title: Repository Proof
docs.text:
The representative repository must demonstrate:

  • Branded ID
  • Insert
  • Read
  • Version update
  • Transaction rollback
  • Error translation
  • Contract test
  • SQLite mapping

docs.title: Migration Proof
docs.text:
The representative migration must demonstrate:

  • Ordered migration
  • Checksum
  • Applied status
  • Restart
  • Rollback or backup recovery
  • Windows
  • Linux

docs.text:
Milestone 03 implementation should create:

docs/implementation/persistence/
├── identifier-policy.md

Must include state transitions for:

  • Rollback

Must include:

  • Methods

docs.title: PR 03A: Identifier Primitives
docs.text:
Scope:

  • Shared identifier primitive

docs.title: PR 03C: Migration Metadata Schema
docs.text:
Scope:

  • Migration table
  • Migration Run
  • Migration Step
  • Checkpoint
  • Conflict
  • Checksums

docs.text:
Scope:

  • Discovery
  • Ordering
  • Exclusivity
  • Status
  • Resume

docs.title: PR 03E: Backup Preflight
docs.text:
Scope:

  • Backup record
  • Backup creation
  • Verification
  • Manifest
  • Restore test

docs.title: PR 03F: Transaction Coordinator
docs.text:
Scope:

  • Transaction interface
  • SQLite implementation
  • Retry

docs.title: PR 03G: Repository Contract Harness
docs.text:
Scope:

  • Repository conventions
  • Contract-test utilities

docs.title: PR 03H: Legacy Identity Mapping
docs.text:
Scope:

  • Mapping table
  • Mapping repository
  • Cardinality
  • Conflict
  • Verification

docs.title: PR 03I: Optimistic Concurrency
docs.text:
Scope:

Scope:

  • Audit record

Scope:

  • One representative new-first or legacy-first repository

Scope:

  • Sanitized fixtures

docs.title: Pull-Request Requirements
docs.text:
Every persistence pull request must state:

  • Tables affected
  • Owning module
  • Migration ID
  • Forward behavior
  • Restart behavior
  • Rollback
  • Backup requirement
  • Concurrency impact
  • Lock impact
  • Query ordering
  • Test fixture
  • Windows result
  • Linux result
  • Compatibility impact

docs.title: Persistence PR Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not combine:

  • Schema migration and broad UI work
  • Migration runner and provider refactor
  • Identifier change and package rebrand
  • Backup implementation and legacy deletion
  • Transaction coordinator and scheduler replacement
  • Repository scaffold and full domain cutover
  • Concurrency change and unrelated dependency update

docs.title: Entry Gates
docs.text:
Milestone 03 may begin when:

  1. Milestone 01 baseline exists.
  2. Milestone 02 boundaries exist or are accepted as implementation target.
  3. Persistence stores are inventoried.
  4. Current write authorities are known enough to avoid accidental cutover.
  5. Current build passes.
  6. Current test failures are tracked.
  7. SQLite remains accepted for version 1.
  8. Backup path is known.
  9. No unresolved architecture contradiction blocks persistence work.
  10. Roadmap branch remains documentation-only.

docs.title: Completion Gates
docs.text:
Milestone 03 is Complete when:

  1. Identifier format is accepted.
  2. Identifier parsing exists.
  3. Identifier generation exists.
  4. Module-owned branded identifiers exist for initial modules.
  5. External identifiers are qualified.
  6. Legacy mapping schema exists.
  7. Mapping uniqueness is enforced.
  8. Mapping conflicts are durable.
  9. Revision identity policy exists.
  10. Canonical serialization policy exists.
  11. Optimistic concurrency policy exists.
  12. Representative versioned aggregate works.
  13. SQLite connection initialization exists.
  14. Foreign keys are enabled and verified.
  15. Busy timeout is configured.
  16. Journal mode policy is implemented.
  17. Connection count is bounded.
  18. Transaction coordinator exists.
  19. Nested transaction policy is enforced.
  20. External calls are excluded from write transactions.
  21. FFmpeg is excluded from write transactions.
  22. Repository interfaces are module-owned.
  23. Representative SQLite repository passes contract tests.
  24. Query ordering policy is enforced.
  25. Schema migration metadata exists.
  26. Applied migration checksum is verified.
  27. Migration exclusivity exists.
  28. Failed migration is durable.
  29. Incomplete migration is detected on restart.
  30. Migration checkpoint exists.
  31. Batch resume is tested.
  32. Conflict state exists.
  33. Backup preflight exists.
  34. Backup verification exists.
  35. Restore rehearsal passes.
  36. Integrity checks exist.
  37. Audit foundation exists.
  38. Idempotency foundation exists or is explicitly deferred.
  39. One compatibility read path uses mappings.
  40. Shadow comparison is observable.
  41. No legacy table is deleted.
  42. No unsupported downgrade occurs.
  43. Windows persistence tests pass or classified failures are tracked.
  44. Linux persistence tests pass.
  45. Failure injection passes.
  46. Disk-full behavior is tested or recorded.
  47. Permission failure behavior is tested.
  48. Migration fixture suite exists.
  49. Schema ownership registry exists.
  50. Write-authority matrix exists.
  51. Transaction policy exists.
  52. Migration state machine exists.
  53. Backup and restore documentation exists.
  54. Completion report exists.
  55. Milestone 04 entry is approved.

docs.title: Completion Evidence
docs.text:
The completion report should include:

  • Active schema version
  • Applied migrations
  • Migration checksums
  • Identifier decision
  • Repository contract results
  • Transaction test results
  • Backup result
  • Restore result
  • Integrity result
  • Windows result
  • Linux result
  • Mapping test result
  • Failure injection result
  • Open conflicts
  • Deferred risks

docs.title: Rollback
docs.text:
Milestone 03 is additive by default.

Rollback options:

  • Revert application code
  • Leave unused additive tables
  • Restore pre-migration backup
  • Mark migration rolled back
  • Remove unreferenced target records
  • Restore legacy read path

docs.title: Additive Table Rollback
docs.text:
Dropping additive tables is not required immediately.

Unused tables may remain until cleanup approval.

docs.title: Identifier Rollback
docs.text:
Once a ChannelForge ID is exposed or referenced, do not regenerate it during rollback.

Preserve mapping.

docs.title: Migration Runner Rollback
docs.text: An older application must not silently ignore newer migration metadata.

docs.title: Backup Rollback
docs.text:
A backup restore must preserve:

  • Database
  • Managed assets
  • Manifest
  • Schema compatibility
  • Mapping consistency

docs.title: Migration Failure
docs.text:
• Fail readiness where required
  • Record run failure
  • Preserve checkpoint
  • Preserve backup
  • Preserve source
  • Expose operator action

docs.title: Database Corruption
docs.text:
• Stop writes
  • Mark health corrupt
  • Preserve files
  • Run diagnostics
  • Require restore or repair workflow

docs.title: Disk Full
docs.text:
• Roll back current transaction
  • Mark operation failed
  • Preserve database integrity
  • Stop migration
  • Expose required free space

docs.title: Busy Exhaustion
docs.text:
• Return stable unavailable or conflict outcome
  • Record retry count
  • Avoid indefinite wait

docs.title: Foreign-Key Failure
docs.text:
• Roll back
  • Record violated relation
  • Do not disable enforcement as workaround

docs.title: Checksum Mismatch
docs.text:
• Stop migration
  • Mark integrity finding
  • Require operator correction

docs.title: Premature Authority Cutover
docs.text:
New tables may accidentally become authoritative.

Mitigation:

  • Write-authority matrix
  • Feature flags
  • Compatibility read strategy
  • No implicit fallback

docs.title: Identifier Instability
docs.text:
Retries may generate duplicate identities.

Mitigation:

  • Durable mapping
  • Idempotency
  • Unique constraints
  • Transactional checkpoint

docs.title: Dual Write Divergence
docs.text:
Legacy and ChannelForge writes may disagree.

Mitigation:

  • Avoid dual write
  • One authority
  • Reconciliation
  • Metrics
  • Explicit failure

docs.title: SQLite Lock Contention
docs.text:
New repositories may increase write contention.

Mitigation:

  • Short transactions
  • Write coordinator
  • Busy timeout
  • Batch size
  • Metrics

docs.title: WAL Storage Compatibility
docs.text:
Unraid or network-backed storage may behave differently.

Mitigation:

  • Platform testing
  • Health checks
  • Alternative journal policy
  • Documentation

docs.title: Backup Invalidity
docs.text:
Backup may appear successful but not restore.

Mitigation:

  • Manifest
  • Checksum
  • Restore rehearsal
  • Version metadata

docs.title: Migration Non-Idempotency
docs.text:
Restart may duplicate or corrupt.

Mitigation:

  • Unique constraints
  • Mapping
  • Checkpoint
  • Failure injection

docs.title: Checksum Drift
docs.text:
Applied migration source may change.

Mitigation:

  • Immutable migration files
  • Checksum verification
  • New corrective migration

docs.title: Repository Leakage
docs.text:
Raw records may escape.

Mitigation:

  • Module-owned ports
  • Architecture tests
  • Record suffix
  • Public export review

docs.title: Shared Transaction Expansion
docs.text:
Application services may create large cross-module transactions.

Mitigation:

  • Ownership
  • Event handoff
  • Duration metrics
  • Review

docs.title: Provider Call in Transaction
docs.text:
Synchronization may hold write lock during network work.

Mitigation:

  • Staged observation
  • Architecture review
  • Transaction API design

docs.title: Identifier Correlation
docs.text:
Time-ordered identifiers may expose creation time.

Mitigation:

  • Decide explicitly
  • Document API exposure
  • UUIDv4 fallback

docs.title: Schema Prefix Permanence
docs.text:
Temporary cf_ names may remain.

Mitigation:

  • Accept if harmless
  • Avoid cosmetic rename without value
  • Document

docs.title: Test Fixture Privacy
docs.text:
Legacy fixture may contain private data.

Mitigation:

  • Synthetic fixtures
  • Sanitization
  • Review
  • Checksums

docs.title: Restore Version Mismatch
docs.text:
Backup may require different application version.

Mitigation:

  • Manifest
  • Compatibility matrix
  • Release archive

docs.title: Managed File Orphaning
docs.text:
Database and filesystem may diverge.

Mitigation:

  • Staged file state
  • Checksums
  • Reconciliation
  • Retention delay

docs.title: Milestone Invariants
docs.text:
1. SQLite remains the version 1 authority.
  2. New domain code does not depend on raw SQLite.
  3. Repositories are module-owned.
  4. Repository implementations do not expose rows.
  5. ChannelForge identifiers are opaque.
  6. ChannelForge identifiers are stable.
  7. ChannelForge identifiers are provider-independent.
  8. ChannelForge identifiers are legacy-independent.
  9. Human-readable keys are not primary identifiers.
  10. External IDs are source-qualified.
  11. Legacy mappings are durable.
  12. Verified mappings are not silently rewritten.
  13. Mapping conflicts are durable.
  14. Immutable revisions remain immutable.
  15. Approved plans remain immutable.
  16. Persisted instants are UTC.
  17. Transactions are short.
  18. Provider calls do not occur in write transactions.
  19. FFmpeg does not run in write transactions.
  20. Foreign keys are enabled.
  21. Required pragmas are verified.
  22. Busy retry is bounded.
  23. Connection count is bounded.
  24. Query ordering is explicit.
  25. Behavioral queries use stable tie-breakers.
  26. Applied migrations are immutable.
  27. Migration checksums are verified.
  28. Migrations are ordered.
  29. Migrations are restart-safe.
  30. Migrations are observable.
  31. Migration progress is durable.
  32. Migration checkpoints are transactional with batch writes where required.
  33. Critical migrations require backup.
  34. Backups are verified.
  35. Restore is tested.
  36. Source data is preserved.
  37. Legacy tables are not deleted in this milestone.
  38. Unsupported downgrade is blocked.
  39. Partial failure is recorded.
  40. Dual write is exceptional.
  41. Write authority is explicit.
  42. Audit records are append-only.
  43. Secrets are excluded from ordinary tables.
  44. Managed file references use checksums.
  45. Database/file divergence is reconcilable.
  46. Integrity checks are available.
  47. Windows behavior is tested.
  48. Linux behavior is authoritative for production.
  49. Failure injection is included.
  50. Migration fixtures are sanitized.
  51. Package rebranding is not mixed with persistence.
  52. Broad UI changes are not mixed with persistence.
  53. Provider behavior is not redesigned here.
  54. Scheduling behavior is not redesigned here.
  55. Playout behavior is not redesigned here.
  56. Attribution remains intact.
  57. Build remains green.
  58. Milestone 04 does not freeze legacy writes before Milestone 03 completion.
  59. Critical conflicts block cutover.
  60. Completion evidence is reviewable.

docs.title: Milestone 04: Legacy Compatibility
docs.text:
• Roadmap version: 0.1
  • Milestone status: In Progress
  • Last updated: 2026-08-18
  • Risk classification: Compatibility / Critical
  • Implementation authority: Compatibility reads, temporary write translation, route isolation, and legacy dependency measurement

docs.title: Purpose
docs.text:
This milestone defines how ChannelForge continues to operate while inherited Tunarr state, routes, jobs, persistence, identifiers, and runtime behavior are replaced incrementally.

It defines:

  • Legacy subsystem boundaries
  • Compatibility read architecture
  • Compatibility read precedence
  • Legacy identifier resolution
  • Lazy mapping
  • Mapping conflict handling
  • Compatibility query behavior
  • Compatibility write architecture
  • Single-write-authority rules
  • Temporary write translation
  • Dual-write restrictions
  • Partial-failure recovery
  • Reconciliation
  • Legacy route classification
  • Route isolation
  • Route deprecation
  • Compatibility response translation
  • Legacy error translation
  • Legacy background-job handling
  • Legacy scheduling containment
  • Legacy output containment
  • Legacy provider-sync containment
  • Legacy write freeze preparation
  • Server-side freeze enforcement
  • Compatibility metrics
  • Usage evidence
  • Support-window rules
  • Compatibility removal criteria
  • Operator diagnostics
  • Testing
  • Pull-request sequencing
  • Entry and completion gates
  • Rollback
  • Risks
  • Deferred decisions

This milestone does not complete final migration.

It establishes controlled coexistence.

docs.text:
This milestone is governed by:

  • docs/architecture/spec/01-terminology.md
