docs.title: Milestone Mission
docs.text:
ChannelForge must preserve working installations while replacing inherited implementation details.

The compatibility milestone must:

  • Preserve user intent
  • Preserve active Channel output where possible
  • Preserve Media Source connectivity
  • Preserve guide compatibility
  • Preserve stream compatibility
  • Preserve legacy identifiers through mappings
  • Keep legacy behavior observable
  • Keep legacy authority explicit
  • Prevent ambiguous write ownership
  • Prevent new ChannelForge modules from importing legacy row shapes
  • Prevent legacy state from overwriting newer canonical state
  • Allow compatibility reads before canonical writes exist
  • Allow temporary write translation only when required
  • Make partial compatibility failures visible
  • Reconcile divergent state
  • Isolate inherited routes
  • Deprecate routes deliberately
  • Freeze legacy writes server-side before cutover
  • Retain rollback
  • Define removal criteria before removal
  • Preserve attribution and license obligations

docs.title: Product Principle
docs.text:
The governing product principle remains:

Build television networks, not playlists.

Compatibility may expose inherited playlist-oriented behavior temporarily.

New ChannelForge contracts must remain network-first.

Compatibility translates legacy concepts.

It does not redefine the ChannelForge domain around legacy shapes.

docs.title: Core Compatibility Principles
docs.text:
1. Preserve user intent before implementation shape.
  2. ChannelForge identities become canonical after cutover.
  3. Legacy identifiers remain mapped.
  4. Reads may migrate before writes.
  5. One write owner exists per concept per phase.
  6. Dual-write is temporary and explicit.
  7. Compatibility behavior is observable.
  8. Compatibility code has removal criteria.
  9. Legacy state never overwrites newer canonical state.
  10. Invalid legacy state becomes conflict.
  11. Operator decisions are not guessed.
  12. Generated artifacts may be regenerated.
  13. Runtime continuity is preserved where practical.
  14. Compatibility can pause safely.
  15. Compatibility can fail safely.
  16. Compatibility can be rolled back.
  17. Historical lineage remains available.
  18. Legacy routes are isolated.
  19. Legacy jobs are isolated.
  20. Legacy direct database access is not available to new modules.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
This milestone covers inherited Tunarr concepts including:

  • Channels
  • Programs
  • Custom shows
  • Filler lists
  • Media Source configurations
  • Plex settings
  • Jellyfin settings
  • Emby settings
  • Scheduling configuration
  • Schedule records
  • Guide data
  • Stream routes
  • FFmpeg settings
  • HDHomeRun-compatible settings
  • XMLTV settings
  • M3U settings
  • Persistent identifiers
  • Preferences
  • Runtime defaults
  • Database state
  • Container paths
  • Environment variables
  • API routes
  • First-party UI callers
  • Background jobs
  • Search indexes
  • Generated artifacts
  • Attribution notices

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
This milestone does not guarantee exact preservation of:

  • Undocumented internal fields
  • Invalid records
  • Corrupt records
  • Temporary caches
  • Runtime sessions
  • Generated temporary files
  • Unsupported provider payloads
  • Unofficial modifications
  • Direct database edits
  • Deprecated routes beyond their support policy
  • Old UI layout
  • Accidental behavior
  • Unsupported plugin state

Unsupported state must be preserved in backup and surfaced.

It must not be fabricated.

docs.title: Legacy Subsystem Definition
docs.text:
The inherited Tunarr codebase is a legacy subsystem during migration.

Legacy subsystem content includes:

  • Legacy database records
  • Legacy persistence helpers
  • Legacy scheduling logic
  • Legacy provider models
  • Legacy route DTOs
  • Legacy API handlers
  • Legacy UI state contracts
  • Legacy identifiers
  • Legacy output generators
  • Legacy global settings
  • Legacy background jobs
  • Legacy file paths
  • Legacy container defaults
  • Legacy error structures
  • Legacy process-control code

docs.title: Compatibility Boundary
docs.text:
New ChannelForge code may access legacy behavior only through:

  • Legacy repositories
  • Compatibility adapters
  • Compatibility application services
  • Migration services
  • Identity mapping repositories
  • Explicit projections
  • Explicit route adapters

docs.title: Forbidden Direct Dependencies
docs.text:
New ChannelForge modules must not depend directly on:

  • Legacy database row types
  • Legacy query builders
  • Legacy ORM records
  • Legacy global settings objects
  • Legacy provider payloads
  • Legacy route DTOs
  • Legacy scheduling classes
  • Legacy output artifact paths
  • Legacy UI state
  • Legacy process singletons
  • Legacy identifiers as canonical IDs

docs.title: Compatibility Namespace
docs.text:
Recommended path:

server/src/compatibility/tunarr/

Possible structure:

server/src/compatibility/tunarr/
├── index.ts
├── README.md
├── metrics/
├── identity/
├── persistence/
├── routes/
├── providers/
├── scheduling/
├── playout/
├── output/
├── settings/
├── jobs/
├── filesystem/
├── errors/
└── testing/

docs.title: Compatibility Public Entry Point
docs.text:
The compatibility namespace exposes only approved adapters.

Other modules must not deep-import compatibility internals.

docs.title: Compatibility Module Ownership
docs.text:
The Migration module coordinates compatibility state.

The owning ChannelForge module owns the target contract.

Example:

  • Channels owns Channel contract.
  • Compatibility implements Channel legacy read adapter.
  • Migration owns identity mapping and conflict.
  • Output owns XMLTV contract.
  • Compatibility implements legacy XMLTV fallback.
  • Media Sources owns source contract.
  • Compatibility implements legacy source adapter.

docs.title: Anti-Corruption Layer
docs.text:
Compatibility is an anti-corruption layer.

It translates:

  • Legacy identity to ChannelForge identity
  • Legacy Channel to Channel read model
  • Legacy program to Catalog observation
  • Legacy custom show to programming input
  • Legacy filler list to filler policy input
  • Legacy schedule item to schedule compatibility record
  • Legacy output settings to output profile input
  • Legacy errors to stable application errors
  • Legacy route requests to ChannelForge commands
  • ChannelForge results to legacy route responses where supported

docs.title: Translation Direction
docs.text:
Translation direction must be explicit.

Possible directions:

  • Legacy to ChannelForge
  • ChannelForge to legacy
  • Bidirectional temporary translation
  • Read-only projection
  • Diagnostic-only comparison

docs.title: Translation Rule
docs.text:
Translation must not silently lose fields required to preserve user intent.

Unsupported fields become:

  • Warning
  • Conflict
  • Preserved opaque metadata
  • Explicit omission

docs.title: Compatibility Architecture
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    LegacyState["Inherited Tunarr State"]
    LegacyRoutes["Legacy Routes"]
    LegacyJobs["Legacy Jobs"]
    CompatRead["Compatibility Read Layer"]
    CompatWrite["Compatibility Write Layer"]
    Mapping["Identity Mapping"]
    Conflict["Conflict Queue"]
    Metrics["Compatibility Metrics"]
    CFModules["ChannelForge Modules"]
    CFState["ChannelForge State"]
    Reconcile["Reconciliation"]
    Freeze["Legacy Write Freeze"]

    LegacyRoutes --> CompatRead
    LegacyRoutes --> CompatWrite
    LegacyJobs --> CompatRead
    LegacyJobs --> CompatWrite
    LegacyState --> CompatRead
    Mapping --> CompatRead
    CompatRead --> CFModules
    CompatRead --> Conflict
    CompatRead --> Metrics
    CFModules --> CompatWrite
    CompatWrite --> CFState
    CompatWrite --> LegacyState
    CompatWrite --> Conflict
    CompatWrite --> Metrics
    Reconcile --> LegacyState
    Reconcile --> CFState
    Reconcile --> Mapping
    Freeze --> LegacyRoutes
    Freeze --> LegacyJobs

docs.title: Compatibility Modes
docs.text:
A concept may be in one compatibility mode:

  • LEGACY_ONLY
  • LEGACY_READ_CANONICAL_WRITE
  • CANONICAL_READ_LEGACY_FALLBACK
  • CANONICAL_ONLY
  • DUAL_COMPARE
  • TEMPORARY_WRITE_TRANSLATION
  • FROZEN_LEGACY_WRITE
  • RETIRED

docs.title: LEGACY_ONLY
docs.text:
Legacy state is authoritative.

ChannelForge reads through an adapter.

No ChannelForge write path exists.

docs.title: LEGACY_READ_CANONICAL_WRITE
docs.text:
ChannelForge writes canonical state.

Legacy reads may still exist.

Legacy runtime may require projection.

docs.title: CANONICAL_READ_LEGACY_FALLBACK
docs.text:
Read canonical first.

Fallback to legacy only when canonical state is absent.

docs.title: CANONICAL_ONLY
docs.text:
Only ChannelForge state is used.

Legacy state remains for rollback or historical diagnostics.

docs.title: DUAL_COMPARE
docs.text:
Both states are read for comparison.

One result remains authoritative.

docs.title: TEMPORARY_WRITE_TRANSLATION
docs.text: One validated command writes authoritative state and produces a required compatibility representation.

docs.title: FROZEN_LEGACY_WRITE
docs.text: Legacy mutation paths are blocked server-side.

docs.title: RETIRED
docs.text:
Compatibility path is removed from active runtime.

Historical fixtures remain.

docs.title: Compatibility Mode Registry
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/compatibility/mode-registry.md

Suggested columns:

Concept Current mode Read authority Write authority Fallback Cutover gate Removal milestone

docs.title: Source-of-Truth Classification
docs.text:
Every legacy concept must be classified:

  • Authoritative
  • Derived
  • Cache
  • Runtime
  • Configuration
  • Secret
  • Historical
  • Unknown

docs.title: Authoritative Legacy Examples
docs.text:
Potential examples:

  • Channel definitions
  • Channel numbers
  • Channel names
  • Program assignments
  • Custom show membership
  • Filler membership
  • Media Source configuration
  • Output settings
  • User-selected order

The baseline inventory decides actual authority.

docs.title: Derived Legacy Examples
docs.text:
Potential examples:

  • XMLTV artifact
  • M3U artifact
  • Search index
  • Cached provider metadata
  • Runtime progress
  • Temporary transcode file

Derived state should normally be regenerated.

docs.title: Unknown Legacy State
docs.text:
Unknown state must be:

  • Inventoried
  • Backed up
  • Excluded from deletion
  • Flagged
  • Assigned an owner
  • Kept out of hidden runtime dependency

docs.title: Compatibility Read
docs.text: A Compatibility Read interprets legacy state without rewriting it first.

docs.title: Compatibility Read Goals
docs.text:
• Keep old installation usable
  • Permit staged migration
  • Produce ChannelForge contracts
  • Resolve legacy identity
  • Record fallback use
  • Detect conflicts
  • Avoid mutation
  • Avoid provider calls where unnecessary
  • Avoid hidden caching
  • Keep deterministic behavior

docs.title: Compatibility Repository
docs.text:
A compatibility repository may:

  • Read ChannelForge state first
  • Resolve explicit mapping
  • Fall back to legacy state
  • Translate to canonical domain or read model
  • Create a proposed mapping where policy permits
  • Record metrics
  • Record conflict
  • Avoid legacy-only writes

docs.title: Recommended Read Precedence
docs.text:
After canonical data exists:

  1. ChannelForge canonical state
  2. Verified identity mapping
  3. Legacy compatibility read
  4. Conflict
  5. Not found

docs.title: Canonical Precedence Rule
docs.text: Legacy state must never overwrite newer ChannelForge state.

docs.title: Read Strategy by Concept
docs.text:
Each concept defines:

  • Canonical table
  • Legacy table
  • Mapping namespace
  • Fallback eligibility
  • Lazy mapping eligibility
  • Conflict behavior
  • Cache behavior
  • Metrics
  • Removal gate

docs.title: Read Context
docs.text:
Compatibility reads should receive:

  • Actor or service identity where applicable
  • Correlation ID
  • Route or operation name
  • Requested identifier
  • Allowed fallback policy
  • Diagnostic mode
  • Cancellation signal

docs.title: Read Result
docs.text:
A compatibility read result may include:

export type CompatibilityReadResult<T> =
  | {
      source: "CANONICAL";
      value: T;
      mappingId?: string;
    }
  | {
      source: "LEGACY_FALLBACK";
      value: T;
      mappingId?: string;
      warningCodes: readonly string[];
    }
  | {
      source: "CONFLICT";
      conflictId: string;
    }
  | {
      source: "NOT_FOUND";
    };

docs.title: Read Result Exposure
docs.text:
Ordinary public APIs should not expose internal compatibility metadata by default.

Authorized diagnostics may expose:

  • Source
  • Mapping
  • Warning
  • Conflict
  • Legacy namespace
  • Legacy ID

docs.title: Legacy ID Lookup
docs.text:
Legacy IDs may resolve through:

  • Mapping table
  • Compatibility route parameter
  • Legacy row lookup
  • Historical reference
  • Import manifest

docs.title: Legacy ID Non-Canonical Rule
docs.text: A legacy ID is never returned as the canonical id after cutover.

docs.title: Lazy Mapping
docs.text:
A compatibility read may materialize a mapping lazily when:

  • Legacy identity is unambiguous
  • Target entity already exists
  • Type matches
  • Uniqueness holds
  • Policy allows lazy mapping
  • The mapping write is idempotent
  • Audit is recorded
  • The read can tolerate the mapping transaction

docs.title: Lazy Mapping Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not lazily map when:

  • Multiple targets exist
  • Parent mapping is missing
  • Legacy record is corrupt
  • Mapping changes authority
  • Mapping requires operator judgment
  • Mapping would merge entities
  • Mapping would split entity
  • Secret material is involved
  • Active publication identity changes

docs.title: Lazy Mapping Failure
docs.text:
A lazy mapping failure must not silently return an incorrect target.

Possible outcomes:

  • Return translated legacy read without mapping
  • Return conflict
  • Return unavailable
  • Retry mapping
  • Queue reconciliation

Policy is concept-specific.

docs.title: Mapping Verification
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Legacy row exists
  • Target entity exists
  • Types match
  • Required fields match
  • Mapping uniqueness holds
  • Parent references resolve
  • No orphan mapping
  • Semantic comparison passes
  • Mapping is not tombstoned

docs.title: Mapping State
docs.text:
Supported mapping states:

  • PROPOSED
  • MAPPED
  • VERIFIED
  • CONFLICT
  • MERGED
  • SPLIT
  • OMITTED
  • TOMBSTONED
  • SUPERSEDED
  • ROLLED_BACK

docs.title: Mapping Conflict
docs.text:
A mapping conflict is durable.

It contains:

  • Qualified legacy identity
  • Candidate ChannelForge identities
  • Reason
  • Evidence
  • Affected route or service
  • First observed
  • Last observed
  • Occurrence count
  • Migration run
  • Operator status

docs.title: Mapping Conflict Behavior
docs.text: A conflict must not be resolved by arbitrary first match.

docs.title: Tombstone
docs.text:
A migration tombstone records that legacy state was:

  • Retired
  • Merged
  • Invalid
  • Omitted
  • Replaced
  • Deleted according to policy

docs.title: Tombstone Read
docs.text:
A tombstoned legacy ID returns a controlled result.

It must not create a new entity automatically.

docs.title: Compatibility Read Metrics
docs.text:
Track:

  • Legacy fallback read count
  • Canonical read count
  • Mapping lookup count
  • Mapping creation count
  • Mapping conflict count
  • Legacy entity type
  • Route template
  • Service operation
  • Success
  • Failure
  • Latency
  • Application version
  • Source schema version
  • Caller class
  • Fallback reason

docs.title: Metric Cardinality
docs.text:
Do not use raw identifiers as high-cardinality metric labels.

Raw IDs may appear in structured diagnostic logs with access controls.

docs.title: Compatibility Read Logging
docs.text:
Structured fields:

  • compatibilityMode
  • legacyNamespace
  • legacyEntityType
  • source
  • routeTemplate
  • operation
  • mappingState
  • conflictId
  • correlationId
  • durationMs

docs.title: Compatibility Read Health
docs.text:
Health states:

  • UNUSED
  • HEALTHY
  • DEGRADED
  • CONFLICTED
  • FAILED
  • FROZEN
  • RETIRED

docs.title: Compatibility Read Removal Criterion
docs.text:
A compatibility read path may be removed when:

  • All supported source versions migrate
  • Migration coverage is complete
  • Usage metrics show no supported use
  • Support window has elapsed
  • Rollback window is closed
  • Historical fixtures remain
  • Release notes announce removal
  • First-party callers are migrated
  • External caller policy is satisfied
  • Operator diagnostics no longer require active path

docs.title: Compatibility Query
docs.text:
Compatibility queries are read-only.

They may join legacy and mapping state.

They must use explicit deterministic ordering.

docs.title: Compatibility Cache
docs.text:
A compatibility cache may improve expensive legacy reads.

It must:

  • Be derived
  • Be bounded
  • Include source version
  • Include invalidation
  • Not become authoritative
  • Not hide fallback usage
  • Be clear on restart

docs.title: Shadow Read
docs.text: Shadow Read compares legacy and canonical representations.

docs.title: Shadow Read Goals
docs.text:
• Detect translation mismatch
  • Measure migration quality
  • Detect stale canonical data
  • Detect hidden legacy behavior
  • Build cutover confidence

docs.title: Shadow Read Authority
docs.text:
One side is always designated authoritative.

Comparison does not create dual authority.

docs.title: Shadow Read Output
docs.text:
Record:

  • Concept
  • Authority
  • Legacy checksum
  • Canonical checksum
  • Difference class
  • Route or operation
  • Timestamp
  • Correlation ID
  • Severity

docs.title: Difference Classes
docs.text:
• EQUAL
  • EXPECTED_FORMATTING_DIFFERENCE
  • EXPECTED_SEMANTIC_DIFFERENCE
  • LEGACY_MISSING
  • CANONICAL_MISSING
  • IDENTITY_MISMATCH
  • VALUE_MISMATCH
  • ORDER_MISMATCH
  • ERROR_MISMATCH
  • UNKNOWN

docs.title: Shadow Read Sampling
docs.text:
High-volume paths may use sampling.

Sampling must not be used for critical identity validation.

docs.title: Shadow Read Performance
docs.text:
Shadow reads must be:

  • Bounded
  • Cancelable
  • Measured
  • Disableable
  • Non-mutating

docs.title: Compatibility Write
docs.text:
Compatibility Write is temporary.

It translates one authoritative command into required legacy representation.

docs.title: Compatibility Write Goals
docs.text:
• Keep legacy runtime working
  • Permit new UI/API adoption
  • Keep one command authority
  • Detect partial failure
  • Reconcile divergence
  • Preserve rollback
  • Remove itself later

docs.title: Write Authority
docs.text: Every concept has exactly one write authority per phase.

docs.title: Write Authority Registry
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/compatibility/write-authority.md

Suggested columns:

Concept Phase Authoritative writer Compatibility target Failure policy Freeze gate

docs.title: Before Cutover
docs.text:
Channel identity:
  legacy write authority
  ChannelForge compatibility read

docs.title: During Temporary Translation
docs.text:
Channel identity:
  ChannelForge command authority
  legacy representation derived

docs.title: After Cutover
docs.text:
Channel identity:
  ChannelForge read/write authority
  legacy mapping read-only

docs.title: Ambiguous Authority Prohibition
docs.text: Legacy and ChannelForge stores may not accept independent writes for the same concept.

docs.title: Temporary Write Translation
docs.text:
Temporary translation is permitted when:

  • Legacy runtime still consumes old tables
  • First-party UI writes new contracts
  • Output still reads legacy shape
  • Cutover spans releases
  • A required external client still depends on legacy route

docs.title: Translation Command Flow
docs.text:
sequenceDiagram
    participant Caller
    participant Route
    participant CFApp as ChannelForge Application
    participant CFDB as ChannelForge State
    participant Compat as Compatibility Translator
    participant Legacy as Legacy State
    participant Recon as Reconciliation

    Caller->>Route: Validated command
    Route->>CFApp: Execute command
    CFApp->>CFDB: Commit authoritative state
    CFApp->>Compat: Produce compatibility representation
    Compat->>Legacy: Write derived legacy state
    alt Legacy write succeeds
        Compat-->>CFApp: Compatibility current
    else Legacy write fails
        Compat->>Recon: Queue reconciliation
        Compat-->>CFApp: Compatibility degraded
    end
    CFApp-->>Route: Explicit result

docs.title: Authoritative Commit Order
docs.text:
Preferred order:

  1. Validate command.
  2. Authorize command.
  3. Commit ChannelForge authoritative state.
  4. Record audit.
  5. Translate to compatibility representation.
  6. Write legacy representation.
  7. Record compatibility status.
  8. Queue reconciliation on failure.
  9. Return explicit result.

Some concepts may require one transaction across schemas in one SQLite database.

That exception must be documented.

docs.title: Single-Transaction Translation
docs.text:
A single SQLite transaction may update canonical and legacy tables when:

  • Both tables share one database
  • No external call occurs
  • Lock duration remains bounded
  • Mapping and status update are included
  • Rollback semantics are clear
  • One command remains authoritative

docs.title: Recovery-Protocol Translation
docs.text:
Use a recovery protocol when:

  • Filesystem is involved
  • Separate store is involved
  • Long transformation is involved
  • Legacy representation is derived asynchronously
  • Atomicity is unavailable

docs.title: Dual-Write Definition
docs.text:
Dual-write means one command produces both canonical and legacy writes.

It does not mean two independent clients may write both stores.

docs.title: Dual-Write Requirements
docs.text:
When unavoidable:

  • ChannelForge command is authoritative after declared cutover phase
  • One validated command produces both outputs
  • Idempotency exists
  • Partial failure is detectable
  • Compatibility status is durable
  • Reconciliation exists
  • Metrics exist
  • Removal milestone exists
  • Rollback exists
  • Tests inject partial failure

docs.title: Dual-Write Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not dual-write:

  • Plaintext secrets
  • Approved Schedule Plans
  • Audit records through independent authorities
  • Runtime stream URLs
  • Provider payloads
  • Plugin internal state
  • Temporary sessions
  • Raw tokens
  • Ephemeral FFmpeg state

docs.title: Partial Failure
docs.text:
Partial failure occurs when:

  • Canonical write succeeds and legacy write fails
  • Legacy write succeeds and canonical write fails
  • Mapping write fails
  • Compatibility status write fails
  • File projection fails
  • Reconciliation enqueue fails

docs.title: Partial Failure Rule
docs.text: Do not report uncomplicated success silently.

docs.title: Partial Failure Result
docs.text:
Possible explicit outcomes:

  • Success with compatibility warning
  • Accepted with reconciliation job
  • Failure with canonical commit retained
  • Failure with transaction rolled back
  • Service degraded
  • Legacy runtime blocked
  • Operator action required

docs.title: Partial Failure Policy
docs.text:
Policy is concept-specific.

It must state:

  • Authority retained
  • Caller response
  • Runtime effect
  • Retry
  • Reconciliation
  • Audit
  • Health
  • Rollback

docs.title: Compatibility Status Record
docs.text:
Suggested conceptual fields:

compatibility_status_id
concept_type
channelforge_id
legacy_namespace
legacy_id
mode
state
canonical_version
legacy_version
last_attempt_at
last_success_at
failure_count
last_error_code
reconciliation_job_id

docs.title: Compatibility Status State
docs.text:
• CURRENT
  • PENDING
  • DEGRADED
  • FAILED
  • CONFLICT
  • FROZEN
  • RETIRED

docs.title: Reconciliation
docs.text: Reconciliation compares and repairs compatibility representation.

docs.title: Reconciliation Inputs
docs.text:
• Canonical entity
  • Legacy representation
  • Mapping
  • Compatibility status
  • Expected translation version
  • Previous findings
  • Policy

docs.title: Reconciliation Output
docs.text:
• Equal
  • Legacy repaired
  • Canonical repair required
  • Conflict
  • Unsupported
  • Retry
  • Operator action

docs.title: Reconciliation Authority
docs.text: Reconciliation must not overwrite canonical state from legacy without an explicit migration command.

docs.title: Reconciliation Job
docs.text:
A reconciliation job:

  • Is idempotent
  • Uses bounded batches
  • Is restart-safe
  • Records progress
  • Records findings
  • Uses mapping
  • Avoids provider calls inside write transactions
  • Does not start FFmpeg
  • Can be canceled safely

docs.title: Reconciliation Finding
docs.text:
Fields:

  • Finding ID
  • Concept
  • Canonical ID
  • Legacy ID
  • Difference
  • Severity
  • Repair action
  • Attempt count
  • Status
  • First observed
  • Last observed
  • Resolved timestamp

docs.title: Reconciliation Severity
docs.text:
• INFO
  • WARNING
  • ERROR
  • CRITICAL

docs.title: Reconciliation Metrics
docs.text:
• Items compared
  • Equal
  • Repaired
  • Conflicts
  • Failed
  • Duration
  • Retry count
  • Oldest unresolved age

docs.title: Reconciliation Schedule
docs.text:
Possible triggers:

  • After write failure
  • On startup
  • Periodic
  • Before cutover
  • Operator request
  • Before legacy freeze
  • Before release validation

docs.title: Legacy Route Inventory
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/compatibility/legacy-route-inventory.md

For each route, record:

  • Method
  • Path
  • Handler
  • Request DTO
  • Response DTO
  • Authentication
  • Authorization
  • Read/write
  • Current callers
  • First-party caller
  • External caller evidence
  • Legacy identifiers
  • Legacy persistence access
  • Target ChannelForge route
  • Compatibility classification
  • Deprecation date
  • Removal gate

docs.title: Legacy Route Classification
docs.text:
Use:

  • PRESERVE_EXACT
  • ADAPT_READ
  • ADAPT_WRITE
  • TRANSLATE_RESPONSE
  • DEPRECATE
  • FREEZE_WRITE
  • INTERNAL_ONLY
  • OUTPUT_PROTOCOL
  • STREAM_PROTOCOL
  • REMOVE_LATER
  • UNKNOWN

docs.title: Preserve Exact
docs.text:
Use only when protocol compatibility requires exact behavior.

Examples may include:

  • HDHomeRun-compatible endpoints
  • Existing M3U endpoint
  • Existing XMLTV endpoint
  • Stream route used by configured clients

Exact preservation must not imply legacy internal ownership.

docs.title: Adapt Read
docs.text:
Legacy route calls ChannelForge query.

Response is translated to legacy shape.

docs.title: Adapt Write
docs.text:
Legacy route translates request to ChannelForge command.

ChannelForge command remains authoritative.

docs.title: Translate Response
docs.text: New application service result is serialized into old DTO.

docs.title: Deprecate
docs.text:
Route remains active during support period.

It provides replacement guidance.

docs.title: Freeze Write
docs.text: Route remains resolvable but rejects mutation after cutover.

docs.title: Internal Only
docs.text: Route is used only by inherited first-party UI and can be removed after UI migration.

docs.title: Output Protocol
docs.text: Route follows external client protocol rather than management API convention.

docs.title: Stream Protocol
docs.text: Route has long-lived response behavior and separate error rules.

docs.title: Route Isolation
docs.text:
Legacy routes must register under an explicit compatibility registration path.

Suggested:

server/src/compatibility/tunarr/routes/

docs.title: Route Registration
docs.text: The application host registers legacy routes separately from ChannelForge v1 routes.

docs.title: Route Tagging
docs.text:
OpenAPI or route metadata should tag:

legacy
deprecated
compatibility

where applicable.

docs.title: Legacy Route Handler Rule
docs.text:
A legacy route handler may:

  • Parse legacy request
  • Authenticate
  • Authorize
  • Translate identifiers
  • Call ChannelForge application service
  • Translate result
  • Add deprecation metadata
  • Record usage

It must not:

  • Query legacy tables directly after an adapter exists
  • Implement domain logic
  • Start FFmpeg directly
  • Generate schedule directly
  • Write both stores independently
  • Expose secrets
  • Guess conflict resolution

docs.title: Route Deprecation
docs.text:
A deprecated route must document:

  • Replacement
  • Support window
  • Behavior differences
  • Identifier differences
  • Error differences
  • Removal gate
  • Migration guidance

docs.title: Deprecation Headers
docs.text:
Where practical, use:

  • Deprecation
  • Sunset
  • Link
  • Warning headers
  • Documentation link

Exact header support must be validated against clients.

docs.title: Deprecation Response Metadata
docs.text:
Management JSON responses may include authorized migration guidance.

Protocol endpoints should avoid breaking response shape.

docs.title: Route Usage Metrics
docs.text:
Track:

  • Route template
  • Method
  • Status
  • Caller class
  • Version
  • Deprecation
  • Compatibility mode
  • Legacy identifier use
  • Replacement route availability
  • Latency
  • Error code

docs.title: Caller Classification
docs.text:
Possible caller classes:

  • First-party web
  • Plex
  • Jellyfin
  • Emby
  • IPTV client
  • Browser
  • Automation
  • Unknown
  • Health probe

docs.title: Caller Privacy
docs.text: Do not fingerprint clients beyond operational need.

docs.title: Route Removal Criterion
docs.text:
A legacy route may be removed when:

  • First-party caller is migrated
  • Supported external clients no longer require it
  • Usage is zero across support window
  • Replacement is documented
  • Release notes announce removal
  • Metrics are trustworthy
  • Rollback window is closed
  • Historical contract tests remain
  • Removal does not break output protocol compatibility

docs.title: Compatibility Error Translation
docs.text: Legacy errors translate to stable application errors.

docs.title: Error Translation Table
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/compatibility/error-translation.md

Fields:

Legacy error ChannelForge error Legacy route response Canonical route response Retryable

docs.title: Error Translation Rule
docs.text:
Do not expose:

  • Stack trace
  • SQL
  • Provider token
  • Authorization header
  • Signed URL
  • Filesystem secret
  • Process command with secret
  • Internal mapping detail to unauthorized caller

docs.title: Legacy Error Preservation
docs.text:
Where clients rely on status semantics, preserve status during support period.

Message text is not a stable contract unless documented.

docs.title: Frozen Write Error
docs.text:
A frozen legacy mutation returns:

  • Controlled status
  • Stable error code
  • Replacement route or workflow
  • Request ID
  • Deprecation information
  • No partial mutation

Suggested error code:

LEGACY_WRITE_FROZEN

docs.title: Compatibility Authorization
docs.text: Compatibility does not bypass security.

docs.title: Authorization Rule
docs.text:
Legacy route authorization maps to current permissions.

Hiding UI is insufficient.

docs.title: Legacy Authentication
docs.text:
Inherited authentication may remain temporarily.

It must translate to a ChannelForge Principal before application service use.

docs.title: Principal Mapping
docs.text:
Record:

  • Legacy identity
  • ChannelForge User ID
  • Role mapping
  • Scope mapping
  • Conflict
  • Last verified

docs.title: Anonymous Output Routes
docs.text:
Output and stream routes may remain unauthenticated according to configured policy.

That does not grant management access.

docs.title: Compatibility Secrets
docs.text: Secret values must never be translated through ordinary compatibility DTOs.

docs.title: Provider Credentials
docs.text:
Compatibility may resolve legacy credential storage through Secret Service adapter.

It must not copy plaintext into ordinary tables.

docs.title: Provider Compatibility
docs.text:
Media Source compatibility must preserve:

  • Source identity
  • Base URL
  • Selected libraries
  • Credentials
  • Provider type
  • Connectivity
  • Path mapping
  • Playback settings
  • Synchronization policy

docs.title: Provider Compatibility Read
docs.text: Legacy provider configuration becomes a ChannelForge Media Source read model.

docs.title: Provider Compatibility Write
docs.text:
Avoid writing provider credentials to both stores.

Preferred strategy:

  • Secret Service authoritative
  • Legacy secret adapter resolves reference
  • Legacy runtime consumes controlled resolver
  • No plaintext projection

docs.title: Provider Sync Containment
docs.text:
Legacy provider synchronization may remain temporarily.

It must be invoked through a compatibility job handler.

docs.title: Provider Sync Write Authority
docs.text:
Per phase, state whether legacy sync writes:

  • Legacy only
  • Canonical observations
  • Temporary projection
  • Disabled

docs.title: Provider Payload Rule
docs.text: Raw provider payload remains inside adapter or compatibility boundary.

docs.title: Scheduling Compatibility
docs.text: Legacy scheduling must remain isolated.

docs.title: Legacy Scheduler Modes
docs.text:
• Legacy authoritative
  • Shadow compare
  • Compatibility input provider
  • Disabled
  • Retired

docs.title: Scheduling Read Compatibility
docs.text:
Legacy schedule state may be translated to:

  • Compatibility schedule read model
  • Historical schedule entry
  • Migration input
  • Published fallback

docs.title: Scheduling Write Compatibility
docs.text:
Do not independently write approved Schedule Plans to legacy and canonical systems.

Approved Schedule Plans are canonical immutable state.

docs.title: Scheduler Shadow Compare
docs.text:
When comparing legacy and ChannelForge schedules:

  • Fix input
  • Fix horizon
  • Fix time zone
  • Fix seed where possible
  • Normalize IDs
  • Normalize expected formatting differences
  • Compare ordering
  • Compare durations
  • Compare continuity
  • Record difference

docs.title: Legacy Scheduler Freeze
docs.text:
Before scheduling cutover:

  • Disable legacy generation commands
  • Disable legacy background generation
  • Disable direct schedule writers
  • Preserve read access
  • Keep active published schedule
  • Expose replacement

docs.title: Playout Compatibility
docs.text: Legacy playout may remain active while publication migrates.

docs.title: Playout Authority
docs.text:
Playout consumes one active publication authority.

It must not choose between independent legacy and canonical schedules implicitly.

docs.title: Playout Fallback
docs.text:
A fallback may use legacy schedule only when:

  • Compatibility mode permits
  • Canonical publication absent
  • Mapping resolves
  • Policy is explicit
  • Usage is recorded

docs.title: FFmpeg Compatibility
docs.text: Legacy FFmpeg settings may be translated to an output or transcode profile.

docs.title: FFmpeg Write Rule
docs.text: Do not write FFmpeg runtime process state to canonical persistence as configuration.

docs.title: Output Compatibility
docs.text:
Output compatibility includes:

  • XMLTV
  • M3U
  • HDHomeRun-compatible discovery
  • HDHomeRun-compatible lineup
  • Stream URLs
  • Channel logos
  • Device identity

docs.title: Output Identity
docs.text: All output adapters must converge on canonical Channel ID after cutover.

docs.title: Legacy Output Fallback
docs.text: Legacy output may remain last-known-good artifact.

docs.title: Artifact Precedence
docs.text:
Recommended:

  1. Valid canonical artifact
  2. Last valid canonical artifact
  3. Supported legacy artifact
  4. Controlled unavailable result

docs.title: Artifact Regeneration
docs.text: Derived legacy artifacts should normally be regenerated.

docs.title: Output Route Stability
docs.text: Protocol-compatible routes may keep legacy path while using canonical state.

docs.title: Device Identity
docs.text:
Changing HDHomeRun-compatible device identity can cause client reconfiguration.

Treat it as a separate compatibility decision.

docs.title: Channel Number Compatibility
docs.text:
Preserve Channel numbers where valid.

Conflicts require operator-visible resolution.

docs.title: Stream URL Compatibility
docs.text: Existing configured stream URLs should remain valid during support window where practical.

docs.title: Stream Redirect
docs.text: Redirect may be used only if client compatibility is verified.

docs.title: Stream Token Compatibility
docs.text: Do not expose provider credentials in compatibility stream URLs.

docs.title: Guide Identity Compatibility
docs.text: XMLTV Channel IDs must remain stable or explicitly mapped.

docs.title: Legacy Background Jobs
docs.text: Inventory every legacy job.

docs.title: Legacy Job Classification
docs.text:
• Read-only
  • Legacy write
  • Compatibility projection
  • Provider synchronization
  • Schedule generation
  • Artifact generation
  • Cleanup
  • Backup
  • Unknown

docs.title: Legacy Job Handler
docs.text:
A legacy job handler may:

  • Call compatibility service
  • Record job status
  • Translate input
  • Record usage

It must not retain hidden write authority after freeze.

docs.title: Legacy Job Freeze
docs.text:
Freeze applies server-side to:

  • Enqueue
  • Start
  • Retry
  • Reschedule
  • Startup recovery

docs.title: Interrupted Legacy Job
docs.text:
On cutover, an interrupted job must be:

  • Completed safely
  • Canceled
  • Reconciled
  • Marked abandoned
  • Migrated

Policy is job-specific.

docs.title: Legacy Settings Compatibility
docs.text:
Inventory:

  • Environment variables
  • Database settings
  • JSON settings
  • Defaults
  • Container paths
  • UI settings

docs.title: Settings Read Precedence
docs.text:
Recommended:

  1. ChannelForge explicit setting
  2. Migrated setting
  3. Supported legacy setting
  4. ChannelForge default

docs.title: Settings Write Authority
docs.text:
New setting writes should target ChannelForge state.

Legacy projection is temporary where runtime requires it.

docs.title: Environment Variable Compatibility
docs.text: Existing variables may remain aliases.

docs.title: Environment Alias Rules
docs.text:
An alias must define:

  • Canonical variable
  • Legacy variable
  • Precedence
  • Conflict behavior
  • Deprecation
  • Removal gate

docs.title: Environment Conflict
docs.text:
If both canonical and legacy variables are set differently:

  • Fail or warn according to risk
  • State which wins
  • Do not guess silently

docs.title: Path Compatibility
docs.text: Existing data paths may remain aliases or migration sources.

docs.title: Path Rules
docs.text:
• Preserve existing mounts
  • Avoid moving data automatically without backup
  • Resolve one canonical data root
  • Record legacy root
  • Avoid duplicating mutable database files
  • Keep managed file ownership explicit

docs.title: Container Compatibility
docs.text: Existing Docker and Unraid configurations should remain operable through documented aliases where possible.

docs.title: Container Compatibility Fields
docs.text:
• Image name
  • Container name
  • Port
  • Data volume
  • Time zone
  • PUID
  • PGID
  • Device mappings
  • Environment variables
  • Health checks
  • Network mode

docs.title: Package Identity Compatibility
docs.text: Package rebranding is not part of this milestone.

docs.title: First-Party UI Compatibility
docs.text: The inherited UI may call legacy routes temporarily.

docs.title: UI Caller Migration
docs.text:
For each UI feature:

  1. Identify route.
  2. Identify legacy DTO.
  3. Identify canonical use case.
  4. Add canonical client.
  5. Compare behavior.
  6. Switch UI.
  7. Record route usage decline.
  8. Remove legacy caller.
  9. Keep route for external support window if needed.

docs.title: UI Feature Flag
docs.text:
A feature flag may select:

  • Legacy UI path
  • Canonical UI path
  • Shadow read
  • Read-only preview

docs.title: UI Write Rule
docs.text: A UI must not submit to both legacy and canonical mutation routes.

docs.title: Compatibility Feature Flags
docs.text:
Feature flags may control:

  • Canonical read
  • Legacy fallback
  • Shadow compare
  • Temporary write translation
  • Legacy route registration
  • Legacy job registration
  • Legacy write freeze
  • Canonical output

docs.title: Feature Flag Requirements
docs.text:
• Default documented
  • Scope documented
  • Persisted or deployment controlled
  • Observable
  • Safe restart
  • No hidden authority
  • Removal milestone

docs.title: Compatibility State Machine
docs.text:
Suggested states:

  • DISCOVERED
  • WRAPPED
  • MEASURED
  • CANONICAL_READ
  • CANONICAL_WRITE
  • LEGACY_WRITE_FROZEN
  • LEGACY_READ_ONLY
  • RETIRED

docs.title: State Transition Rules
docs.text:
stateDiagram-v2
    [*] --> DISCOVERED
    DISCOVERED --> WRAPPED
    WRAPPED --> MEASURED
    MEASURED --> CANONICAL_READ
    CANONICAL_READ --> CANONICAL_WRITE
    CANONICAL_WRITE --> LEGACY_WRITE_FROZEN
    LEGACY_WRITE_FROZEN --> LEGACY_READ_ONLY
    LEGACY_READ_ONLY --> RETIRED

    CANONICAL_READ --> WRAPPED: rollback
    CANONICAL_WRITE --> CANONICAL_READ: rollback
    LEGACY_WRITE_FROZEN --> CANONICAL_WRITE: rollback

docs.title: Transition Evidence
docs.text:
Every transition records:

  • Concept
  • Previous state
  • New state
  • Actor
  • Application version
  • Migration run
  • Metrics snapshot
  • Validation
  • Rollback point
  • Timestamp

docs.title: Legacy Write Freeze
docs.text: Legacy Write Freeze disables inherited mutation paths.

docs.title: Freeze Scope
docs.text:
Freeze may apply to:

  • Legacy management routes
  • Legacy UI forms
  • Legacy background jobs
  • Legacy direct database writers
  • Legacy schedule writers
  • Legacy provider sync writers
  • Legacy output generators
  • Legacy settings writers
  • Legacy cleanup jobs

docs.title: Freeze Enforcement
docs.text:
Freeze must be server-side.

UI hiding is insufficient.

docs.title: Freeze Registry
docs.text:
Create:

docs/implementation/compatibility/freeze-registry.md

Fields:

Write path Concept Enforcement point Replacement Validation Rollback

docs.title: Freeze Preflight
docs.text:
Before freeze:

  • Canonical writer passes tests
  • Mapping coverage complete
  • Reconciliation current
  • Compatibility status healthy
  • Backup verified
  • Rollback point recorded
  • First-party caller migrated
  • Jobs drained
  • Active streams policy decided
  • Output policy decided
  • Operator notified

docs.title: Freeze Activation
docs.text: Freeze activation should be atomic where practical.

docs.title: Freeze Activation Record
docs.text:
Record:

  • Freeze ID
  • Scope
  • Activated at
  • Activated by
  • Migration run
  • Application version
  • Backup
  • Validation
  • Rollback eligibility

docs.title: Freeze Runtime Behavior
docs.text:
A frozen writer:

  • Performs no mutation
  • Returns stable error
  • Records usage
  • Provides replacement
  • Does not enqueue hidden work
  • Does not partially translate

docs.title: Freeze Rollback
docs.text:
Rollback may re-enable legacy writes only when:

  • Canonical writes are paused
  • Reconciliation confirms state
  • Mapping remains valid
  • Backup exists
  • Operator approves

docs.title: Freeze Validation
docs.text:
After freeze:

  • Legacy write attempts fail
  • Canonical writes succeed
  • Legacy reads still work where supported
  • Output continues
  • Streams continue according to policy
  • Jobs use canonical services
  • Metrics record attempts
  • No direct database writer bypasses freeze

docs.title: Direct Write Detection
docs.text: Architecture tests and runtime instrumentation should detect legacy direct writes.

docs.title: Write Detection Strategies
docs.text:
• Static import rules
  • Repository wrappers
  • SQLite update hooks where available
  • Query logging
  • Table triggers for diagnostics where safe
  • Test-only instrumentation
  • Code search
  • Feature-gated writer registry

docs.title: SQLite Trigger Caution
docs.text: Diagnostic triggers must not become permanent business logic.

docs.title: Compatibility Metrics
docs.text: Create a compatibility dashboard or diagnostic report.

docs.title: Required Metrics
docs.text:
• Legacy fallback reads
  • Canonical reads
  • Shadow comparisons
  • Shadow mismatches
  • Legacy route calls
  • Deprecated route calls
  • Legacy write attempts
  • Frozen write attempts
  • Temporary translation successes
  • Temporary translation failures
  • Reconciliation queue depth
  • Oldest reconciliation finding
  • Mapping conflicts
  • Lazy mappings
  • Unmapped legacy IDs
  • Compatibility latency
  • Compatibility errors
  • Legacy job executions
  • Legacy output fallbacks

docs.title: Metric Dimensions
docs.text:
Bounded dimensions:

  • Concept
  • Entity type
  • Route template
  • Operation
  • Compatibility mode
  • Result
  • Application version
  • Source schema version

docs.title: Compatibility Diagnostic API
docs.text:
Authorized diagnostics may expose:

  • Mode registry
  • Write authority
  • Route usage
  • Fallback count
  • Mapping health
  • Conflict count
  • Reconciliation state
  • Freeze state
  • Removal readiness

docs.title: Diagnostic Security
docs.text:
Do not expose:

  • Raw credentials
  • Full provider URLs with tokens
  • Private media paths
  • Raw database rows
  • Session secrets
  • Arbitrary SQL

docs.title: Compatibility Support Bundle
docs.text:
A support bundle may include:

  • Version
  • Schema version
  • Mode registry
  • Metrics summary
  • Conflict summary
  • Route inventory
  • Freeze state
  • Mapping counts
  • Sanitized logs
  • Checksums

docs.title: Removal Readiness Report

Create:

docs/implementation/compatibility/removal-readiness.md

For each path:

  • Current usage
  • Last observed use
  • Supported source versions
  • First-party callers
  • External callers
  • Replacement
  • Test fixtures

docs.title: Support Window
docs.text: A compatibility path remains through a defined support window.

docs.title: Support Window Inputs
docs.text:
• Release cadence
  • Supported upgrade paths
  • Client behavior
  • External API users
  • Migration fixture coverage
  • Rollback policy
  • Operator impact

docs.title: Zero Usage
docs.text:
Zero observed usage is necessary but not always sufficient.

Metrics may be incomplete.

docs.title: Removal Approval
docs.text:
Removal requires:

  • Evidence
  • Review
  • Release note
  • Upgrade guidance
  • Fixture retention
  • Explicit PR

docs.title: Legacy Read Retention
docs.text: Compatibility reads may remain longer than write paths.

docs.title: Legacy State Retention
docs.text:
Legacy tables may remain after runtime retirement.

Deletion occurs later.

docs.title: Attribution Preservation
docs.text:
Compatibility and migration must preserve:

  • Tunarr zlib license
  • Notice
  • Git history
  • Attribution documentation
  • Inherited source headers where applicable

docs.title: Testing Strategy

  • Partial failure

  • Caller response

docs.title: Dual-Write Failure Injection

Inject:

  • Failure before canonical commit

  • Failure during legacy write
  • Failure after legacy write

docs.title: Legacy Route Tests

docs.title: Milestone Mission
docs.text:
ChannelForge must own a normalized programming inventory without becoming a live proxy for one media server.

The Media Sources and Catalog milestone must:

  • Preserve provider connectivity
  • Preserve credentials securely
  • Preserve provider identity and provenance
  • Prevent provider IDs from becoming canonical identity
  • Keep provider payloads behind adapter boundaries
  • Normalize Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby observations
  • Support multiple configured servers of the same provider type
  • Support multiple libraries per server
  • Support multiple source copies of one logical title
  • Support multiple playback variants per title
  • Preserve historical references when sources disappear
  • Reconcile deletions safely
  • Avoid destructive synchronization
  • Keep user overrides authoritative
  • Make matching explainable
  • Make merge and split reversible where practical
  • Keep stream URLs out of canonical Catalog state
  • Resolve stream access only at runtime
  • Expose deterministic, stable Catalog queries
  • Produce immutable Catalog Snapshots
  • Support migration from inherited Tunarr program records
  • Keep external calls outside database write transactions
  • Keep synchronization restart-safe
  • Keep one failed source from corrupting unrelated sources
  • Preserve Docker and Unraid deployment assumptions

docs.title: Product Principle
docs.text:
The governing product principle remains:

Build television networks, not playlists.

A network-first scheduling system requires a provider-independent Catalog.

The Catalog represents programmable media.

It does not represent one provider's playlist, library tree, or API payload.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
1. ChannelForge owns canonical Catalog Item identity.
  2. ChannelForge owns Media Source identity.
  3. Provider identifiers are qualified external identities.
  4. Provider payloads do not become domain objects.
  5. Metadata and playback availability are separate.
  6. User overrides remain authoritative.
  7. Synchronization is additive and reconciling.
  8. Historical references survive source deletion.
  9. Final playback URLs are resolved at playout time.
  10. The scheduler reads local normalized state.
  11. Provider failures remain isolated.
  12. Deduplication is explainable.
  13. Merge and split lineage is preserved.
  14. Catalog queries are deterministically ordered.
  15. Catalog Snapshots support reproducible planning.
  16. External calls are bounded and cancelable.
  17. Synchronization is idempotent.
  18. Full reconciliation remains authoritative.
  19. Webhooks are hints.
  20. Provider credentials remain inside restricted boundaries.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Version 1 includes built-in Media Source adapters for:

  • Plex
  • Jellyfin
  • Emby

Version 1 Catalog may represent:

  • Movies
  • Series
  • Seasons
  • Episodes
  • Specials
  • Trailers
  • Music videos
  • Bumpers
  • Idents
  • Advertisements
  • Filler
  • Slates
  • Other media

The first UI may expose a narrower subset.

The domain must not assume all programmable media are movies or episodes.

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
This milestone does not require:

  • Automatic media acquisition
  • Filesystem crawling outside configured adapters
  • Public catalog federation
  • Cloud-hosted catalog
  • Cross-instance universal media IDs
  • Machine-learning matching
  • Final metadata-provider ecosystem
  • DRM circumvention
  • Permanent provider stream URLs
  • Final FFmpeg command construction
  • Final playback session management
  • Final scheduling algorithms
  • Final public release UI
  • Plugin-provided source adapters
  • Music-library scheduling
  • Photo-library scheduling
  • Full person-identity graph
  • Distributed synchronization workers
  • PostgreSQL
  • Removal of every inherited Tunarr program table

docs.title: Current Baseline
docs.text:
The inherited runtime already supports Plex, Jellyfin, and Emby connectivity.

The inherited workspace exposes provider types through shared packages.

The current implementation likely mixes:

  • Provider DTOs
  • Program models
  • Persistence records
  • Scheduling models
  • API contracts
  • Playback details

Milestone 05 must route this behavior through the Media Sources and Catalog module boundaries established in Milestone 02.
