docs.title: Module Boundary Rule
docs.text:
Media Sources produces normalized provider observations.

Catalog consumes observations.

Catalog domain logic does not call Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby directly.

docs.title: Media Source Aggregate
docs.text: A Media Source represents one configured provider instance.

docs.title: Media Source Fields
docs.text:
Required conceptual fields:

mediaSourceId
providerType
displayName
sourceDescriptor
credentialReference
enabledState
trustPolicy
connectionPolicy
synchronizationPolicy
preferredMetadataPriority
playbackPriority
healthState
activeCapabilitySnapshotId
adapterVersion
createdAt
updatedAt
archivedAt
version

docs.title: Provider Type
docs.text:
Initial built-in values:

  • PLEX
  • JELLYFIN
  • EMBY

Future values may include:

  • LOCAL_INDEX
  • GENERIC_HTTP
  • CUSTOM_PLUGIN

Provider type values are stable domain identifiers.

They are not inferred from display name or URL.

docs.title: Media Source Identity
docs.text:
Every Media Source has a ChannelForge-owned mediaSourceId.

Changing any of these does not automatically create a new Media Source:

  • Display name
  • Hostname
  • Port
  • Scheme
  • Credential
  • Internal address
  • External address
  • Metadata priority
  • Playback priority
  • Included libraries

A new Media Source is required when the provider instance should be treated as independently addressable, auditable, and synchronized.

docs.title: Source Identity Verification
docs.text:
A provider adapter should return a provider identity observation.

Possible fields:

  • Provider server identifier
  • Provider machine identifier
  • Product name
  • Server name
  • Provider version
  • Installation identifier
  • Owner identity where safe
  • Account scope
  • Observed timestamp

docs.title: Source Identity Change
docs.text:
A provider identity change may indicate:

  • Server reinstall
  • Wrong URL
  • Restored provider database
  • Reverse-proxy target change
  • Credential switched to different server
  • Provider bug

The operator must not be silently moved to a different provider instance when identity changes materially.

docs.title: Source Identity Conflict
docs.text:
Possible outcomes:

  • Accept identity change
  • Treat as new Media Source
  • Revert configuration
  • Mark conflict
  • Disable synchronization
  • Continue read-only diagnostics

docs.title: Source Descriptor
docs.text:
A Source Descriptor includes:

  • Provider type
  • Internal base URI
  • External base URI where needed
  • Client-facing base URI where needed
  • Credential Reference
  • TLS policy
  • Proxy policy
  • Timeout policy
  • Redirect policy
  • Allowed custom headers
  • Included library IDs
  • Excluded library IDs
  • Source labels
  • Enabled state

docs.title: Address Purposes
docs.text:
A Media Source may require separate addresses for:

  • Server-to-server calls
  • Container-to-host calls
  • Client-visible URLs
  • Reverse-proxy calls
  • Local-LAN calls
  • Remote provider calls

Address purpose must be explicit.

docs.title: Base URI Validation
docs.text:
Validation must include:

  • Allowed scheme
  • Host
  • Port range
  • Path normalization
  • No embedded credentials
  • No fragment where unsupported
  • No unsupported protocol
  • Trusted-host policy
  • Loopback policy
  • Link-local policy
  • Metadata-service address protection
  • Redirect policy
  • DNS rebinding policy
  • Credential forwarding policy

docs.title: Local Deployment Policy
docs.text: ChannelForge must support ordinary local deployment without requiring a reverse proxy.

docs.title: TLS Policy
docs.text:
Supported policy may include:

  • Standard validation
  • Custom trust store
  • Explicit self-signed trust
  • Certificate pinning
  • Source-scoped insecure mode

docs.title: Insecure TLS Mode
docs.text:
Insecure mode must:

  • Be disabled by default
  • Be source-specific
  • Display a warning
  • Be audited
  • Never apply globally
  • Never disable unrelated provider security

docs.title: Proxy Policy
docs.text:
A Source may use:

  • Direct connection
  • Instance proxy
  • Source-specific proxy
  • No proxy for local addresses

Proxy credentials are secret material.

docs.title: Redirect Policy
docs.text:
Adapters define:

  • Maximum redirects
  • Cross-host redirects
  • Scheme downgrade
  • Credential forwarding
  • Signed URL behavior

Authorization headers must not be forwarded to unrelated hosts.

docs.title: Credential Reference
docs.text:
Media Source records store a Credential Reference.

They do not store decrypted secret material.

docs.title: Provider Credential Types
docs.text:
Possible types:

  • API token
  • Access token
  • Username and password
  • Device authorization result
  • Refresh credential
  • Client certificate
  • Custom header secret

Version 1 should prefer provider-issued tokens over reusable passwords.

docs.title: Credential Access
docs.text: An adapter receives secret material only for the duration of the provider operation.

docs.title: Credential Prohibitions
docs.text:
Secrets must not be:

  • Stored in Catalog tables
  • Returned through ordinary API responses
  • Included in Schedule Plans
  • Included in XMLTV
  • Included in ordinary M3U
  • Logged
  • Embedded in exceptions
  • Embedded in audit notes
  • Included in support bundles without redaction
  • Included in provider-neutral observations
  • Included in search indexes

docs.title: Credential Rotation
docs.text:
Rotation must:

  1. Store new secret material atomically.
  2. Preserve Media Source ID.
  3. Increment credential version.
  4. Run connection verification.
  5. Recalculate source health.
  6. Record audit.
  7. Avoid deleting Catalog state on transient failure.
  8. Retain rollback according to secret policy.
  9. Invalidate old HTTP clients.
  10. Avoid exposing old or new secret.

docs.title: Credential Revocation
docs.text:
Revocation:

  • Blocks new provider operations
  • Marks authentication state
  • Preserves Catalog state
  • Preserves approved plans
  • Preserves history
  • May permit bounded cached runtime access only if policy explicitly allows it

docs.title: Media Source Lifecycle
docs.text:
Suggested states:

  • UNCONFIGURED
  • UNVERIFIED
  • AVAILABLE
  • DEGRADED
  • UNAVAILABLE
  • AUTHENTICATION_FAILED
  • DISABLED
  • ARCHIVED
  • CONFLICT

docs.title: Source Activation
docs.text:
A Media Source becomes active only after:

  • Configuration validates
  • Provider identity resolves
  • Credential validates
  • Adapter supports provider version
  • At least one supported library exists or source purpose is explicit
  • No blocking identity conflict exists
  • Required security policy passes

docs.title: Source Disable
docs.text:
Disabling a Media Source:

  • Stops new synchronization
  • Stops new runtime selection
  • Preserves Catalog Items
  • Preserves Source Bindings
  • Preserves history
  • Recalculates availability
  • May mark future plans stale
  • Does not delete credentials automatically

docs.title: Source Archive
docs.text:
Archiving:

  • Disables source
  • Preserves identity
  • Preserves Source Bindings
  • Preserves history
  • Hides source from ordinary lists
  • Requires explicit restoration
  • Does not hard-delete credentials until retention policy permits

docs.title: Connection Setup Workflow
docs.text:
1. Select provider type.
  2. Enter address.
  3. Provide or authorize credential.
  4. Validate address.
  5. Run connection probe.
  6. Display provider identity.
  7. Run capability discovery.
  8. Discover libraries.
  9. Select libraries.
  10. Save source configuration.
  11. Queue initial synchronization.
  12. Establish health state.

docs.title: Connection Test
docs.text:
Connection Test must not mutate the Catalog.

It may persist:

  • Test timestamp
  • Reachability
  • Authentication result
  • Provider identity
  • Provider version
  • Capability observation
  • Latency
  • TLS observation
  • Warning
  • Error classification

docs.title: Adapter Registry
docs.text: The Adapter Registry maps provider type and adapter version to an implementation.

docs.title: Adapter Registration
docs.text:
Each registration includes:

  • Provider type
  • Adapter version
  • Supported ports
  • Configuration schema
  • Capability declarations
  • Provider-version range
  • Fixture version
  • Migration support
  • Deprecation state
  • Health-check support
  • Playback-resolution support
  • Webhook support

docs.title: Unknown Adapter
docs.text: An unknown provider type or adapter version cannot be activated.

docs.title: Adapter Version
docs.text: Adapter version changes when behavior affecting normalized observations changes.

docs.title: Adapter Upgrade
docs.text:
An adapter upgrade may trigger:

  • Capability refresh
  • Full synchronization
  • Observation reparse
  • Search projection rebuild
  • Conflict review
  • Catalog revision change
  • Migration

docs.title: Adapter Ports
docs.text:
Core ports include:

ConnectionProbePort
ProviderIdentityPort
CapabilityDiscoveryPort
LibraryDiscoveryPort
CatalogEnumerationPort
CatalogItemDetailPort
ArtworkAccessPort
PlaybackResolutionPort
ChangeFeedPort
WebhookVerificationPort
ProviderHealthPort

An adapter implements only supported ports.

docs.title: Connection Probe Port
docs.text:
Input:

  • Source Descriptor
  • Credential Reference
  • Timeout
  • Cancellation
  • Correlation ID

Output:

  • Reachability
  • Authentication result
  • Provider identity
  • Provider version
  • Server time
  • Latency
  • TLS observation
  • Warnings
  • Error classification

docs.title: Capability Discovery Port
docs.text:
Returns a normalized Capability Snapshot.

Potential capability values:

  • Library enumeration
  • Incremental updates
  • Webhooks
  • Artwork access
  • Direct stream
  • Provider transcode
  • Byte ranges
  • Offset seek
  • Multiple media parts
  • Multiple versions
  • Audio selection
  • Subtitle selection
  • User-scoped visibility
  • Deletion events
  • Update tokens
  • Item version tokens
  • Remote access
  • Local path exposure

docs.title: Capability State
docs.text:
Values:

  • SUPPORTED
  • UNSUPPORTED
  • UNKNOWN
  • DEGRADED
  • REQUIRES_CONFIGURATION

docs.title: Capability Snapshot
docs.text:
Fields:

capabilitySnapshotId
mediaSourceId
adapterVersion
providerVersion
observedAt
capabilities
confidence
warnings
expiresAt
contentChecksum

Capabilities are observations.

They are not permanent provider assumptions.

docs.title: Library Discovery Port
docs.text: Returns normalized Library Descriptors.

docs.title: Library Descriptor
docs.text:
Fields:

  • External library ID
  • Name
  • Library type
  • Included media kinds
  • Item count estimate
  • Enabled or hidden state
  • Provider update timestamp
  • Parent scope
  • Access state
  • Provider metadata
  • Warning list

docs.title: Normalized Library Types
docs.text:
• MOVIES
  • TV
  • MIXED
  • MUSIC
  • PHOTOS
  • OTHER

Version 1 Catalog import may exclude unsupported library types.

Unsupported libraries should remain visible for diagnostics where practical.

docs.title: Library Binding
docs.text:
A Library Binding records operator inclusion and synchronization policy.

Fields:

libraryBindingId
mediaSourceId
externalLibraryId
libraryType
displayName
inclusionState
synchronizationPolicy
importFilters
lastDiscoveredAt
lastSynchronizedAt
archivedAt
version

docs.title: Library Inclusion State
docs.text:
• PENDING_REVIEW
  • INCLUDED
  • EXCLUDED
  • UNSUPPORTED
  • MISSING
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Library Inclusion
docs.text:
Library inclusion is explicit.

A newly discovered library defaults according to instance policy.

Changing inclusion queues synchronization and recalculates availability.

docs.title: Library Removal
docs.text:
A missing library:

  • Is not deleted immediately
  • Enters grace state
  • Preserves Source Bindings
  • Preserves Catalog history
  • Creates source health finding
  • May mark future plans stale

docs.title: Path Mapping
docs.text: Path mapping translates provider paths to ChannelForge-accessible paths where direct file access is permitted.

docs.title: Path Mapping Fields
docs.text:
• Media Source ID
  • Provider path prefix
  • ChannelForge path prefix
  • Platform
  • Case policy
  • Separator policy
  • Priority
  • Enabled state
  • Validation state
  • Last verified
  • Notes

docs.title: Path Mapping Invariants
docs.text:
• Mapping is source-scoped
  • Mapping does not escape approved roots
  • Mapping preserves relative suffix
  • Most specific matching prefix wins
  • Ordering is deterministic
  • Mapping is validated on Windows and Linux
  • Provider path remains preserved
  • Failed mapping does not delete variant
  • Direct path is not required for provider-mediated playback

docs.title: Path Mapping Security
docs.text:
Prevent:

  • Directory traversal
  • Unapproved host paths
  • Secret paths in API
  • Writable media mount assumption
  • Symlink escape
  • Case-fold collision
  • UNC misuse
  • Container-host confusion

docs.title: Provider-Neutral Observation
docs.text:
Adapters emit normalized observations.

They do not emit provider DTOs to Catalog.

docs.title: Source Item Observation
docs.text:
Conceptual fields:

mediaSourceId
adapterVersion
providerVersion
externalLibraryId
externalItemType
externalItemId
externalParentIds
sourceVersionToken
observedAt
fieldObservations
artworkObservations
playbackVariantObservations
warnings
rawPayloadReference

docs.title: Field Observation
docs.text:
Fields:

  • Field name
  • Raw value
  • Normalized candidate
  • Source field
  • Locale
  • Precision
  • Confidence
  • Warning
  • Observed timestamp

docs.title: Observation Invariants
docs.text:
• External identity is qualified
  • Source values are preserved
  • Invalid values are recorded as warnings
  • Secrets are absent
  • Output is deterministic for the same provider payload and adapter version
  • Provider-specific semantics stay inside adapter
  • Observation schema is versioned

docs.title: Provider Error
docs.text: Adapters translate failures into stable categories.

docs.title: Error Categories
docs.text:
• INVALID_CONFIGURATION
  • AUTHENTICATION_FAILED
  • AUTHORIZATION_FAILED
  • NOT_FOUND
  • TIMEOUT
  • RATE_LIMITED
  • PROVIDER_UNAVAILABLE
  • UNSUPPORTED_PROVIDER_VERSION
  • INVALID_RESPONSE
  • PARTIAL_RESPONSE
  • CONNECTION_RESET
  • TLS_FAILED
  • CANCELLED
  • UNKNOWN

docs.title: Retryability
docs.text:
Retryability is explicit.

Likely retryable:

  • Timeout
  • Temporary unavailable
  • Rate limit
  • Connection reset
  • Selected server error
  • Transient cursor failure

Likely non-retryable:

  • Invalid configuration
  • Authentication failure
  • Authorization failure
  • Unsupported provider version
  • Invalid permanent ID
  • Explicit item not found

docs.title: Timeout Policy
docs.text:
Timeout classes:

  • Connection timeout
  • Request timeout
  • Streaming response timeout
  • Idle read timeout
  • Operation budget

Large synchronization must not use one unbounded request.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
Every job-bound external operation accepts cancellation.

Cancellation must:

  • Stop pagination
  • Close response bodies
  • Release sockets
  • Preserve completed checkpoints
  • Mark job state
  • Avoid Catalog corruption

docs.title: Retry Policy
docs.text:
Fields:

  • Maximum attempts
  • Initial delay
  • Maximum delay
  • Backoff
  • Jitter
  • Retryable categories
  • Rate-limit policy
  • Operation budget
  • Cancellation

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Per-source rate-limit handling may use:

  • Provider Retry-After
  • Quota reset
  • Remaining request count
  • Adapter defaults
  • ChannelForge limiter

docs.title: Request Concurrency
docs.text:
Per-source concurrency is bounded.

Separate limits may apply to:

  • Catalog listing
  • Item detail
  • Artwork
  • Playback resolution
  • Health
  • Webhook verification

docs.title: HTTP Client Boundary
docs.text:
Adapters use a controlled HTTP client abstraction supporting:

  • Timeouts
  • Cancellation
  • Redaction
  • Correlation IDs
  • Retry hooks
  • Metrics
  • TLS policy
  • Proxy policy
  • Response-size limits
  • Streaming
  • Test substitution

docs.title: Response Size Limits
docs.text:
Bound:

  • Metadata responses
  • Error bodies
  • Artwork
  • Webhooks
  • Pagination pages

docs.title: Catalog Aggregate
docs.text:
Catalog Item is the principal Catalog aggregate root.

It represents one logical programmable unit.

docs.title: Catalog Item Fields
docs.text:
Conceptual fields:

catalogItemId
mediaKind
canonicalTitle
sortTitle
originalTitle
alternateTitles
summary
longDescription
tagline
releaseDate
releaseYear
originalAirDate
durationMs
contentRating
genres
tags
languages
countries
studios
credits
seriesId
seasonId
seasonNumber
episodeNumber
absoluteEpisodeNumber
availabilityState
metadataCompletenessState
artworkState
contentRevision
createdAt
updatedAt
archivedAt

Fields that do not apply remain absent.

They are not fabricated.

docs.title: Catalog Item Identity
docs.text:
Every Catalog Item has a ChannelForge-owned catalogItemId.

It remains stable through:

  • Title correction
  • Metadata correction
  • Source URL change
  • Source server change
  • Library move
  • Path change
  • Encoding replacement
  • Artwork change
  • Source archival
  • Provider migration

docs.title: Identity Is Not Title
docs.text: Title changes do not create new Catalog Items automatically.

docs.title: Identity Is Not Provider Location
docs.text: Provider path, URL, library, and media-part location are Source Binding or Playback Variant concerns.

docs.title: Media Kind
docs.text:
Initial values:

  • MOVIE
  • SERIES
  • SEASON
  • EPISODE
  • SPECIAL
  • TRAILER
  • MUSIC_VIDEO
  • BUMPER
  • IDENT
  • ADVERTISEMENT
  • FILLER
  • SLATE
  • OTHER

docs.title: Media Kind Change
docs.text:
A kind change may require:

  • Hierarchy validation
  • Scheduling eligibility recalculation
  • Source Binding review
  • Conflict
  • Audit
  • Catalog revision change

A kind change must not rewrite approved historical Schedule Entries.

docs.title: Catalog Hierarchy
docs.text:
Normal episodic hierarchy:

Series
  -> Season
    -> Episode

docs.title: Hierarchy Rules
docs.text:
• Season belongs to one Series
  • Episode belongs to one Series
  • Episode may belong to one Season
  • Special may belong to a Series without ordinary Season
  • Movie requires no Series
  • Presentation media requires no episodic hierarchy
  • Hierarchy uses ChannelForge IDs
  • Provider parent IDs remain in Source Bindings or observations

docs.title: Hierarchy State
docs.text:
• RESOLVED
  • PENDING_PARENT
  • CONFLICT
  • ORPHANED
  • MANUALLY_ASSIGNED

docs.title: Missing Parent
docs.text:
Missing parent records:

  • Do not fabricate identity
  • Create warning
  • May create placeholder parent if policy explicitly permits
  • Exclude item from ordered series scheduling where unsafe
  • Remain eligible for standalone programming if policy permits

docs.title: Hierarchy Correction
docs.text:
Correction:

  • Preserves Catalog Item ID where possible
  • Records previous relationship
  • Updates progression indexes
  • Marks dependent draft plans stale
  • Does not mutate approved Schedule Entries

docs.title: Canonical Title
docs.text:
Default precedence:

  1. User override
  2. Accepted manual resolution
  3. ChannelForge normalized decision
  4. Preferred metadata provider
  5. Preferred Media Source
  6. Other Media Source
  7. Generated placeholder

docs.title: Sort Title
docs.text:
Sort Title:

  • Supports deterministic ordering
  • May remove leading articles
  • May normalize punctuation
  • May be locale-aware
  • May be overridden
  • Is not identity

docs.title: Original Title
docs.text: Preserves original-language title where known.

docs.title: Alternate Titles
docs.text:
Records:

  • Value
  • Locale
  • Type
  • Provenance
  • Confidence
  • Active state

docs.title: Description Model
docs.text:
Fields:

  • Summary
  • Long description
  • Tagline

Generated text must be identified as generated or derived.

docs.title: Date Model
docs.text:
Possible fields:

  • Release date
  • Original air date
  • Digital release date
  • Physical release date
  • Year-only fallback

Partial precision must be retained.

docs.title: Duration
docs.text: Duration is scheduling-critical.

docs.title: Duration Sources
docs.text:
Potential sources:

  • Provider item duration
  • Playback Variant duration
  • Measured probe duration
  • User override
  • Imported legacy duration

docs.title: Duration Precedence
docs.text:
Recommended:

  1. User override
  2. Verified measured duration
  3. Preferred available Playback Variant
  4. Trusted provider duration
  5. Migrated legacy duration
  6. Unknown

docs.title: Duration Conflict
docs.text:
A material duration mismatch creates:

  • Warning
  • Conflict when above tolerance
  • Availability or playout preflight impact
  • Catalog revision change
  • Possible plan staleness

docs.title: Duration Precision
docs.text: Store integer milliseconds unless stronger precision is proven necessary.

docs.title: Rating Model
docs.text:
Content ratings should preserve:

  • Rating system
  • Region
  • Value
  • Source
  • Unrated state
  • Unknown state

Missing rating does not mean unrestricted.

docs.title: Genre and Tag Model
docs.text:
Provider labels are preserved.

Canonical genres and tags may map provider values.

Mappings are:

  • Versioned
  • Reversible
  • Auditable
  • Non-destructive

docs.title: Credits
docs.text:
Credits may include:

  • Name
  • Role
  • Character
  • Billing order
  • Source
  • External person ID
  • Provenance

Version 1 does not require a full person graph.

docs.title: Studio and Network Metadata
docs.text:
Original broadcast network metadata remains descriptive Catalog metadata.

It is not a ChannelForge Network entity.

docs.title: Language
docs.text:
Use standard language tags where practical.

Preserve unknown raw source values.

docs.title: Country
docs.text:
Use stable normalized codes where practical.

Do not infer country solely from language.

docs.title: Source Binding
docs.text: A Source Binding connects one Catalog Item to one item on one Media Source.

docs.title: Source Binding Fields
docs.text:
sourceBindingId
catalogItemId
mediaSourceId
externalItemType
externalItemId
externalLibraryId
externalParentIds
externalPathOrKey
externalVersionToken
sourceMetadataChecksum
sourceAvailabilityState
firstSeenAt
lastSeenAt
lastSynchronizedAt
missingSince
archivedAt
matchState
matchConfidence
matchDecisionId

docs.title: Source Binding Unique Identity
docs.text:
Default uniqueness:

mediaSourceId
+ externalItemType
+ externalItemId

Library scope may be included when provider semantics require it.

docs.title: External ID Reuse
docs.text:
Provider reuse of an external ID for a different item creates a conflict.

It must not silently replace the prior binding.

docs.title: Source Binding States
docs.text:
• ACTIVE
  • MISSING
  • UNAVAILABLE
  • DISABLED
  • CONFLICT
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Source Binding Match State
docs.text:
• NEW
  • AUTO_MATCHED
  • MANUALLY_MATCHED
  • MANUALLY_CREATED
  • REVIEW_REQUIRED
  • REJECTED_MATCH
  • SPLIT
  • MERGED

docs.title: Source Snapshot
docs.text:
A synchronization may retain a normalized Source Snapshot.

Fields:

  • Source Binding ID
  • Adapter version
  • Provider version
  • Raw payload reference
  • Normalized payload reference
  • Payload checksum
  • Observed timestamp
  • Parse warnings
  • Field observations
  • Parent relationships
  • Playback observations

Raw payload retention is bounded.

Normalized provenance required for decisions remains available.

docs.title: Playback Variant
docs.text: A Playback Variant represents one playable realization through one Source Binding.

docs.title: Playback Variant Fields
docs.text:
playbackVariantId
sourceBindingId
externalMediaPartId
container
videoCodec
audioCodecs
subtitleCodecs
width
height
aspectRatio
frameRate
scanType
bitRate
hdrFormat
colorCharacteristics
audioChannelCount
audioTracks
subtitleTracks
durationMs
fileSize
sourcePathOrKey
directPlayObservations
directStreamObservations
transcodeObservations
availabilityState
lastVerifiedAt
variantVersionToken

docs.title: Playback Variant Identity
docs.text:
A variant remains stable while the provider treats it as the same media part.

Replacing the underlying file may:

  • Update variant
  • Create new variant
  • Archive old variant
  • Trigger duration reevaluation
  • Trigger capability reevaluation

docs.title: Playback Variant States
docs.text:
• AVAILABLE
  • UNVERIFIED
  • MISSING
  • UNPLAYABLE
  • DISABLED
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Capability Observation
docs.text:
A Playback capability observation may include:

  • Output profile
  • Direct play
  • Direct stream
  • Transcode required
  • Container compatibility
  • Codec compatibility
  • Bit-rate compatibility
  • Subtitle burn requirement
  • Observed timestamp
  • Source version
  • ChannelForge version

Final runtime decision occurs in Playout.

docs.title: Stream URL Rule
docs.text:
Permanent provider stream URLs are not canonical Playback Variant identity.

Short-lived URLs may be cached only with:

  • Expiration
  • Source Binding reference
  • Security controls
  • Redaction
  • Runtime-cache classification

docs.title: Availability
docs.text: Catalog Item availability is derived.

docs.title: Catalog Availability States
docs.text:
• AVAILABLE
  • PARTIALLY_AVAILABLE
  • UNAVAILABLE
  • UNKNOWN
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Available
docs.text: At least one eligible Source Binding has at least one usable Playback Variant.

docs.title: Partially Available
docs.text: At least one usable option remains, but one or more expected bindings or variants are unavailable.

docs.title: Unavailable
docs.text: No eligible usable Playback Variant remains.

docs.title: Unknown
docs.text: Availability is unverified or synchronization is incomplete.

docs.title: Archived
docs.text: Item remains historical but is excluded from ordinary programming.

docs.title: Availability Inputs
docs.text:
• Media Source enabled state
  • Source health
  • Library inclusion
  • Source Binding state
  • Playback Variant state
  • Manual exclusion
  • Output-profile requirements
  • Verification age
  • Local-path requirement
  • Codec or container requirement

docs.title: Availability Change
docs.text:
When availability changes:

  • Recalculate Catalog Item
  • Increment scheduling-relevant Catalog revision
  • Emit event
  • Affect future plans
  • Mark dependent draft plans stale
  • Do not mutate approved plans
  • Permit Playout to choose alternate variant
  • Recalculate health findings

docs.title: Metadata Provenance
docs.text: Every effective field must be explainable.

docs.title: Provenance Types
docs.text:
• USER_OVERRIDE
  • SOURCE
  • METADATA_PROVIDER
  • DERIVED
  • MIGRATED
  • PACK_IMPORT
  • SYSTEM_DEFAULT

docs.title: Provenance Fields
docs.text:
provenanceId
catalogItemId
fieldName
valueReference
provenanceType
sourceEntity
sourceField
observedAt
confidence
precedence
acceptedState
supersededAt
decisionId

docs.title: Default Metadata Precedence
docs.text:
1. User override
  2. Accepted manual resolution
  3. ChannelForge normalized decision
  4. Preferred metadata provider
  5. Preferred Media Source
  6. Other Media Sources
  7. Derived value
  8. System fallback

Precedence may differ by field.

docs.title: Field-Specific Precedence
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Duration may prefer measured variant
  • Artwork may prefer user upload
  • Rating may prefer regional provider
  • Episode order may prefer configured order source
  • Summary may preserve local provider edits

docs.title: User Override
docs.text:
A user override records:

  • Target field or relationship
  • Prior effective value
  • New value
  • Actor
  • Timestamp
  • Note
  • Active state

Synchronization cannot overwrite an active user override.

docs.title: Override Removal
docs.text: Removing an override recalculates effective value from remaining provenance.

docs.title: Normalization Pipeline
docs.text:
Canonical sequence:

1. Fetch source records
2. Parse provider payload
3. Validate source identity
4. Emit provider-neutral observations
5. Normalize field candidates
6. Resolve hierarchy
7. Resolve or create Catalog Item identity
8. Upsert Source Binding
9. Upsert Playback Variants
10. Recalculate effective metadata
11. Recalculate availability
12. Detect conflicts
13. Commit bounded transaction
14. Emit events after commit
15. Update projections
16. Advance checkpoint

docs.title: Normalization Requirements
docs.text:
Normalization is:

  • Deterministic
  • Versioned
  • Idempotent
  • Source-aware
  • Locale-aware where required
  • Non-destructive
  • Explainable
  • Safe under partial data
  • Testable from fixtures

docs.title: Normalization Version
docs.text:
A normalization version identifies behavior affecting canonical output.

A version change may require:

  • Reprocessing observations
  • Catalog revision change
  • Conflict review
  • Search rebuild
  • Snapshot invalidation
  • Migration

docs.title: Text Normalization
docs.text:
May include:

  • Unicode normalization
  • Whitespace normalization
  • Control-character removal
  • Safe HTML stripping
  • Punctuation normalization
  • Search case folding

Original source value remains preserved.

docs.title: Date Normalization
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Parsed value
  • Precision
  • Time zone when supplied
  • Source
  • Raw value
  • Warning

Invalid dates remain raw observations and do not become effective normalized values.

docs.title: Numeric Normalization
docs.text:
Define:

  • Unit
  • Rounding
  • Precision
  • Range
  • Missing versus zero
  • Overflow
  • Warning

docs.title: Identifier Normalization
docs.text:
External IDs remain strings unless adapter guarantees other stable semantics.

Do not remove leading zeros or change case without provider-specific proof.

docs.title: Matching
docs.text: Matching decides whether a Source Item Observation attaches to an existing Catalog Item or creates a new item.

docs.title: Match Inputs
docs.text:
Potential signals:

  • Provider metadata IDs
  • Title
  • Original title
  • Alternate title
  • Release year
  • Exact date
  • Media kind
  • Series hierarchy
  • Season and episode numbers
  • Duration
  • Edition
  • Library context
  • Existing operator decision
  • Legacy mapping
  • File fingerprint where available

docs.title: Match Outputs
docs.text:
• Existing Catalog Item
  • New Catalog Item
  • Review required
  • Conflict
  • Rejected match
  • Distinct edition

docs.title: Match Decision
docs.text:
A Match Decision records:

  • Candidate IDs
  • Evidence
  • Algorithm version
  • Confidence
  • Threshold
  • Decision
  • Actor or automatic policy
  • Timestamp
  • Reversibility
  • Conflict reference

docs.title: Automatic Match
docs.text: Automatic match is allowed only above configured confidence and when no blocking ambiguity exists.

docs.title: Manual Match
docs.text:
Manual match requires:

  • Source item
  • Candidate preview
  • Evidence
  • Conflict check
  • Actor confirmation
  • Audit

docs.title: Matching Prohibitions
docs.text:
Do not match solely by:

  • Title
  • Provider row number
  • File name
  • Library position
  • Database order
  • First search result
  • Unqualified external ID

docs.title: Deduplication
docs.text: Deduplication is explainable and reversible where practical.

docs.title: Duplicate Candidate
docs.text:
A duplicate candidate is not a duplicate fact.

It requires evidence and state.

docs.title: Duplicate Candidate States
docs.text:
• PROPOSED
  • AUTO_ACCEPTED
  • REVIEW_REQUIRED
  • ACCEPTED
  • REJECTED
  • SUPERSEDED

docs.title: Merge
docs.text:
A merge:

  • Chooses surviving Catalog Item ID
  • Preserves merged IDs as aliases or tombstones
  • Reassigns eligible Source Bindings
  • Reassigns provenance
  • Preserves audit
  • Preserves schedule references
  • Records reason
  • Creates lineage
  • Detects binding collision

docs.title: Merge Invariants
docs.text:
• One surviving ID
  • No duplicate active Source Binding
  • Historical Schedule Entry remains interpretable
  • User overrides are reviewed
  • Hierarchy remains valid
  • Collections update deterministically
  • Search index rebuilds
  • Catalog revision increments

docs.title: Split
docs.text:
A split:

  • Preserves original lineage
  • Creates one or more new Catalog Items
  • Reassigns Source Bindings
  • Copies or reassigns metadata deliberately
  • Preserves historical references
  • Records actor and reason
  • Updates conflicts
  • Updates projections

docs.title: Split Invariants
docs.text:
• Every active binding has one target
  • Historical approved schedule is not silently rewritten
  • New IDs are stable
  • Mapping remains auditable
  • Hierarchy is validated
  • Availability recalculates

docs.title: Catalog Conflict
docs.text:
Conflict types may include:

  • External ID reuse
  • Ambiguous match
  • Hierarchy conflict
  • Duration mismatch
  • Media-kind mismatch
  • Provider identity mismatch
  • Binding collision
  • Metadata disagreement
  • Edition ambiguity
  • Missing parent
  • Merge collision
  • Split ambiguity

docs.title: Catalog Conflict State
docs.text:
• OPEN
  • AUTO_RESOLVED
  • OPERATOR_RESOLVED
  • DISMISSED
  • SUPERSEDED

docs.title: Conflict Resolution Actions
docs.text:
• Accept match
  • Create new Catalog Item
  • Merge
  • Split
  • Reassign Source Binding
  • Override field
  • Prefer source
  • Archive binding
  • Mark distinct edition
  • Defer
  • Dismiss false positive

Every action is audited.

docs.title: Artwork
docs.text:
Catalog artwork describes media.

It is distinct from Network or Channel presentation assets.

docs.title: Artwork Types
docs.text:
• Poster
  • Background
  • Banner
  • Logo
  • Thumbnail
  • Episode still
  • Square image
  • Clear logo
  • Icon
  • Guide image

docs.title: Artwork Fields
docs.text:
artworkId
catalogItemId
artworkType
source
sourceUrlOrKey
managedStorageReference
mimeType
width
height
fileSize
checksum
locale
suitability
preferredState
validationState
firstSeenAt
lastVerifiedAt
archivedAt

docs.title: Artwork States
docs.text:
• REMOTE
  • CACHED
  • MANAGED
  • MISSING
  • INVALID
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Artwork Selection
docs.text:
Stable precedence:

  1. User-selected
  2. Network or Channel override where applicable
  3. Preferred metadata provider
  4. Preferred Media Source
  5. Best validated dimensions
  6. Locale
  7. Stable ID tie-break

docs.title: Artwork Caching
docs.text:
Artwork may be:

  • Proxied
  • Cached
  • Imported into managed storage
  • Referenced remotely

docs.title: Artwork Security
docs.text: Provider credentials must not appear in public artwork URLs.

docs.title: Artwork Validation
docs.text:
Validate:

  • MIME
  • File signature
  • Dimensions
  • Maximum size
  • Corruption
  • Path safety
  • Animation policy
  • Checksum

docs.title: Custom Collections
docs.text: A Custom Collection groups Catalog Items for programming.

docs.title: Collection Fields
docs.text:
collectionId
name
description
owner
membershipMode
staticMembers
dynamicSelector
includeOverrides
excludeOverrides
sortPolicy
createdAt
updatedAt
archivedAt
version

docs.title: Membership Modes
docs.text:
• STATIC
  • DYNAMIC
  • HYBRID

docs.title: Collection Invariants
docs.text:
• Members use Catalog Item IDs
  • Provider collection IDs are not canonical
  • Dynamic evaluation is deterministic for a Catalog Snapshot
  • Historical snapshots retain archived members
  • Collection changes increment Catalog revision
  • Dependent draft plans may become stale

docs.title: Catalog Labels
docs.text:
Labels support programming-specific classification.

Examples:

  • Holiday
  • Family
  • Late-night
  • Comfort
  • Premiere
  • Classic
  • Local
  • Original
  • Short-form
  • High-priority

docs.title: Label Assignment
docs.text:
Records:

  • Catalog Item ID
  • Label ID
  • Provenance
  • Effective date range
  • Created timestamp
  • Removed timestamp

docs.title: Franchise Relationships
docs.text:
Franchise groups related works.

It does not imply Series hierarchy.

docs.title: Franchise Uses
docs.text:
• Repeat spacing
  • Themed blocks
  • Sequel ordering
  • Spin-offs
  • Shared-universe blocks

docs.title: Synchronization
docs.text: Synchronization converts provider observations into Catalog state.

docs.title: Synchronization Types
docs.text:
• Full
  • Incremental
  • Targeted item
  • Library-scoped
  • Metadata refresh
  • Artwork refresh
  • Playback-variant refresh
  • Reconciliation
  • Migration import

docs.title: Synchronization Run
docs.text:
Fields:

synchronizationRunId
mediaSourceId
mode
state
adapterVersion
providerVersion
normalizationVersion
startedAt
completedAt
cursor
checkpoint
observedCount
createdCount
updatedCount
unchangedCount
missingCount
conflictCount
warningCount
failureCount

docs.title: Synchronization State
docs.text:
• QUEUED
  • CONNECTING
  • DISCOVERING
  • ENUMERATING
  • NORMALIZING
  • COMMITTING
  • RECONCILING
  • COMPLETED
  • COMPLETED_WITH_WARNINGS
  • PAUSED
  • CANCELLED
  • FAILED

docs.title: Full Synchronization
docs.text: Full synchronization enumerates all included libraries.

docs.title: Full Synchronization Sequence
docs.text:
1. Create run.
  2. Resolve adapter.
  3. Resolve secret.
  4. Probe source when required.
  5. Capture capability snapshot.
  6. Enumerate included libraries.
  7. Enumerate items with stable pagination.
  8. Normalize observations.
  9. Stage bounded batch.
  10. Commit Catalog changes.
  11. Mark observed bindings.
  12. Advance checkpoint.
  13. Identify active bindings not observed.
  14. Enter missing grace state.
  15. Recalculate availability.
  16. Detect conflicts.
  17. Update search projection.
  18. Update Catalog revision.
  19. Emit events.
  20. Complete run.

docs.title: Full Reconciliation Authority
docs.text:
Full reconciliation remains authoritative for detecting absence.

Incremental hints do not permanently replace it.

docs.title: Incremental Synchronization
docs.text:
Incremental synchronization may use:

  • Provider cursor
  • Update timestamp
  • Item version token
  • Webhook hint
  • Library change token
  • Provider event feed

docs.title: Incremental Rules
docs.text:
• Cursor is provider-specific and opaque
  • Cursor is scoped to Media Source and adapter version
  • Cursor commits after corresponding Catalog transaction
  • Cursor failure does not delete unseen items
  • Cursor reset triggers full reconciliation
  • Provider omission is not deletion unless contract proves it
  • Incremental state is restart-safe

docs.title: Webhook Hint
docs.text:
A webhook is a hint.

It may queue:

  • Targeted refresh
  • Library refresh
  • Full reconciliation
  • Health check

A webhook does not directly mutate canonical Catalog state.

docs.title: Webhook Requirements
docs.text:
• Verify source
  • Bound payload
  • Deduplicate
  • Record event ID
  • Return quickly
  • Queue job
  • Re-read provider state
  • Avoid trusting payload as authoritative
  • Rate limit

docs.title: Bounded Batches
docs.text: Synchronization writes bounded batches.

docs.title: Batch Sequence
docs.text:
1. Fetch outside transaction.
  2. Normalize outside transaction where practical.
  3. Begin transaction.
  4. Upsert Catalog Items.
  5. Upsert Source Bindings.
  6. Upsert Playback Variants.
  7. Write provenance.
  8. Write conflicts.
  9. Update checkpoint.
  10. Commit.
  11. Emit progress.
  12. Continue.

docs.title: Transaction Rules
docs.text:
• No provider call inside write transaction
  • No artwork download inside Catalog write transaction
  • No FFmpeg probe inside provider-call transaction
  • Lock duration bounded
  • Checkpoint corresponds to committed batch
  • Failure preserves prior committed batches
  • Retry is idempotent

docs.title: Missing Detection
docs.text: A Source Binding not observed during full synchronization does not become archived immediately.

docs.title: Missing Grace Period
docs.text:
A binding progresses:

ACTIVE
-> MISSING
-> UNAVAILABLE
-> ARCHIVED

according to policy and repeated reconciliation.

docs.title: Missing Detection Inputs
docs.text:
• Full synchronization completed
  • Library remained included
  • Provider query covered relevant scope
  • Provider identity unchanged
  • No partial-response warning
  • No cancellation
  • No cursor ambiguity

docs.title: Partial Enumeration
docs.text: A partial enumeration must not mark unseen items missing.

docs.title: Source Deletion
docs.text:
A provider deletion hint may:

  • Queue targeted verification
  • Mark candidate missing
  • Preserve prior metadata
  • Preserve historical references
  • Await reconciliation according to policy

docs.title: Synchronization Failure Isolation
docs.text: One malformed item should not fail the full run unless continuing is unsafe.

docs.title: Item Failure
docs.text:
Record:

  • Source item identity
  • Error category
  • Adapter version
  • Raw payload reference
  • Warning
  • Retryability
  • Count
  • Last occurrence

docs.title: Source-Level Failure
docs.text:
Source-level failure:

  • Does not mutate unrelated Media Sources
  • Does not delete Catalog state
  • Updates source health
  • Preserves approved plans
  • Leaves prior Catalog state inspectable
  • Schedules retry according to policy

docs.title: Synchronization Idempotency
docs.text: Reprocessing the same observation set and versions must not duplicate effective state.

docs.title: Idempotency Mechanisms
docs.text:
• Source Binding unique constraint
  • Playback Variant identity
  • Observation checksum
  • Match Decision lookup
  • Run checkpoint
  • Upsert with expected version
  • Provenance deduplication
  • Conflict deduplication

docs.title: Synchronization Cancellation
docs.text:
Cancellation:

  • Stops pagination
  • Stops new provider requests
  • Completes or rolls back current transaction
  • Persists checkpoint
  • Marks run canceled
  • Preserves committed Catalog state
  • Does not mark unseen items missing

docs.title: Synchronization Retry
docs.text:
Retry behavior:

  • Resumes safe checkpoint
  • Reuses run or creates linked attempt
  • Respects provider rate limit
  • Avoids duplicate mapping
  • Avoids duplicate conflicts
  • Records attempt

docs.title: Synchronization Scheduling
docs.text:
Per-source scheduling policy may define:

  • Full interval
  • Incremental interval
  • Quiet hours
  • Retry window
  • Maximum duration
  • Concurrency
  • Maintenance suppression
  • Manual-only mode

docs.title: Source Synchronization Serialization
docs.text:
Only one full synchronization per Media Source runs at a time.

Targeted refresh may run concurrently only when adapter and persistence policy permit it.

docs.title: Cross-Source Concurrency
docs.text: Different Media Sources may synchronize concurrently within global limits.

docs.title: Health Versus Availability
docs.text:
Integration Health describes provider reachability.

Catalog Availability describes playable inventory.

A temporarily unavailable provider does not immediately erase historical availability.

docs.title: Integration Health Fields
docs.text:
• Reachability
  • Authentication
  • Authorization
  • Provider version support
  • Latency
  • Error category
  • Last success
  • Last failure
  • Consecutive failure count
  • Capability freshness
  • Synchronization freshness

docs.title: Source Health State
docs.text:
• HEALTHY
  • DEGRADED
  • UNAVAILABLE
  • AUTHENTICATION_FAILED
  • UNSUPPORTED
  • DISABLED
  • UNKNOWN

docs.title: Playback Resolution
docs.text:
Playback Resolution is an integration port used by Playout.

It does not return permanent Catalog URLs.

docs.title: Playback Resolution Input
docs.text:
• Media Source ID
  • Source Binding ID
  • Playback Variant ID
  • Requested offset
  • Output capability
  • Transcode policy
  • Cancellation
  • Correlation ID

docs.title: Playback Resolution Output
docs.text:
• Access method
  • Short-lived URL or direct path
  • Required headers
  • Expiration
  • Seek support
  • Provider transcode option
  • Security classification
  • Diagnostic warnings

docs.title: Playback Resolution Security
docs.text:
• Credentials remain server-side
  • Signed URL is short-lived
  • Logs redact query secrets
  • Client receives only ChannelForge stream URL unless policy says otherwise
  • Redirect does not forward credentials to unrelated host

docs.title: Playback Resolution Failure
docs.text:
Failure updates runtime diagnostics.

It does not delete Catalog Item.

It may update Playback Variant verification state through a separate bounded command.

docs.title: Plex Adapter
docs.text:
The Plex adapter must implement:

  • Connection probe
  • Provider identity
  • Capability discovery
  • Library discovery
  • Item enumeration
  • Item detail
  • Hierarchy
  • Media parts
  • Artwork access
  • Playback resolution
  • Health
  • Change hints where supported

docs.title: Plex Identity
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Server identity
  • Library identity
  • Item identity
  • Parent identities
  • Media-part identities
  • Provider metadata IDs

docs.title: Plex Authentication
docs.text:
• Uses provider-issued access credential
  • Keeps credential server-side
  • Separates acquisition from synchronization
  • Redacts token
  • Reuses controlled client

docs.title: Plex Media Kinds
docs.text:
Normalize:

  • Movie
  • Series
  • Season
  • Episode
  • Special where inferable
  • Trailer or extra when configured
  • Other

Provider extras do not automatically enter programming inventory.

docs.title: Plex Hierarchy
docs.text:
Preserve enough relationships for:

Series -> Season -> Episode

Missing parents create warnings.

docs.title: Plex Playback Variants
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Media-part ID
  • Container
  • Video codec
  • Audio codec
  • Resolution
  • Bit rate
  • Duration
  • File size
  • Streams
  • Path or key
  • Version token

docs.title: Plex Playback Resolution
docs.text:
May return:

  • Direct access
  • Provider direct stream
  • Provider transcode
  • Required headers
  • Offset parameters

ChannelForge decides whether provider-side transcoding is permitted.

docs.title: Plex Full Reconciliation
docs.text:
Provider change hints may accelerate synchronization.

Periodic full reconciliation remains required.

docs.title: Jellyfin Adapter
docs.text:
The Jellyfin adapter must implement:

  • Connection probe

  • Capability discovery

  • Item enumeration
  • User-scoped visibility
  • Item detail
  • Hierarchy
  • Media source options
  • Artwork
  • Playback information
  • Health
  • Change hints where supported

docs.title: Jellyfin Identity
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Server identity
  • Library identity
  • Item identity
  • Parent identity
  • Media source identity
  • Provider metadata IDs
  • Version observation

docs.title: Jellyfin Authentication
docs.text: The configured account must access included libraries and playback information.

docs.title: Jellyfin Hierarchy
docs.text: Provider virtual folders must not become canonical Seasons without type validation.

docs.title: Jellyfin Playback Variants
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Media source ID
  • Path or remote key
  • Container
  • Protocol
  • Runtime
  • Bit rate
  • Video streams
  • Audio streams
  • Subtitle streams
  • Direct-play observations
  • Transcode observations
  • Version token

docs.title: Jellyfin Playback Resolution
docs.text:
May produce:

  • Direct play
  • Direct stream
  • Provider transcode
  • Stream selection
  • Required token handling
  • Offset behavior
  • Container hints

docs.title: Emby Adapter
docs.text: The Emby adapter must implement the same provider-neutral ports where supported.

docs.title: Emby Identity
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Server identity
  • Library identity
  • Item identity
  • Parent identity
  • Media source identity
  • Provider metadata IDs
  • Version observation

docs.title: Emby Authentication
docs.text:
• Uses provider-supported credential
  • Remains server-side
  • Has required library scope
  • Has playback-information scope where needed

docs.title: Emby Hierarchy
docs.text: Validate Series, Season, Episode, and Special relationships.

docs.title: Emby Playback Variants
docs.text: Normalize provider media-source and stream details into Playback Variant observations.

docs.title: Emby Version Differences
docs.text: Provider-version-specific behavior remains inside adapter fixtures.

docs.title: Provider Contract Consistency
docs.text:
All adapters must produce equivalent semantic observation categories.

Equivalent does not mean identical provider fields.

docs.title: Adapter Fixture Suite
docs.text:
Each adapter requires fixtures for:

  • Authentication success
  • Authentication failure
  • Server identity
  • Version support
  • Library discovery
  • Movie
  • Series
  • Season
  • Episode
  • Special
  • Multiple versions
  • Multiple parts
  • Missing parent
  • Missing metadata
  • Artwork
  • Pagination
  • Rate limit
  • Timeout
  • Partial response
  • Deleted item
  • Playback resolution
  • Provider transcode
  • Unsupported type

docs.title: Adapter Contract Test
docs.text:
The shared contract verifies:

  • Provider-neutral output
  • Qualified IDs
  • Secret omission
  • Stable pagination
  • Error mapping
  • Cancellation
  • Retry classification
  • Versioned fixtures
  • No Catalog domain dependency
  • Deterministic observation

docs.title: Search
docs.text: Catalog search is a derived projection.

docs.title: Search Fields
docs.text:
• Canonical title
  • Alternate title
  • Series title
  • Summary
  • Genre
  • Tag
  • Label
  • Cast and crew
  • Studio
  • Year
  • Media kind
  • Source
  • Availability
  • Collection
  • Franchise
  • External ID
  • Catalog Item ID

docs.title: Search Normalization
docs.text:
May use:

  • Case folding
  • Diacritic folding
  • Tokenization
  • Prefix match
  • Phrase match
  • Stable ranking

docs.title: Search Authority
docs.text:
Search index is derived.

Catalog remains authoritative.

docs.title: Search Failure
docs.text: Search failure must not prevent direct Catalog reads or synchronization commits.

docs.title: Search Rebuild
docs.text:
A rebuild:

  • Uses Catalog revision
  • Is restart-safe
  • Has job status
  • Uses bounded batches
  • Swaps projection after validation where applicable
  • Preserves old projection until replacement validates

docs.title: Filter Semantics
docs.text:
Filters distinguish:

  • Missing
  • Empty
  • Unknown
  • False
  • Zero
  • Archived
  • Unavailable
  • Disabled

docs.title: Sort Semantics
docs.text:
Stable sorts may include:

  • Title
  • Sort title
  • Release date
  • Original air date
  • Duration
  • Recently added
  • Recently synchronized
  • Availability
  • Series order
  • Deterministic randomized order

Every sort ends with Catalog Item ID tie-break.

docs.title: Pagination
docs.text:
Cursor pagination is preferred for large mutable Catalog collections.

Cursor includes:

  • Sort key
  • Catalog Item ID
  • Filter fingerprint
  • Sort fingerprint
  • Catalog revision where required

docs.title: Catalog Revision
docs.text: A scheduling-relevant Catalog revision changes when relevant state changes.

docs.title: Scheduling-Relevant Changes
docs.text:
• Catalog Item creation
  • Archival
  • Media kind
  • Duration
  • Rating
  • Genre
  • Tag
  • Label
  • Hierarchy
  • Availability
  • Collection membership
  • Franchise membership
  • Source Binding eligibility
  • Playback Variant eligibility
  • Effective guide title where snapshots require it

docs.title: Non-Scheduling Changes
docs.text: Pure diagnostic metadata may use separate revision tracking.

docs.title: Catalog Snapshot
docs.text: Scheduling consumes a stable Catalog Snapshot.

docs.title: Snapshot Fields
docs.text:
catalogSnapshotId
createdAt
catalogRevisionWatermark
includedCatalogItemIds
metadataRevisionMap
availabilityRevisionMap
selectorEvaluationVersion
normalizationVersion
contentChecksum
retentionState

docs.title: Snapshot Strategies
docs.text:
Possible implementation:

  • Materialized immutable item membership
  • Revision watermark plus revision map
  • Content-addressed selector result
  • Generation input bundle
  • SQLite snapshot abstraction

docs.title: Snapshot Requirements
docs.text:
A Catalog Snapshot must:

  • Be immutable
  • Be reproducible
  • Use stable ordering
  • Identify normalization version
  • Identify selector version
  • Include effective scheduling metadata
  • Include availability decision inputs
  • Preserve required lineage
  • Have checksum
  • Be retainable with approved plans
  • Avoid live provider calls

docs.title: Snapshot Creation
docs.text:
Snapshot creation:

  1. Resolve Catalog revision.
  2. Evaluate eligibility.
  3. Sort deterministically.
  4. Capture IDs and revisions.
  5. Calculate checksum.
  6. Commit immutable snapshot.
  7. Return Snapshot ID.

HTML scraping must not become the primary adapter behavior.

docs.title: Playback Boundary
docs.text:
Milestone 05 must preserve the distinction between:

  • Metadata discovery
  • Web-player eligibility
  • Linear-planning eligibility
  • Linear-playout eligibility

A YouTube watch URL is not a direct media source.

Milestone 05 must not add:

  • YouTube downloading
  • YouTube stream extraction
  • YouTube-to-FFmpeg restreaming
  • BumpWorthy scraping or downloading
  • Arbitrary remote URL playback

docs.text:

DISCOVERY_INBOX

Automatic add or scheduling requires:

  • A supported playable source
  • Known duration
  • Permitted Rights Status
  • Permitted Playability Status
  • Successful matching
  • Explicit operator policy

docs.title: Media Source Rollback

docs.title: Catalog Rollback

  • Preserve canonical Catalog tables
  • Preserve mappings
  • Preserve conflicts
  • Stop canonical writes
  • Preserve approved schedule references

docs.title: Provider Adapter Rollback
docs.text:
Rollback may select prior adapter version when:

  • Fixture compatibility exists
  • Schema remains supported
  • Cursor is compatible or reset
  • Full reconciliation follows

docs.title: Synchronization Rollback
docs.text:
Do not roll back committed source observations by deleting source state automatically.

Use prior snapshot, backup, or corrective synchronization.

docs.title: Merge Rollback
docs.text:
Merge rollback requires:

  • Lineage
  • No incompatible later writes
  • Binding history
  • Collection repair
  • Historical schedule policy
  • Operator approval

docs.title: Split Rollback
docs.text: Split rollback requires equivalent lineage and conflict review.

docs.title: Snapshot Rollback
docs.text:
Snapshots are immutable.

Rollback selects an older snapshot or publication input.

docs.title: Provider Authentication Failure
docs.text:
• Mark Source authentication failed
  • Stop new provider calls
  • Preserve Catalog
  • Preserve approved plans
  • Expose credential action
  • Avoid deleting bindings

docs.title: Provider Unavailable
docs.text:
• Mark source degraded or unavailable
  • Preserve prior observations
  • Avoid destructive reconciliation
  • Retry according to policy
  • Keep unrelated sources active

docs.title: Provider Identity Change
docs.text:
• Stop synchronization
  • Create conflict
  • Preserve mappings
  • Require operator decision
  • Avoid attaching new server data to old source silently

docs.title: Synchronization Failure
docs.text:
• Preserve committed batches
  • Preserve checkpoint
  • Mark run failed
  • Record source health
  • Avoid marking unseen items missing
  • Permit resume

docs.title: Normalization Failure
docs.text:
• Record item warning or failure
  • Preserve raw observation reference
  • Continue when safe
  • Do not fabricate field

docs.title: Match Conflict
docs.text:
• Do not choose first candidate
  • Create durable conflict
  • Preserve source item
  • Exclude from unsafe scheduling where required

docs.title: Search Failure
docs.text:
• Keep Catalog reads available
  • Mark projection stale
  • Queue rebuild
  • Preserve old projection when valid

docs.title: Artwork Failure
docs.text:
• Preserve prior artwork
  • Mark candidate invalid or missing
  • Do not expose secret URL
  • Continue Catalog synchronization

docs.title: Snapshot Failure
docs.text:
• Do not publish partial snapshot
  • Preserve prior snapshot
  • Record Catalog revision
  • Return stable error

  • Partial-response state

  • Threshold
  • Conflict

docs.title: Duration Drift

docs.title: Source Reinstall

  • New Source option

docs.title: Path Mapping Failure

  • Windows/Linux tests

  • Bounded batches
  • Checkpoint
  • Metrics
  • Indexes

docs.title: Webhook Overtrust

  • Deduplication
  • Queue refresh
  • Full reconciliation

docs.title: Adapter Version Drift
docs.text:

Mitigation:

  • Unsupported state

docs.title: Search Dependency
docs.text:

Mitigation:

  • Derived projection
  • Direct read fallback
  • Rebuild
  • Health

docs.title: Merge Damage
docs.text:
Incorrect merge may affect history.

Mitigation:

  • Preview
  • Lineage
  • Tombstone
  • Audit
  • Rollback criteria

docs.title: Snapshot Size
docs.text:
Materialized snapshots may be large.

Mitigation:

  • Strategy evaluation
  • Content addressing
  • Revision maps
  • Retention

docs.title: Legacy Migration Ambiguity
docs.text:
Legacy program records may lack enough identity.

Mitigation:

  • Placeholder
  • Conflict
  • Preserve schedule history
  • Operator review

Mitigation:

  • /config

docs.title: Milestone Mission
docs.text:
ChannelForge must model television Networks as durable editorial identities and Channels as tuneable output feeds.

The Networks and Channels milestone must:

  • Establish Network as the editorial owner
  • Establish Channel as the output-facing broadcast identity
  • Keep Network and Channel identity stable
  • Separate human-readable names from canonical IDs
  • Make profile changes revisioned
  • Make programming configuration revisioned
  • Make activated revisions immutable
  • Preserve one active revision per configuration type
  • Permit explicit Channel overrides
  • Prevent Channel overrides from mutating Network revisions
  • Keep channel numbering stable
  • Keep XMLTV, M3U, and HDHomeRun identity aligned
  • Preserve time-zone semantics
  • Preserve schedule history through changes
  • Preserve inherited Channel configuration
  • Avoid automatic destructive renumbering
  • Keep seasonal programming available for ordinary year-round rotation unless an explicit hard exclusion is configured
  • Support seasonal boosts and seasonal blocks without making seasonal titles disappear from the normal Catalog
  • Prepare immutable inputs for deterministic scheduling
  • Keep live playout outside editorial configuration
  • Keep provider IDs outside Network and Channel configuration
  • Keep migration reversible
  • Make every important editorial change auditable

docs.title: Product Principle
docs.text:
The governing product principle is:

Build television networks, not playlists.

A Network is not a list of media.

A Network is an editorial identity with:

  • Mission
  • Audience
  • Content boundaries
  • Programming preferences
  • Scheduling policies
  • Branding
  • Dayparts
  • Blocks
  • Rules
  • One or more Channels

A Channel is not the Network.

A Channel is a numbered or otherwise addressable output feed operating under one Network.

docs.title: Core Principles
docs.text:
1. A Network owns editorial identity.
  2. A Channel owns tuneable output identity.
  3. A Channel belongs to one Network in version 1.
  4. A Network may own multiple Channels.
  5. Network and Channel IDs are ChannelForge-owned.
  6. Names, slugs, numbers, and call signs are mutable human-facing keys.
  7. Activated profile revisions are immutable.
  8. Activated Programming Configuration Revisions are immutable.
  9. A Schedule Plan records every revision used.
  10. Channel overrides are explicit overlays.
  11. Channel overrides do not mutate Network revisions.
  12. Output adapters use one canonical Output Identity.
  13. Time-zone context is explicit.
  14. Persisted instants remain UTC.
  15. Dayparts use local editorial time.
  16. Seasonal programming is policy, not Catalog deletion.
  17. Seasonal titles remain available year-round unless explicitly excluded.
  18. Approved Schedule Plans remain immutable.
  19. Archival preserves history.
  20. Legacy migration preserves user intent.

docs.title: Slug Rules
docs.text:
A slug should be:

  • Lowercase
  • URL-safe
  • Stable enough for operator recognition
  • Unique among non-archived Networks
  • Mutable through controlled command
  • Redirectable or aliasable where public routes use it

docs.title: Slug Is Not Identity

docs.title: Network Status
docs.text:
Suggested states:

  • DRAFT
  • ACTIVE
  • PAUSED
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Draft Network
docs.text:
A Draft Network:

  • May have no active Channel
  • May have incomplete branding
  • May have draft Programming Configuration
  • Cannot publish live output
  • Can be previewed
  • Can be deleted only when never referenced and policy permits

docs.title: Active Network
docs.text:
An Active Network:

  • Has a valid primary time zone
  • Has at least one non-archived Channel
  • Has an active Network Profile Revision
  • Has an active Programming Configuration Revision
  • Has no blocking validation error
  • May publish schedules through its Channels

docs.title: Paused Network
docs.text:
A Paused Network:

  • Preserves identity
  • Preserves active revisions
  • Preserves Channels
  • Preserves approved schedules
  • Prevents new publication or playout according to policy
  • May continue guide display according to policy
  • May be resumed

docs.title: Archived Network
docs.text:
An Archived Network:

  • Is removed from ordinary active lists
  • Cannot create new active schedules
  • Preserves Channels
  • Preserves profile revisions
  • Preserves Programming Configuration Revisions
  • Preserves Branding revisions
  • Preserves schedules
  • Preserves audit
  • Preserves migration mapping
  • Requires explicit restore

docs.title: Network Lifecycle Transitions
docs.text:
Allowed transitions:

DRAFT -> ACTIVE
DRAFT -> ARCHIVED
ACTIVE -> PAUSED
ACTIVE -> ARCHIVED
PAUSED -> ACTIVE
PAUSED -> ARCHIVED
ARCHIVED -> DRAFT
ARCHIVED -> PAUSED

Exact restore target depends on validation.

  • No blocking migration conflict

docs.title: Network Archive
docs.text: Archiving a Network does not hard-delete its Channels.

docs.title: Revision Creation
docs.text:

docs.title: Revision Activation
docs.text:
Activation:

  1. Validates content.
  2. Calculates canonical hash.
  3. Verifies expected active revision.
  4. Marks current active revision superseded.
  5. Activates new revision atomically.
  6. Updates Network active reference.
  7. Records audit.
  8. Emits event.
  9. Marks dependent draft plans stale where required.
  10. Does not mutate approved plans.

docs.title: Activated Revision Immutability
docs.text:
After activation, profile content cannot change.

Corrections create a new revision.

docs.title: Network Display Name
docs.text:
Display Name is stored in the Network Profile Revision.

Changing it creates a new revision.

docs.title: Short Name
docs.text: Short Name supports constrained output and UI surfaces.

docs.title: Call Sign or Brand Code
docs.text:
This value is editorial branding.

It is not the canonical Channel ID.

docs.title: Editorial Mission
docs.text:
The Editorial Mission states the Network's programming purpose.

Examples:

  • Showcase supernatural horror across film and episodic television
  • Present family-safe animation throughout the day
  • Run classic cinema with curated evening blocks
  • Provide science-fiction programming with franchise marathons

The mission is descriptive and may inform future recommendations.

It does not directly execute scheduling.

docs.title: Editorial Profile
docs.text: The Editorial Profile defines what belongs on the Network.

docs.title: Editorial Profile Fields
docs.text:
Potential fields:

  • Preferred genres
  • Excluded genres
  • Preferred eras
  • Excluded eras
  • Allowed media kinds
  • Desired novelty
  • Desired familiarity
  • Franchise behavior
  • Series-completion behavior
  • Movie-to-episode balance
  • Seasonal behavior
  • Content-rating limits
  • Original-programming labels
  • Network-specific labels
  • Repeat tolerance
  • Short-form tolerance
  • Presentation-media policy

docs.title: Editorial Profile Semantics
docs.text:
Editorial Profile values are defaults and guidance.

Hard constraints belong in explicit Programming Rules.

docs.title: Preferred Genre
docs.text:
A preferred genre increases eligibility score or selector priority.

It does not necessarily exclude other genres.

docs.title: Excluded Genre
docs.text: An excluded genre is effective only when represented as an explicit hard constraint or Catalog policy.

docs.title: Seasonal Behavior
docs.text:
Seasonal programming supports:

  • Seasonal boost
  • Seasonal block
  • Seasonal premiere window
  • Seasonal collection
  • Seasonal branding
  • Seasonal repeat adjustment
  • Holiday-specific daypart
  • Temporary priority increase

docs.title: Seasonal Availability Rule
docs.text:
Seasonal programming metadata does not remove titles from ordinary year-round rotation by default.

A holiday or seasonal title remains eligible outside its season unless:

  • An explicit hard exclusion is configured
  • A selector is intentionally season-only
  • The operator disables ordinary eligibility
  • Content availability changes

docs.title: Seasonal Boost
docs.text:
A seasonal boost may increase:

  • Candidate score
  • Block priority
  • Collection priority
  • Repeat tolerance
  • Branding assignment
  • Promotional frequency

The boost is evaluated in a specified local date range and time zone.

docs.title: Seasonal Hard Window
docs.text: A season-only rule must be explicit and visibly classified as a hard constraint.

docs.title: Seasonal Overlap
docs.text:
A title may belong to:

  • Ordinary rotation
  • Seasonal collection
  • Holiday block
  • Franchise block
  • Manual collection

These memberships are not mutually exclusive.

docs.title: Audience Profile
docs.text: The Audience Profile describes intended viewers.

docs.title: Audience Profile Fields
docs.text:
• General audience description
  • Age-band constraints
  • Household suitability
  • Language expectations
  • Desired pacing
  • Desired repeat tolerance
  • Daypart-specific suitability
  • Content sensitivity
  • Accessibility preferences

docs.title: Privacy Rule
docs.text:
Audience Profile is editorial configuration.

It must not become behavioral tracking of actual viewers without separate approved privacy architecture.

docs.title: Network Relationships
docs.text:
A Network:

  • Has one active Network Profile Revision
  • Has one active Programming Configuration Revision
  • Has zero or one active Branding Profile Revision
  • Owns one or more Channels when active
  • Has historical Schedule Plans through Channels
  • Has Health Snapshots
  • May originate from Template Snapshot
  • May reference shared Presentation Assets

docs.title: Network Invariants
docs.text:
1. An active Network has at least one non-archived Channel.
  2. An active Network has one valid IANA time zone.
  3. Network identity changes create a new profile revision.
  4. Archiving preserves Channels and history.
  5. Programming rules use Catalog concepts, not provider IDs.
  6. Recommendations cannot silently mutate Network state.
  7. Template changes cannot silently mutate an existing Network.
  8. Active slugs are unique.
  9. Active revision references resolve.
  10. Activated revisions are immutable.
  11. Network defaults do not retroactively alter approved plans.
  12. Seasonal labels do not remove year-round eligibility automatically.

docs.title: Channel Aggregate
docs.text:
A Channel represents a tuneable broadcast output.

A Channel belongs to exactly one Network in version 1.

docs.title: Channel ID
docs.text:
channelId is:

  • Opaque
  • Stable
  • ChannelForge-owned
  • Independent of Channel number
  • Independent of guide ID
  • Independent of tuner lineup ID
  • Independent of legacy Channel ID
  • Independent of provider identity

docs.title: Channel Status
docs.text:
Suggested states:

  • DRAFT
  • ACTIVE
  • PAUSED
  • MAINTENANCE
  • ARCHIVED

docs.title: Draft Channel
docs.text:
A Draft Channel:

  • May have provisional number
  • May have no active publication
  • Cannot be exposed as active output
  • Can be previewed
  • May be deleted if never referenced

docs.title: Active Channel
docs.text:
An Active Channel:

  • Belongs to active or paused Network according to policy
  • Has unique number within output scope
  • Has active Channel Profile Revision
  • Has canonical Output Identity
  • Has output configuration
  • May have active publication
  • Has no blocking validation conflict

docs.title: Paused Channel
docs.text:
A Paused Channel:

  • Preserves active publication
  • Preserves schedule
  • Prevents or suspends live playout according to policy
  • May remain in guide according to policy
  • Can resume without regenerating identity

docs.title: Maintenance Channel
docs.text:
A Maintenance Channel:

  • Preserves identity
  • May serve slate or maintenance output
  • May remain in guide
  • Does not rewrite approved schedule
  • Records operator action
  • Has explicit fallback behavior

docs.title: Archived Channel
docs.text:
An Archived Channel:

  • Is excluded from active lineup
  • Preserves number history
  • Preserves Output Identity
  • Preserves guide history
  • Preserves Schedule Plans
  • Preserves publications
  • Preserves playout history
  • Preserves migration mapping
  • Requires explicit restore

docs.title: Channel Lifecycle Transitions
docs.text:
DRAFT -> ACTIVE
DRAFT -> ARCHIVED
ACTIVE -> PAUSED
ACTIVE -> MAINTENANCE
ACTIVE -> ARCHIVED
PAUSED -> ACTIVE
PAUSED -> MAINTENANCE
PAUSED -> ARCHIVED
MAINTENANCE -> ACTIVE
MAINTENANCE -> PAUSED
MAINTENANCE -> ARCHIVED
ARCHIVED -> DRAFT
ARCHIVED -> PAUSED

  • Programming override
  • Access policy

docs.title: Channel Profile Revision Rule
docs.text: An activated Channel Profile Revision is immutable.

docs.title: Channel Profile Inheritance
docs.text:
Effective Channel profile may derive from:

  1. Channel-specific revision
  2. Network Profile defaults
  3. Instance defaults

The resulting effective profile must be reproducible.

docs.title: Channel Profile Override
docs.text:
A Channel override must identify:

  • Overridden field
  • Base Network revision
  • Override value
  • Actor
  • Created timestamp
  • Revision
  • Removal behavior

docs.title: Override Removal
docs.text:
Removing an override restores inheritance from the active Network revision.

It does not restore a copied stale value.

docs.title: Channel Number
docs.text: Channel Number is a value object.

docs.title: Channel Number Fields
docs.text:
major
minor
canonicalDisplay
sortKey

docs.title: Channel Number Examples
docs.text:
• 7
  • 7.1
  • 102
  • 500.25

docs.title: Channel Number Parsing
docs.text:
Parsing must distinguish:

  • Major-only
  • Major and minor
  • Invalid punctuation
  • Leading zero policy
  • Negative
  • Fractional ambiguity
  • Overflow
  • Client-incompatible value

docs.title: Channel Number Canonicalization
docs.text: Canonical display must be deterministic.

docs.title: Channel Number Storage
docs.text:
Store structured major and optional minor values.

Do not rely only on a display string.

docs.title: Channel Number Scope
docs.text:
Active Channel number uniqueness applies within configured output scope.

Version 1 default scope:

one active ChannelForge instance

A future output-profile-specific scope may be introduced only through explicit design.

docs.title: Channel Number Uniqueness
docs.text:
Two active Channels cannot share the same canonical number in the same scope.

Archived Channels may preserve historical numbers.

docs.title: Channel Number Change
docs.text:
Changing a number:

  • Preserves Channel ID
  • Creates audit
  • Updates canonical Output Identity revision
  • Regenerates output artifacts
  • May affect client lineup
  • Does not rewrite approved Schedule Entries
  • May require operator warning

docs.title: Renumbering Prohibition
docs.text:
Migration must not automatically renumber a legacy Channel unless:

  • A conflict exists
  • An explicit migration policy is selected
  • The operator approves or policy is pre-approved
  • Old and new values are recorded
  • Client impact is shown

docs.title: Number Conflict
docs.text:
A number conflict may be resolved by:

  • Preserve first and renumber second
  • Assign minor number
  • Keep one Channel inactive
  • Use operator-selected number
  • Split output scope in a future supported design

No resolution is guessed silently.

docs.title: Call Sign
docs.text:
Call Sign is human-facing.

It is not canonical identity.

docs.title: Canonical Output Identity
docs.text: Every published Channel has one canonical Output Identity.

docs.title: Output Identity Fields
docs.text:
channelId
guideChannelId
tunerLineupId
displayNumber
displayName
logoReference
identityRevision

docs.title: Output Identity Rule
docs.text: XMLTV, M3U, HDHomeRun-compatible endpoints, and stream routing derive from the same Output Identity.

docs.title: Guide Channel ID
docs.text:
Guide ID must be:

  • Stable
  • Unique
  • Compatible with XMLTV policy
  • Mapped from legacy guide ID where preserving it is required
  • Independent of provider ID
  • Auditable when changed

docs.title: Tuner Lineup ID
docs.text: Tuner lineup identity must map back to channelId.

docs.title: Output Adapter Prohibition
docs.text: Output adapters must not invent separate canonical Channel IDs.

docs.title: Output Identity Revision
docs.text:
Output-facing mutable fields may use an identity revision.

Changes that may increment revision:

  • Channel number
  • Guide ID
  • Display name
  • Logo
  • Tuner publication state
  • Output policy

docs.title: Output Identity Compatibility
docs.text:
Changing output identity may affect:

  • Plex Live TV
  • Jellyfin Live TV
  • Emby Live TV
  • IPTV clients
  • Guide mapping
  • Cached lineup
  • Existing bookmarks

The UI must warn before high-impact changes.

docs.title: Channel Output Configuration Reference
docs.text:
The Channel references output configuration.

Output configuration may include:

  • Stream mode
  • Transcode profile
  • Fallback behavior
  • Maximum sessions
  • Guide publication state
  • Tuner publication state
  • Stream access policy
  • Startup buffering policy
  • Maintenance behavior

Milestone 06 stores the reference and ownership.

Milestone 08 implements final playout and output behavior.

docs.title: Channel Time Zone
docs.text: A Channel normally inherits Network primary time zone.

docs.title: Time-Zone Override
docs.text:
A Channel may define an override when:

  • It represents a regional feed
  • It represents a time-shift feed
  • Its editorial day differs
  • Imported legacy semantics require it
  • Operator explicitly configures it

docs.title: Time-Zone Precedence
docs.text:
1. Channel override
  2. Network primary time zone
  3. Instance default during migration only

An active Network must ultimately have an explicit valid primary time zone.

docs.title: IANA Time Zone
docs.text:
Use an IANA identifier.

Examples:

  • America/Los_Angeles
  • America/New_York
  • Europe/London

Do not persist a bare numeric UTC offset as the editorial time zone.

docs.title: Persisted Time
docs.text: All persisted instants remain UTC.

docs.title: Local Editorial Time
docs.text:
Local time applies to:

  • Dayparts
  • Weekdays
  • Calendar dates
  • Seasonal ranges
  • Holidays
  • Operator timeline display
  • Effective ranges

docs.title: Daylight Saving Time
docs.text: DST ambiguity must be explicit.

docs.title: DST Gap
docs.text:
A nonexistent local time may:

  • Shift forward
  • Skip occurrence
  • Use configured policy
  • Fail validation

Policy belongs to scheduling specification.

docs.title: DST Fold
docs.text:
A repeated local time requires:

  • Earlier occurrence
  • Later occurrence
  • Both
  • Explicit policy

docs.title: Time-Shifted Channel
docs.text: A time-shifted Channel reuses editorial programming with a defined offset.

docs.title: Time-Shift Policy Fields
docs.text:
sourceChannelId
offsetMinutes
effectiveTimeZone
publicationPolicy
guidePolicy
brandingPolicy

docs.title: Time-Shift Rules
docs.text:
• Source Channel must belong to allowed Network scope
  • Offset is explicit
  • Output Identity remains distinct
  • Channel ID remains distinct
  • Schedule derivation is reproducible
  • Time shift does not mutate source plan
  • Guide times reflect shifted instants
  • DST policy is explicit
  • Branding may inherit or override
  • Runtime uses separate publication identity

docs.title: Time-Shift Non-Goal
docs.text:
Milestone 06 defines configuration.

Milestone 07 and Milestone 08 define scheduling and playout realization.

docs.title: Branding Historical Preservation

docs.title: Programming Revision Ownership
docs.text:
A Network owns the base Programming Configuration.

A Channel may have an explicit overlay revision.

docs.title: Base and Overlay
docs.text:
Effective programming input is:

  1. Active Network Programming Configuration Revision
  2. Active Channel overlay revision
  3. Explicit instance defaults copied into snapshot where allowed

docs.title: Overlay Rule
docs.text:
The Channel overlay:

  • References base revision
  • Contains only explicit differences
  • Has its own revision ID
  • Has deterministic merge semantics
  • Cannot mutate base
  • Is snapshotted into Schedule Plan inputs

docs.title: Overlay Conflicts
docs.text:
A base revision change may make an overlay:

  • Valid
  • Stale
  • Conflicted
  • Invalid

The system must validate before activation or schedule generation.

docs.title: Programming Revision Activation
docs.text:
Activation validates:

  • Owner
  • Effective range
  • Dayparts

  • Selectors
  • Catalog references
  • Repeat policy
  • Timing policy
  • Filler policy
  • Randomization policy
  • Seasonal policy
  • Overlay compatibility
  • Human-readable explanations

docs.title: Use Immutability
docs.text:
A Programming Configuration Revision becomes immutable after:

  • Activation, or
  • Use in any Schedule Plan

docs.title: Draft Editing
docs.text: Editing a draft does not alter active configuration.

docs.title: Clone Revision
docs.text:
A new draft may clone:

  • Active revision
  • Historical revision
  • Template
  • Imported legacy configuration
  • Another Network
  • Blank defaults

docs.title: Daypart
docs.text: A Daypart is a named recurring local-time interval.

docs.title: Daypart Fields

endLocalTime
