docs.title: Daypart Examples
docs.text:
• Weekday Morning
  • Prime Time
  • Late Night
  • Saturday Cartoons
  • Weekend Afternoon
  • Overnight
  • Holiday Evening

docs.title: Daypart Time Zone
docs.text: Daypart local time is interpreted in effective Channel time zone unless an explicit permitted override exists.

docs.title: Overnight Daypart
docs.text:
A Daypart may cross midnight.

Example:

Late Night: 22:00 -> 02:00

The ownership date rule must be explicit.

docs.title: Daypart Overlap
docs.text: Overlapping Dayparts require deterministic precedence.

docs.title: Daypart Precedence
docs.text:
Possible precedence inputs:

  • Priority
  • Specific date range
  • Channel overlay
  • Explicit block priority
  • Stable ID tie-break

docs.title: Daypart Validation
docs.text:
Validate:

  • Day selection
  • Time format
  • Zero-length interval
  • Full-day intent
  • Midnight crossing
  • Effective range
  • Priority
  • DST policy
  • Overlap explanation

docs.title: Catalog Selector

docs.title: Selector Fields

Potential criteria:

  • Content rating

  • Explicit exclude IDs
  • Source policy
  • Metadata completeness
  • Seasonal label

docs.title: Selector Rule
docs.text:
Selectors use normalized Catalog fields.

They do not query Plex, Jellyfin, or Emby directly.

docs.title: Selector Stability
docs.text: Selector evaluation against one Catalog Snapshot must be deterministic.

docs.title: Explicit Include
docs.text: Explicit include uses Catalog Item IDs.

docs.title: Explicit Exclude
docs.text: Explicit exclusion is a hard constraint only within the selector or rule scope where configured.

docs.title: Seasonal Selector
docs.text:
A seasonal selector may identify holiday or event titles.

Membership does not make the title season-only.

docs.title: Programming Rule
docs.text: A Programming Rule describes one constraint, preference, or placement behavior.

docs.title: Rule Fields
docs.text:
ruleId
ruleType
classification
parameters
priority
weight
enabledState
explanationTemplate
algorithmVersionRequirement

docs.title: Rule Classifications
docs.text:
• Hard constraint
  • Soft constraint
  • Placement rule
  • Spacing rule
  • Sequence rule
  • Quota rule
  • Timing rule
  • Presentation rule

docs.title: Hard Constraint
docs.text:
Failure makes a candidate ineligible.

Examples:

  • Maximum content rating
  • Required availability
  • Allowed media kind
  • Must fit unbreakable window
  • Minimum exclusion interval
  • Explicit season-only window

docs.title: Soft Constraint
docs.text:
A soft constraint contributes score.

Examples:

  • Prefer items not aired recently
  • Prefer target genre balance
  • Prefer chronological progression
  • Prefer seasonal title during its season
  • Prefer unused promotional assets
  • Prefer target duration distribution

docs.title: Seasonal Preference
docs.text:
The default seasonal behavior is a soft preference or block-level priority increase.

It does not remove seasonal titles from the ordinary rotation outside the season.

docs.title: Placement Rule
docs.text:
Controls occupation of time.

Examples:

  • Start at boundary
  • Fill to boundary
  • Allow overrun
  • Preserve episode order
  • Insert bumper
  • Alternate media kind
  • Movie followed by shorts
  • Keep franchise installments in order

docs.title: Spacing Rule
docs.text:
Controls repeat distance.

Examples:

  • Minimum title repeat interval
  • Minimum episode repeat interval
  • Franchise spacing
  • Seasonal repeat tolerance
  • Bumper cooldown
  • Ident cooldown

docs.title: Sequence Rule
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Episode order
  • Release order
  • Custom order
  • Shuffle with seed
  • Marathon sequence
  • Alternating series

docs.title: Quota Rule
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Movie count
  • Episode count
  • Genre ratio
  • Series share
  • Filler ceiling
  • Seasonal content target
  • Original label target

docs.title: Timing Rule
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Start at local time
  • End before boundary
  • No overnight start
  • Holiday effective range
  • Prime-time minimum duration
  • Daypart-specific rating

docs.title: Presentation Rule
docs.text:
Examples:

  • Bumper before program
  • Ident at hour boundary
  • Rating card before restricted item
  • Seasonal ident during date range
  • Technical slate on missing content

docs.title: Rule Precedence
docs.text:
Precedence must be deterministic.

Suggested order:

  1. Safety hard constraints
  2. Explicit operator exclusions
  3. Channel hard overrides
  4. Network hard constraints
  5. Block hard constraints
  6. Sequence requirements
  7. Placement rules
  8. Quotas
  9. Soft preferences
  10. Stable tie-break

The exact scheduling evaluation belongs to Milestone 07.

docs.title: Rule Explanation
docs.text: Every activated rule must provide a human-readable explanation template.

docs.title: Repetition Policy
docs.text:
Global repetition policy may include:

  • Title repeat interval
  • Episode repeat interval
  • Series repeat interval
  • Franchise repeat interval
  • Same-day repeat policy
  • Same-week repeat policy
  • Recently aired window
  • Exception policy
  • Seasonal repeat adjustment

docs.title: Seasonal Repeat Adjustment
docs.text:
During a configured season, repeat tolerance may be relaxed for seasonal titles.

Outside the season, ordinary repeat policy applies.

The title remains eligible unless explicitly excluded.

docs.title: Timing Policy
docs.text:
Global timing policy may include:

  • Default block alignment
  • Hour boundaries
  • Half-hour boundaries
  • Overrun
  • Underrun
  • Filler insertion
  • Slate insertion
  • Off-air policy
  • DST handling

docs.title: Filler Policy
docs.text:
Filler policy defines:

  • Eligible filler selector
  • Maximum filler duration
  • Minimum filler duration
  • Repeat interval
  • Trimming allowance
  • Bumper use
  • Slate fallback
  • Gap tolerance
  • Priority

docs.title: Randomization Policy
docs.text:
Randomization policy defines:

  • Algorithm version
  • Seed source
  • Tie-break behavior
  • Shuffle scope
  • Stability requirements
  • Reproducibility

docs.title: Randomization Rule
docs.text:
Activated configuration stores randomization policy.

Generated Schedule Plan stores actual seed and algorithm version.

docs.title: Effective Range
docs.text: A Programming Revision may have an effective time range.

docs.title: Effective Range Semantics
docs.text:
An effective range controls revision selection.

It does not mutate the revision.

docs.title: Future Revision
docs.text: A future revision may be scheduled for activation.

docs.title: Revision Selection
docs.text:
At schedule-generation time, selection must be explicit.

The plan records selected revision ID.

docs.title: Configuration Snapshot
docs.text: Scheduling receives an immutable configuration snapshot.

docs.title: Configuration Snapshot Contents
docs.text:
• Network ID
  • Channel ID
  • Network Profile Revision
  • Channel Profile Revision
  • Branding Revision
  • Programming Revision
  • Channel overlay
  • Effective time zone
  • Output policy references
  • Content hashes
  • Catalog Snapshot ID

docs.title: Configuration Fingerprint
docs.text:
A deterministic fingerprint supports:

  • Plan reproducibility
  • Stale detection
  • Approval
  • Audit
  • Comparison

docs.title: Stale Draft Plan
docs.text:
A draft plan may become stale when:

  • Active profile changes
  • Programming revision changes
  • Channel overlay changes
  • Catalog revision changes
  • Time zone changes
  • Output compatibility changes
  • Branding asset becomes invalid

Approved plans are not mutated.

docs.title: Network-Owned Configuration
docs.text:
Network owns:

  • Editorial mission
  • Audience Profile
  • Editorial Profile
  • Primary time zone
  • Base Programming Configuration
  • Default Branding
  • Default Catalog policy
  • Default guide-description policy
  • Default content-rating policy

docs.title: Channel-Owned Configuration
docs.text:
Channel owns:

  • Channel number
  • Output Identity
  • Output configuration reference
  • Time-zone override
  • Time shift
  • Channel Profile
  • Branding override
  • Programming overlay
  • Active publication reference
  • Channel lifecycle

docs.title: Instance-Owned Defaults
docs.text:
Instance may provide:

  • Default time zone during creation
  • Default schedule horizon
  • Default output settings
  • Default locale
  • Default guide policy
  • Default channel number suggestion

Defaults are copied or referenced according to policy.

Instance defaults do not retroactively mutate active revisions.

docs.title: Catalog-Owned Inputs
docs.text:
Catalog owns:

  • Catalog Item identity
  • Metadata
  • Availability
  • Collections
  • Labels
  • Playback Variants
  • Catalog Snapshots

Network and Channel rules reference Catalog IDs and normalized fields.

docs.title: Publication-Owned State
docs.text:
Publication owns active approved-plan selection.

Channel stores a reference according to aggregate design.

docs.title: Playout-Owned State
docs.text:
Playout owns active sessions.

Channel lifecycle commands may request Playout action through application services.

docs.title: Override Ownership
docs.text:
Every override identifies:

  • Base owner
  • Base revision
  • Override owner
  • Override revision
  • Field or rule
  • Effective range
  • Actor
  • Audit
  • Removal behavior

docs.title: Override Prohibitions
docs.text:
An override must not:

  • Modify base revision
  • Hide its source
  • Use provider IDs as Catalog identity
  • Silently disable safety rules
  • Change approved plan
  • Alter another Channel
  • Become a mutable unversioned settings blob

docs.title: Network Creation Workflow
docs.text:
1. Create Network ID.
  2. Validate slug.
  3. Select time zone.
  4. Create draft Network Profile Revision.
  5. Create draft Programming Configuration Revision.
  6. Optionally create draft Branding Profile Revision.
  7. Create or attach first Channel.
  8. Validate.
  9. Activate revisions.
  10. Activate Network.
  11. Record audit.

docs.title: Channel Creation Workflow
docs.text:
1. Select Network.
  2. Create Channel ID.
  3. Assign provisional Channel number.
  4. Create draft Channel Profile Revision.
  5. Derive Output Identity.
  6. Select output configuration.
  7. Choose inherited or override time zone.
  8. Add optional branding override.
  9. Add optional programming overlay.
  10. Validate.
  11. Activate Channel Profile Revision.
  12. Activate Channel.
  13. Record audit.

docs.title: Clone Network Workflow
docs.text:
Cloning may copy:

  • Network Profile
  • Programming Configuration
  • Branding
  • Channel definitions
  • Output references
  • Template lineage

Cloning generates new entity IDs and revision IDs.

It does not copy active Schedule Plans as active output.

docs.title: Clone Channel Workflow
docs.text:
Cloning generates:

  • New Channel ID
  • New number
  • New Output Identity
  • New profile revision
  • New override revisions

It may reference the same Network base configuration.

docs.title: Template Application
docs.text:
A Template may create:

  • Network
  • Network Profile Revision
  • Programming Configuration Revision
  • Branding Profile Revision
  • Channel definitions
  • Asset assignments

docs.title: Template Independence
docs.text:
After application, the Network operates from ChannelForge-owned revisions.

Later Template changes do not mutate it.

docs.title: Legacy Migration
docs.text: Legacy Tunarr Channels migrate into Network and Channel entities.

docs.title: Legacy Migration Goals
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Channel number
  • Channel name
  • Time zone
  • Guide identity
  • Icon or logo
  • Enabled state
  • Output profile
  • Schedule source
  • Runtime settings
  • Existing guide behavior
  • Existing stream compatibility
  • Existing user order
  • Provider references through Catalog mapping

docs.title: Legacy Network Assignment
docs.text: Because inherited Tunarr Channels may not have a first-class Network, migration must assign them deliberately.

docs.title: Network Assignment Strategies
docs.text:
Supported strategies:

  • One default migrated Network
  • Group by legacy metadata
  • One Network per legacy grouping
  • Operator-selected grouping
  • One Network per Channel for strict isolation

docs.title: Default Migrated Network
docs.text:
A default migrated Network should have:

  • Stable generated Network ID
  • Clear name
  • Migration provenance
  • Draft Network Profile Revision
  • Draft Programming Configuration Revision
  • Operator-editable branding
  • Explicit time zone
  • Legacy migration reference

docs.title: Default Network Naming
docs.text:
Suggested starting name:

Migrated Network

The UI should encourage operator editing.

docs.title: Channel Migration Mapping
docs.text: Each legacy Channel maps to one ChannelForge Channel ID.

docs.title: Channel Mapping Fields
docs.text:
• Legacy namespace
  • Legacy Channel ID
  • ChannelForge Channel ID
  • Network ID
  • Mapping state
  • Number
  • Guide ID
  • Source schema version
  • Migration run
  • Verification
  • Conflict

docs.title: Legacy Number Preservation
docs.text: Preserve the existing Channel number when valid and conflict-free.

docs.title: Automatic Renumbering Prohibition
docs.text: Do not automatically renumber without explicit migration policy.

docs.title: Legacy Name Preservation
docs.text:
Preserve:

  • Display name
  • Short name where available
  • Call sign where available
  • Guide name
  • Existing icon label

docs.title: Legacy Time Zone
docs.text:
When explicit legacy time zone exists:

  • Validate IANA value
  • Preserve it
  • Record provenance
  • Create conflict when invalid

docs.title: Missing Legacy Time Zone
docs.text:
When no explicit time zone exists:

  1. Use Instance default.
  2. Record inferred provenance.
  3. Flag review where schedule semantics may change.
  4. Do not pretend the value came from legacy data.

docs.title: Legacy Guide Identity
docs.text:
Preserve guide ID where client compatibility requires it.

Map it to canonical Channel ID.

docs.title: Legacy Logo
docs.text:
Legacy logo may become:

  • Presentation Asset
  • Remote reference
  • Managed imported asset
  • Conflict
  • Missing warning

docs.title: Legacy Enabled State
docs.text:
Map to:

  • Active
  • Paused
  • Draft
  • Archived

The mapping policy must be explicit.

docs.title: Legacy Output Profile
docs.text:
Translate to an output configuration reference.

Unsupported settings become:

  • Warning
  • Preserved migration metadata
  • Conflict
  • Deferred runtime mapping

docs.title: Legacy Schedule Configuration
docs.text: Inherited scheduling configuration becomes a Programming Configuration Revision.

docs.title: Migration Revision Status
docs.text:
A migrated Programming Configuration Revision may be:

  • Draft requiring review
  • Active after verified automatic migration
  • Invalid
  • Conflict

docs.title: Automatic Activation
docs.text:
Automatic activation is allowed only when:

  • Translation is complete
  • Semantics are verified
  • No conflict exists
  • Policy permits
  • Validation passes
  • Operator policy has accepted automatic activation

docs.title: Default Migration Behavior
docs.text:
Default behavior should favor:

DRAFT requiring operator review

when schedule semantics could change.

docs.title: Legacy Seasonal Behavior
docs.text: Legacy seasonal lists or scheduling rules should migrate without removing titles from ordinary rotations unless the original configuration explicitly encoded season-only exclusion.

docs.title: Legacy Schedule Source
docs.text:
Preserve source references through:

  • Catalog Item mapping
  • Collection mapping
  • Explicit include list
  • Explicit exclude list
  • Conflict
  • Placeholder

docs.title: Legacy Runtime Settings
docs.text: Runtime settings remain compatibility configuration until Milestone 08.

docs.title: Legacy Channel Conflict Types
docs.text:
• Duplicate number
  • Invalid number
  • Missing name
  • Invalid time zone
  • Duplicate guide ID
  • Missing logo
  • Unsupported output profile
  • Unresolved program IDs
  • Invalid schedule rule
  • Provider-specific rule
  • Missing Catalog mapping
  • Conflicting Network grouping

docs.title: Migration Conflict Resolution
docs.text:
Possible actions:

  • Change number
  • Change guide ID
  • Choose Network
  • Choose time zone
  • Accept inferred time zone
  • Select output profile
  • Remove unsupported rule
  • Convert rule
  • Keep draft
  • Exclude Channel
  • Archive Channel
  • Defer

docs.title: Migration Verification
docs.text:
Verify:

  • Legacy Channel exists
  • Network exists
  • Channel exists
  • Mapping unique
  • Number preserved or approved change
  • Name preserved
  • Time zone preserved or provenance recorded
  • Guide ID preserved or approved change
  • Logo mapped
  • Enabled state mapped
  • Output profile mapped
  • Schedule configuration mapped
  • Catalog references resolve
  • Active status validates

docs.title: Compatibility Read
docs.text:
Before cutover:

  1. Read canonical Network and Channel when present.
  2. Resolve legacy mapping.
  3. Fall back to legacy Channel.
  4. Translate to ChannelForge read model.
  5. Record fallback.
  6. Avoid duplicate entity creation.

docs.title: Compatibility Write
docs.text: Temporary write translation may be required when legacy runtime still consumes Channel rows.

docs.title: Write Authority
docs.text: Per migration phase, authority must be explicit.

docs.title: Legacy Write Freeze
docs.text:
Before final Channel cutover:

  • Legacy Channel create route is frozen
  • Legacy Channel update route is frozen
  • Legacy Channel delete or archive route is frozen
  • Legacy scheduling writer is frozen
  • Legacy Channel background writer is frozen
  • First-party UI uses canonical commands
  • Server-side enforcement exists
  • Rollback exists

docs.title: Persistence Foundations
docs.text:
Milestone 06 may introduce tables or equivalent repositories for:

  • Network
  • Network Profile Revision
  • Channel
  • Channel Profile Revision
  • Output Identity
  • Branding Profile
  • Branding Profile Revision

  • Asset Assignment

  • Programming Configuration Revision

  • Rule Set
  • Rule

  • Channel Programming Overlay

docs.title: Schema Ownership
docs.text:
Networks owns Network tables.

Channels owns Channel and Output Identity tables.

Branding owns Branding and Presentation Asset tables.

Programming owns Programming Configuration tables.

docs.title: Revision Storage
docs.text:
Revisions may store:

  • Normalized relational children
  • Canonical JSON document
  • Hybrid relational and JSON

The chosen representation must preserve:

  • Immutability
  • Validation
  • Canonical hashing
  • Query needs
  • Migration
  • Human diagnostics

docs.title: Canonical Hash
docs.text: Every activated revision has deterministic content hash.

docs.title: Foreign Keys
docs.text:
Required relationships include:

  • Channel to Network
  • Profile Revision to owner
  • Programming Revision to Network
  • Channel overlay to Channel and base revision
  • Branding Revision to owner
  • Asset Assignment to asset and owner
  • Active revision references
  • Publication reference to Channel

docs.title: Archive Constraints
docs.text: Archiving does not cascade-delete historical revisions.

docs.title: Optimistic Concurrency
docs.text:
Mutable aggregate roots use expected version.

Revision creation uses expected active revision where appropriate.

docs.title: Network Rollback
docs.text:
Rollback may:

  • Disable canonical Network mode
  • Restore compatibility reads
  • Preserve Network IDs
  • Preserve revisions
  • Preserve mappings
  • Stop canonical writes

docs.title: Channel Rollback
docs.text:
Rollback may:

  • Restore legacy Channel read authority
  • Preserve Channel IDs
  • Preserve number mapping
  • Preserve guide mapping
  • Preserve canonical revisions
  • Pause canonical commands

docs.title: Revision Rollback
docs.text:
Activated revisions are not edited backward.

Rollback activates a prior valid revision through a new activation record or explicit pointer rollback according to policy.

docs.title: Renumber Rollback
docs.text:
Renumber rollback:

  • Restores prior number if available
  • Validates uniqueness
  • Regenerates output identity
  • Records audit
  • Warns client impact

docs.title: Time-Zone Rollback
docs.text:
Restoring prior time zone may mark draft plans stale.

Approved plans remain unchanged.

docs.title: Programming Rollback
docs.text:
Activate prior Programming Configuration Revision.

Do not mutate current revision.

docs.title: Branding Rollback
docs.text:
Activate prior valid Branding Revision.

Preserve assets.

docs.title: Migration Rollback
docs.text:
• Restore legacy authority
  • Preserve mapping
  • Preserve migration findings
  • Restore backup when required
  • Do not regenerate IDs
  • Reconcile temporary writes

docs.title: Network Activation Failure
docs.text:
• Keep Network Draft or prior state
  • Preserve active revisions
  • Return validation
  • Do not partially activate

docs.title: Channel Activation Failure
docs.text:
• Preserve prior Channel state
  • Do not publish output identity partially
  • Return conflict
  • Preserve number reservation according to transaction policy

docs.title: Revision Activation Failure
docs.text:
• Keep current active revision
  • Keep draft
  • Record failure
  • Do not supersede active revision

docs.title: Number Conflict
docs.text:
• Reject activation or renumber command
  • Return conflicting Channel reference where authorized
  • Do not guess replacement

docs.title: Time-Zone Failure
docs.text:
• Reject invalid zone
  • Preserve prior zone
  • Return actionable error
  • Do not persist bare offset as zone

docs.title: Asset Failure
docs.text:
• Keep prior Branding Revision
  • Mark draft invalid
  • Preserve asset diagnostics

docs.title: Programming Validation Failure
docs.text:
• Keep revision Draft or Invalid
  • Return rule and path
  • Do not activate partially

docs.title: Migration Conflict
docs.text:
• Preserve legacy Channel
  • Preserve mapping proposal
  • Keep canonical entity Draft where appropriate
  • Require operator decision

docs.title: Network/Channel Confusion
docs.text:
Implementation may treat each Channel as an isolated Network.

Mitigation:

  • Explicit ownership
  • Module separation
  • Network-first UI
  • Aggregate tests

docs.title: Revision Bypass
docs.text:
Mutable settings blobs may bypass immutable revisions.

Mitigation:

  • Repository boundaries
  • Activation commands
  • Architecture tests
  • Hashes

docs.title: Number Collision
docs.text:
Migration or restore may produce duplicate numbers.

Mitigation:

  • Unique constraint
  • Conflict queue
  • No automatic renumber
  • Activation gate

docs.title: Output Identity Drift
docs.text:
Guide, playlist, and tuner identity may diverge.

Mitigation:

  • Canonical Output Identity
  • Cross-output tests
  • Shared ID mapping

docs.title: Time-Zone Drift
docs.text:
Instance defaults may silently change editorial meaning.

Mitigation:

  • Explicit Network zone
  • Migration provenance
  • Revision snapshot
  • DST tests

docs.title: Seasonal Exclusion Error
docs.text:
Seasonal labels may accidentally remove titles from ordinary rotation.

Mitigation:

  • Default soft preference
  • Explicit hard-rule classification
  • UI distinction
  • Invariant tests

docs.title: Override Complexity
docs.text:
Channel overlays may become opaque.

Mitigation:

  • Sparse overrides
  • Provenance
  • Diff
  • Fingerprint
  • Staleness validation

docs.title: Legacy Schedule Semantic Drift
docs.text:
Migration may approximate inherited rules incorrectly.

Mitigation:

  • Draft review default
  • Characterization
  • Conflict
  • Comparison
  • No automatic activation when ambiguous

docs.title: Branding Asset Loss
docs.text:
Replacing logos may break guide history.

Mitigation:

  • Managed assets
  • Checksums
  • Retention
  • Revision references

docs.title: Slug Coupling
docs.text:
External callers may treat slug as identity.

Mitigation:

  • Canonical IDs
  • Redirect or alias policy
  • API contracts

docs.title: Time-Shift Ambiguity
docs.text:
Offset feeds may behave incorrectly at DST transitions.

Mitigation:

  • Explicit policy
  • UTC plan instants
  • tests
  • Separate output identity

docs.title: Oversized Revision Documents
docs.text:
Large rules may degrade validation.

Mitigation:

  • Limits
  • relational children
  • canonical hashing
  • performance tests

docs.title: Migration Grouping Error
docs.text:
Default Network assignment may not match user intent.

Mitigation:

  • Preview
  • operator grouping
  • reversible mapping
  • clear default Network

docs.title: UI Overload
docs.text:
Network-first concepts may feel more complex than Channels alone.

Mitigation:

  • Guided builders
  • defaults
  • progressive disclosure
  • templates

ChannelForge schedules television Networks rather than shuffling playlists.

The Scheduling milestone must:

  • Generate one immutable Schedule Plan per Channel and horizon
  • Use only immutable or versioned inputs
  • Use UTC instants for all planned entry boundaries
  • Evaluate editorial time using an IANA time zone
  • Handle daylight-saving transitions deterministically
  • Resolve Dayparts deterministically
  • Resolve Programming Blocks deterministically
  • Distinguish hard constraints from soft preferences
  • Respect active Network and Channel revisions
  • Respect Catalog Snapshot identity and revision
  • Respect locks and fixed events
  • Respect repeat cooldowns
  • Respect series progression
  • Respect seasonal policy
  • Preserve seasonal titles for year-round rotation unless explicitly excluded
  • Use recorded random seeds
  • Use a versioned deterministic random generator
  • Avoid database-return-order dependence
  • Avoid live provider calls in candidate evaluation
  • Avoid FFmpeg execution
  • Produce human-readable rule evidence
  • Produce structured failures
  • Use bounded search and backtracking
  • Validate before approval
  • Keep approval separate from publication
  • Preserve active approved output on failure
  • Create new plans instead of mutating existing plans
  • Detect and classify staleness
  • Compare against inherited scheduling behavior during migration
  • Remain practical for SQLite and one container

docs.title: Product Principle
docs.text:
The governing product principle remains:

Build television networks, not playlists.

A schedule must express editorial identity across time.

It is not enough to fill empty duration.

The scheduler must account for:

  • Network mission
  • Audience expectations
  • Daypart suitability
  • Programming Block intent
  • Content boundaries
  • Series continuity
  • Repeat tolerance
  • Seasonal intent
  • Catalog depth
  • Duration
  • Availability
  • Presentation identity
  • Guide quality
  • Fixed events
  • Operational policy

docs.title: Core Separation
docs.text:
ChannelForge separates:

  1. Programming configuration
  2. Schedule generation
  3. Schedule validation
  4. Schedule approval
  5. Schedule publication
  6. Runtime playout
  7. Actual airing history

These stages must not collapse into one mutable playlist.

docs.title: Scope
docs.text:
Version 1 supports:

  • Continuous linear schedules
  • One Schedule Plan per Channel
  • Planning Horizons of days or weeks
  • Local-time editorial rules
  • Repeating Dayparts
  • Programming Blocks
  • Catalog Selectors
  • Hard constraints
  • Soft preferences
  • Quotas
  • Cooldowns
  • Series progression
  • Deterministic weighted selection
  • Fixed boundaries
  • Flexible boundaries
  • Fixed events
  • Manual placements
  • Locked entries
  • Filler
  • Presentation entries
  • Explicit Off-Air entries
  • Draft generation
  • Preview
  • Simulation
  • Validation
  • Manual approval
  • Policy-based approval
  • Extension
  • Range regeneration
  • Gap repair
  • Staleness
  • Structured diagnostics
  • Legacy comparison

docs.title: Non-Goals
docs.text:
Version 1 does not require:

  • Real-time audience optimization
  • Personalized schedules per viewer
  • Machine-learned recommendations
  • Advertising auctions
  • Rights-window optimization beyond explicit rules
  • Distributed planning
  • Multi-node consensus
  • Live-event rights management
  • Frame-accurate broadcast automation
  • Automatic media acquisition
  • Dynamic schedule mutation during playback
  • FFmpeg command construction
  • Runtime source failover implementation
  • Client-specific Schedule Plans
  • Provider API calls per candidate
  • Autonomous creative editorial decisions
  • Automatic override of operator locks
  • Automatic publication without policy approval

docs.title: Scheduling Module Ownership
docs.text:
The Scheduling module owns:

  • Generation Request
  • Generation Attempt
  • Generator version
  • Rule registry
  • Rule implementation version
  • Schedule Plan
  • Schedule Entry
  • Rule Evidence
  • Candidate Evaluation
  • Generation diagnostics
  • Validation Result
  • Plan staleness
  • Manual lock
  • Fixed-event scheduling representation
  • Progression proposal
  • Plan comparison
  • Generation metrics

docs.title: Programming Module Ownership
docs.text:
Programming owns:

  • Programming Configuration Revision
  • Dayparts
  • Programming Blocks
  • Rules
  • Catalog Selectors
  • Repeat policy configuration
  • Timing policy configuration
  • Filler policy configuration
  • Randomization policy configuration
  • Seasonal policy configuration

Scheduling consumes those revisions.

Scheduling does not mutate them.

docs.title: Catalog Module Ownership
docs.text:
Catalog owns:

  • Catalog Items
  • Catalog Snapshots
  • Availability
  • Collections
  • Labels
  • Series hierarchy
  • Franchise relationships
  • Duration provenance
  • Playback Variant eligibility

Scheduling reads a Catalog Snapshot.

Scheduling does not query providers live.

docs.title: Channels Module Ownership
docs.text:
Channels owns:

  • Channel ID
  • Channel time zone
  • Channel Profile Revision
  • Output Identity
  • Channel lifecycle
  • Channel override revision references

docs.title: Networks Module Ownership
docs.text:
Networks owns:

  • Network ID
  • Network Profile Revision
  • Editorial Profile
  • Audience Profile
  • Network lifecycle

docs.title: Branding Module Ownership
docs.text:
Branding owns:

  • Branding Profile Revision
  • Presentation Asset references
  • Asset Assignment policy

Scheduling may create presentation Schedule Entries from immutable eligible assets.

docs.title: Publication Module Ownership
docs.text:
Publication owns:

  • Active approved-plan selection
  • Schedule Publication
  • Artifact generation requests
  • Last-known-good publication

Scheduling approval does not activate publication.

docs.title: Playout Module Ownership
docs.text:
Playout owns:

  • Runtime source selection
  • Playback Variant resolution
  • FFmpeg process plan
  • Active session
  • Recovery
  • Airing Records

Scheduling does not start or control runtime sessions.

docs.title: Planning Horizon
docs.text:
The Planning Horizon is the half-open interval:

[startInstant, endInstant)

Start is inclusive.

End is exclusive.

docs.title: Requested Horizon
docs.text: The requested horizon is the interval requested by the command.

docs.title: Actual Covered Interval
docs.text:
The actual covered interval may include:

  • Carry-In before the requested start
  • Carry-Out beyond the requested end

Coverage metrics are calculated against the requested horizon.

docs.title: Schedule Cursor
docs.text:
The Schedule Cursor is the next UTC instant requiring a planning decision.

The cursor advances only after one or more draft entries are committed to Working State.

docs.title: Temporal Context
docs.text:
Temporal Context is derived from the cursor and recorded time zone.

It includes:

  • UTC instant
  • Local date
  • Local weekday
  • Local wall-clock time
  • UTC offset
  • DST status
  • Holiday membership
  • Seasonal membership
  • Active Dayparts
  • Active Blocks
  • Upcoming boundaries

docs.title: Candidate
docs.text:
A Candidate is:

  • Catalog Item
  • Presentation Asset
  • Filler Item
  • Slate
  • Explicit Off-Air option
  • Imported fixed segment
  • Manual placement

docs.title: Eligible Candidate
docs.text: An Eligible Candidate satisfies every applicable hard constraint.

docs.title: Candidate Score
docs.text:
A Candidate Score is the deterministic numeric result of:

  • Soft preferences
  • Quota pressure
  • Sequence preference
  • Boundary efficiency
  • Novelty
  • Repeat penalty
  • Seasonal boost
  • Selector weight
  • Presentation preference
  • Deterministic tie-breaking

docs.title: Placement
docs.text: Placement turns a Candidate into one or more proposed Schedule Entries with UTC start and end instants.

docs.title: Coverage
docs.text: Coverage is the interval set inside the requested horizon occupied by explicit Schedule Entries.

docs.title: Gap
docs.text: A Gap is an uncovered interval where policy requires coverage.

docs.title: Off-Air
docs.text:
Off-Air is an explicit Schedule Entry.

An uncovered gap is not Off-Air.

docs.title: Boundary
docs.text:
A Boundary is an editorial or technical instant affecting placement.

Examples:

  • Daypart start
  • Daypart end
  • Programming Block start
  • Programming Block end
  • Top of hour
  • Half hour
  • Quarter hour
  • Fixed event
  • Manual placement
  • Planning Horizon end
  • Publication handoff

docs.title: Lock
docs.text: A Lock protects an existing Schedule Entry or interval from permitted regeneration.

docs.title: Fixed Event
docs.text: A Fixed Event requires content or an explicit event representation at a specific time or interval.

docs.title: Generation Request
docs.text: A Generation Request is the application command starting planning.

docs.title: Generation Request Fields
docs.text:
generationRequestId
networkId
channelId
horizonStart
horizonEnd
generationMode
networkProfileRevisionId
channelProfileRevisionId
programmingConfigurationRevisionId
channelOverrideRevisionId
brandingProfileRevisionId
catalogSnapshotId
existingSchedulePlanId
lockedEntryIds
fixedEventReferences
randomSeed
generatorVersion
requestedBy
requestedAt
approvalPolicy
diagnosticVerbosity
runtimeBudgetMs
candidateEvaluationBudget
idempotencyKey
previewOnly

docs.title: Generation Modes
docs.text:
• FULL
  • EXTEND
  • REGENERATE_RANGE
  • REPAIR_GAPS
  • PREVIEW
  • SIMULATE

docs.title: Full Generation
docs.text:
Creates a new plan for the entire requested horizon.

It does not mutate an existing plan.

docs.title: Extend
docs.text:
Preserves an existing prefix and adds entries after its end.

Extension validates:

  • Same Channel
  • Compatible revision policy
  • Exact or allowed boundary
  • Relevant history tail
  • Existing-plan checksum
  • Lock preservation
  • No publication conflict

docs.title: Regenerate Range
docs.text:
Creates a new plan derived from an existing plan.

Entries outside the selected interval are preserved by immutable copy or reference.

The result receives a new Schedule Plan ID.

docs.title: Repair Gaps
docs.text:
Fills explicit uncovered intervals while preserving surrounding entries.

Repair respects:

  • Locked entries
  • Fixed events
  • Existing boundaries
  • Repeat history
  • Filler limits
  • Neighbor continuity
  • Publication freeze windows

docs.title: Preview
docs.text:
Generates a complete draft and validation result.

It cannot be approved directly unless promoted through a normal validated workflow.

docs.title: Simulate
docs.text:
Evaluates scheduling behavior and metrics.

Simulation may relax publication or playout constraints according to explicit policy.

Simulation output is clearly labeled.

docs.title: Idempotency
docs.text:
Identical idempotency key and request hash should return the same Generation Request result.

The seed is not regenerated on retry.

docs.title: Required Immutable Inputs
docs.text:
A Generation Request resolves:

  • Channel ID
  • Network ID
  • Horizon
  • Editorial time zone
  • Network Profile Revision
  • Channel Profile Revision
  • Programming Configuration Revision
  • Channel override revision
  • Branding Profile Revision
  • Catalog Snapshot
  • Relevant Schedule History snapshot
  • Relevant Airing History snapshot
  • Locks
  • Fixed events
  • Generator version
  • Rule versions
  • Randomization version
  • Seed
  • Generation mode
  • Approval policy
  • Budgets

docs.title: Input Snapshot Rule
docs.text:
All inputs capable of changing output are represented by:

  • Immutable ID
  • Revision
  • Snapshot
  • Version
  • Content checksum

The generator does not repeatedly read mutable live configuration.

docs.title: Snapshot Consistency
docs.text: Paged Catalog and history loads must belong to the same snapshot or watermark.

docs.title: Configuration Fingerprint
docs.text:
The generator records one deterministic configuration fingerprint covering:

  • Network Profile
  • Channel Profile
  • Programming Configuration
  • Channel overlay
  • Branding
  • Time zone
  • Rule versions
  • Catalog Snapshot
  • Generator version

docs.title: Input Resolution
docs.text:
Input resolution validates:

  • Entity existence
  • Entity lifecycle
  • Revision activation
  • Revision immutability
  • Revision ownership
  • Channel ownership
  • Time zone
  • Catalog Snapshot availability
  • Lock ownership
  • Fixed-event ownership
  • Horizon bounds
  • Generator compatibility
  • Rule compatibility
  • Seed presence

A failed Generation Attempt need not persist an invalid Schedule Plan.

docs.title: Schedule Plan Immutability
docs.text:
After persistence:

  • Entries do not change
  • Input references do not change
  • Seed does not change
  • Generator versions do not change
  • Checksum does not change
  • Guide snapshots do not change

Status and approval metadata may be separate records.

docs.title: Schedule Entry
docs.text: A Schedule Entry represents one planned interval.

docs.title: Schedule Entry Fields
docs.text:
scheduleEntryId
schedulePlanId
sequenceNumber
startInstant
endInstant
durationMs
entryKind
catalogItemId
presentationAssetId
sourceBindingHint
playbackVariantHint
programmingBlockId
daypartIds
ruleEvidenceReference
presentationInstructions
continuityMetadata

fallbackClassification

docs.title: Entry Kinds
docs.text:
• PROGRAM
  • BUMPER
  • IDENT
  • PROMO
  • ADVERTISEMENT
  • FILLER
  • SLATE
  • OFF_AIR
  • CARRY_IN
  • CARRY_OUT
  • FIXED_EVENT
  • MANUAL

docs.title: Entry Duration
docs.text: Every entry has positive duration.

docs.title: Entry Ordering
docs.text:
Entries are ordered by:

  1. Start instant
  2. Sequence number
  3. Schedule Entry ID

Generation never depends on database default ordering.

docs.title: Entry Overlap
docs.text:
Overlaps are prohibited unless a separately defined overlay model explicitly permits them.

Version 1 ordinary linear Schedule Plans do not require overlapping entries.

docs.title: Guide Metadata Snapshot
docs.text:
Approved plans retain guide-facing metadata.

Potential fields:

  • Title
  • Episode title
  • Series title
  • Description
  • Rating
  • Genres
  • Season number
  • Episode number
  • Original air date
  • Artwork reference
  • Entry kind
  • Language

docs.title: Working State
docs.text:
The generator maintains mutable in-memory Working State.

The persisted result remains immutable.

docs.title: Working State Fields
docs.text:
• Current cursor
  • Active Daypart stack
  • Active Block stack
  • Upcoming boundaries
  • Selected entries
  • Working repeat history
  • Working progression state
  • Quota counters
  • Presentation cooldown state
  • Backtracking checkpoints
  • Candidate evaluation count
  • Warning list
  • Runtime budget remaining

docs.title: Working State Determinism
docs.text:
Working State uses:

  • Stable collection ordering
  • Versioned data structures where serialization matters
  • Explicit integer arithmetic
  • Explicit random streams
  • No process-global mutable state

docs.title: UTC Storage
docs.text: Every entry boundary is stored as a UTC instant.

docs.title: Editorial Time Zone
docs.text: Dayparts, local dates, weekdays, holidays, and seasonal rules use the Channel's recorded IANA time zone.

docs.title: Local-Time Derivation
docs.text:
For each cursor instant derive:

  • Local date
  • Weekday
  • Local time
  • Offset
  • DST status
  • Holiday
  • Season
  • Daypart membership
  • Block membership

docs.title: Spring DST Transition
docs.text:
When a local interval does not exist:

  • It contributes no elapsed schedulable duration
  • A block entirely inside the gap is skipped unless relocation is configured
  • Fixed local starts require resolution policy
  • Default relocation moves to first valid instant after transition
  • Warning is recorded

docs.title: Fall DST Transition
docs.text:
When a local interval occurs twice:

  • Each occurrence is a distinct UTC interval
  • Recurring Dayparts apply to both unless configured otherwise
  • Fixed starts use explicit fold policy

docs.title: Fold Policies
docs.text:
• FIRST_OCCURRENCE
  • SECOND_OCCURRENCE
  • BOTH
  • REJECT_AMBIGUOUS

docs.title: Duration Precision
docs.text:
Scheduling uses integer milliseconds or finer integer units.

Floating-point accumulation must not determine boundaries.

docs.title: Horizon Validation
docs.text:
The horizon must:

  • Start before end
  • Fit configured min and max
  • Fit supported timestamp range
  • Respect generation budget
  • Align with regeneration policy
  • Match locked-entry scope
  • Avoid unsupported publication overlap

docs.title: Horizon Defaults
docs.text:
A practical initial default is several days to two weeks.

Exact defaults remain Instance settings.

docs.title: Scheduling Pipeline
docs.text:
1. Validate Generation Request
2. Resolve immutable inputs
3. Verify versions and checksums
4. Load Catalog Snapshot
5. Load bounded relevant history
6. Build temporal context
7. Resolve active Dayparts
8. Resolve active Programming Blocks
9. Resolve fixed events and locks
10. Build Candidate set
11. Apply hard constraints
12. Calculate soft scores
13. Apply quota adjustments
14. Apply deterministic tie-breaking
15. Select Candidate
16. Attempt placement
17. Insert required presentation entries
18. Update Working State
19. Advance cursor
20. Backtrack when allowed
21. Repeat until complete or terminal failure
22. Validate complete plan
23. Compute content checksum
24. Persist immutable plan and evidence
25. Emit post-commit events

docs.title: Daypart Resolution
docs.text:
At each cursor:

  1. Convert cursor to local context.
  2. Find matching Dayparts.
  3. Apply date restrictions.
  4. Apply weekday restrictions.
  5. Apply time interval.
  6. Resolve overlap precedence.
  7. Produce stable ordered Daypart stack.

docs.title: Daypart Precedence
docs.text:
Suggested precedence:

  1. Explicit Channel override
  2. Specific date range
  3. Higher priority
  4. Narrower interval
  5. Stable Daypart ID

The exact rule is versioned.

docs.title: Cross-Midnight Daypart
docs.text: A Daypart crossing midnight must define which local date owns the occurrence.

docs.title: Programming Block Resolution
docs.text:
Blocks may be activated by:

  • Daypart
  • Explicit local window
  • Fixed UTC window
  • Calendar date
  • Seasonal range
  • Recurrence
  • Manual event

docs.title: Block Stack
docs.text:
Multiple Blocks may apply.

The scheduler resolves:

  • Primary Block
  • Overlay rules
  • Presentation policy
  • Selector union or intersection
  • Boundary behavior
  • Priority

docs.title: Block Precedence
docs.text:
Suggested order:

  1. Fixed event
  2. Manual placement
  3. Explicit Channel Block
  4. Network Block with specific date
  5. Higher priority
  6. Narrower scope
  7. Stable Block ID

docs.title: Block Conflict
docs.text:
An irreconcilable conflict produces validation or generation failure.

It does not use arbitrary first match.

docs.title: Seasonal Rules
docs.text: Seasonal rules are evaluated using recorded local date and calendar version.

docs.title: Seasonal Default
docs.text: Seasonal labels and seasonal collections do not make items ineligible outside the season.

docs.title: Seasonal Boost
docs.text:
Inside an active range, a seasonal boost may increase:

  • Candidate score
  • Selector priority
  • Quota target
  • Repeat tolerance
  • Presentation frequency

docs.title: Season-Only Rule
docs.text: A season-only restriction is an explicit hard constraint.

docs.title: Holiday Calendar
docs.text:
A Holiday Calendar must have:

  • Calendar version
  • Locale or region
  • Time-zone interpretation
  • Date set
  • Source
  • Content checksum

docs.title: Candidate Query
docs.text: Candidate querying begins from Catalog Snapshot data.

docs.title: Candidate Query Inputs
docs.text:
• Active selectors
  • Media kinds
  • Availability
  • Duration limits
  • Hierarchy
  • Labels
  • Collections
  • Franchise
  • Rating
  • Language
  • Explicit include
  • Explicit exclude
  • Block scope
  • Local context

docs.title: Candidate Query Invariants
docs.text:
• No live provider calls
  • Stable ordering
  • Catalog Snapshot consistency
  • Explicit pagination
  • Stable tie-break
  • Bounded candidate count
  • Explainable exclusion

docs.title: Candidate Set
docs.text: The raw Candidate set contains candidates before hard constraints.

docs.title: Candidate Pool
docs.text:
A bounded Candidate Pool may be used for expensive scoring.

Pool policy is versioned.

docs.title: Candidate Pool Selection
docs.text:
Pool formation may prioritize:

  • Selector priority
  • Basic eligibility
  • Duration fit
  • Progression relevance
  • Low repeat penalty
  • Stable deterministic sample

docs.title: Candidate Set Empty
docs.text:
If no Candidates exist, the generator proceeds according to:

  • Filler policy
  • Off-Air policy
  • Backtracking policy
  • Failure policy

docs.title: Hard Constraints
docs.text:
A hard constraint determines eligibility.

Failure cannot be overridden by score.

docs.title: Hard Constraint Examples
docs.text:
• Catalog Item unavailable
  • Content rating exceeds limit
  • Media kind not allowed
  • Explicit exclusion
  • Duration cannot fit hard boundary
  • Item aired within hard cooldown
  • Series progression requires another episode
  • Required language absent
  • Required daypart mismatch
  • Fixed event conflict
  • Locked interval conflict
  • Season-only rule inactive
  • Maximum airings exceeded
  • Missing required presentation asset
  • Invalid guide metadata when required

docs.title: Hard Constraint Result
docs.text:
PASS
FAIL
NOT_APPLICABLE
ERROR

docs.title: Hard Constraint Evidence
docs.text:
Records:

  • Rule ID
  • Rule version
  • Candidate ID
  • Result
  • Reason code
  • Relevant values
  • Scope
  • Evaluation duration

docs.title: Hard Constraint Ordering
docs.text: Evaluate cheap indexed constraints before expensive ones.

docs.title: Constraint Error
docs.text:
An evaluator error is not treated as pass.

Policy may:

  • Fail candidate
  • Fail generation
  • Mark rule invalid
  • Continue only when rule is explicitly optional

docs.title: Soft Preferences
docs.text: Soft preferences adjust score.

docs.title: Soft Preference Examples
docs.text:
• Prefer unseen item
  • Prefer underrepresented genre
  • Prefer chronological progression
  • Prefer seasonal item in season
  • Prefer exact boundary fit
  • Prefer unused presentation asset
  • Prefer target runtime distribution
  • Prefer less recently aired title
  • Prefer source diversity
  • Prefer desired movie-to-episode balance

docs.title: Score Model
docs.text: A score is computed with deterministic integer or fixed-point arithmetic.

docs.title: Floating-Point Policy
docs.text:
Floating point must not create platform-dependent ordering.

Use:

  • Integers
  • Fixed-point values
  • Decimal library with deterministic semantics
  • Explicit rounding

docs.title: Score Components
docs.text:
Each component records:

  • Rule ID
  • Version
  • Raw value
  • Normalized value
  • Weight
  • Contribution
  • Bound
  • Explanation

docs.title: Score Bounds
docs.text: Every soft rule should have bounded contribution unless documented otherwise.

docs.title: Score Tie
docs.text: Ties are resolved deterministically.

docs.title: Quotas
docs.text: Quotas track targets across a scope.

docs.title: Quota Scopes
docs.text:
• Block
  • Daypart
  • Local day
  • Local week
  • Horizon
  • Network coordination window

docs.title: Quota Dimensions
docs.text:
• Media kind
  • Genre
  • Series
  • Franchise
  • Collection
  • Label
  • Rating
  • Duration band
  • Seasonal content
  • Presentation share
  • Filler share

docs.title: Hard Quota
docs.text:
A hard quota is allowed only when feasibility can be evaluated sufficiently.

An impossible hard quota produces failure or validation error.

It does not silently become soft.

docs.title: Soft Quota
docs.text:
A soft quota adjusts score according to deficit or surplus.

Adjustment is bounded.

docs.title: Quota State
docs.text:
Records:

  • Rule ID
  • Scope
  • Target
  • Current amount
  • Remaining duration
  • Remaining candidate capacity
  • Projected deficit
  • Projected surplus

docs.title: Repeat Dimensions
docs.text:
Repeat policy may apply to:

  • Catalog Item
  • Episode
  • Movie
  • Series
  • Season
  • Franchise
  • Genre
  • Collection
  • Block
  • Presentation Asset
  • Guide title
  • Custom grouping key

docs.title: History Sources
docs.text:
• PLANNED
  • AIRED
  • PLANNED_AND_AIRED
  • APPROVED_ONLY
  • ANY_GENERATED

docs.title: Default History Source
docs.text: Viewer-facing repeat policy should default to planned and aired history with duplicate lineage deduplicated.

docs.title: Cooldown
docs.text:
A cooldown may be:

  • Hard
  • Soft
  • Exact-item
  • Series-level
  • Franchise-level
  • Daypart-specific
  • Block-specific
  • Seasonal-adjusted

docs.title: Repeat Window
docs.text:
Repeat windows evaluate backward from proposed start.

Working State entries already generated are included.

docs.title: Maximum Airings
docs.text:
Examples:

  • No more than twice per local week
  • No more than once per 48 hours
  • No more than three episodes from one Series per Block
  • No more than one ident every 30 minutes

docs.title: Minimum Separation
docs.text:
May use:

  • Elapsed duration
  • Intervening entries
  • Intervening unique titles
  • Local days
  • Block occurrences

docs.title: Presentation Repeat Policy
docs.text:
Presentation assets use independent cooldowns.

Their short duration must not permit excessive repetition.

docs.title: Repeat Evidence
docs.text:
Records:

  • Dimension
  • Candidate key
  • History source
  • Last occurrence
  • Window
  • Count
  • Threshold
  • Result
  • Penalty or failure

docs.title: Series Policies
docs.text:
• CHRONOLOGICAL
  • AIR_DATE
  • DVD_ORDER
  • ABSOLUTE_ORDER
  • RANDOM_EPISODE
  • RANDOM_SEASON_THEN_EPISODE
  • SHUFFLED_CYCLE
  • MANUAL_QUEUE
  • LATEST_UNAIRED
  • CUSTOM

docs.title: Progression Scope
docs.text:
Progression may be scoped to:

  • Network
  • Channel
  • Block
  • Selector
  • Template application

Version 1 default should be Channel plus Selector or Block.

docs.title: Progression Cursor
docs.text:
Fields:

progressionCursorId
scopeKey
seriesId
orderingPolicy
lastSelectedEpisodeId
nextExpectedEpisodeId
cycleNumber
lastCommittedSchedulePlanId
lastAiringRecordId
resetPolicy
version

docs.title: Planned Versus Aired Progression
docs.text:
Version 1 default:

  • Planning uses latest approved progression
  • Working State advances provisionally
  • Draft generation does not commit progression
  • Approval commits planned progression lineage
  • Failed airing records create exceptions
  • Publication and actual airing remain distinct

docs.title: Missing Episode
docs.text:
Policy may:

  • Stop progression
  • Skip temporarily
  • Select another Series
  • Select later episode
  • Insert filler
  • Fail Block

Skipping is recorded.

Skipping does not mark the episode complete.

docs.title: Series Cycle
docs.text:
When a Series completes:

  • Stop
  • Restart
  • Restart after cooldown
  • Start deterministic shuffled cycle
  • Exclude from Selector
  • Require operator action

docs.title: Progression Proposal
docs.text:
A generated plan records proposed progression updates.

Approval commits them atomically with approval metadata or through a coordinated transaction.

docs.title: Progression Race
docs.text: Approval verifies expected progression version.

docs.title: Sequencing Rules
docs.text: Sequencing evaluates adjacency and recent order.

docs.title: Sequencing Examples
docs.text:
• Avoid two movies consecutively
  • Alternate comedy and drama
  • Place bumper after two episodes
  • Place ident before first program of hour
  • Keep multipart episodes together
  • Pair short with feature
  • Avoid same Series in adjacent Blocks
  • Preserve double-feature order

docs.title: Sequencing Classification
docs.text:
• Hard
  • Soft
  • Placement-producing
  • Presentation-producing

docs.title: Sequence Evidence
docs.text:
Records:

  • Prior entries
  • Rule
  • Expected pattern
  • Candidate effect
  • Result
  • Explanation

docs.title: Candidate Ranking
docs.text:
Default stable ordering:

  1. Hard-constraint eligibility
  2. Total preference score
  3. Explicit Selector priority
  4. Boundary efficiency
  5. Sequence preference
  6. Deterministic random tie-break
  7. Stable Catalog Item ID

docs.title: Ranking Version
docs.text: The ranking model is part of generator versioning.

docs.title: Seed
docs.text:
Every Generation Request has one stored seed.

Seed may be:

  • User supplied
  • Derived from idempotency key
  • Generated once and persisted
  • Derived from Channel and horizon under configured policy

docs.title: Seed Storage
docs.text: The actual seed used is stored verbatim in plan metadata.

docs.title: Random Algorithm
docs.text: The pseudo-random algorithm is versioned.

docs.title: Random Streams
docs.text:
Independent streams should exist for:

  • Candidate tie-break
  • Weighted selection
  • Filler selection
  • Presentation selection
  • Template variation
  • Backtracking branch order

docs.title: Random Stream Derivation
docs.text:
A stream may derive from:

  • Root seed
  • Channel ID
  • Horizon
  • Cursor instant
  • Block ID
  • Concern name
  • Candidate ID
  • Generator version

docs.title: Random Independence
docs.text: Adding one random decision in one concern should not shift all later decisions in unrelated concerns.

docs.title: Deterministic Tie-Break
docs.text:
The tie-break must not depend on:

  • Database row order
  • Thread scheduling
  • Object hash randomization
  • Current wall clock
  • Unordered map iteration
  • Process-global state
  • Host platform

docs.title: Weighted Selection
docs.text:
Weighted selection:

  • Uses deterministic random source
  • Uses stable Candidate ordering
  • Uses nonnegative weights
  • Defines zero-weight behavior
  • Records selected weight
  • Records draw
  • Records pool checksum

docs.title: Weight Semantics
docs.text: Weights are not probabilities until normalized in the current pool.

docs.title: Reproducibility Contract
docs.text:
Given identical:

  • Generator version
  • Rule versions
  • Randomization version
  • Input revisions
  • Catalog Snapshot
  • History snapshot
  • Horizon
  • Seed
  • Generation mode
  • Locks
  • Fixed events
  • Budgets

ChannelForge must produce the same ordered Schedule Entries and relevant diagnostics.

docs.title: Placement Inputs
docs.text:
• Candidate duration
  • Cursor
  • Upcoming boundaries
  • Required lead-in
  • Required lead-out
  • Block policy
  • Daypart policy
  • Trim eligibility
  • Overrun tolerance
  • Minimum useful gap
  • Filler availability
  • Locked intervals
  • Fixed events

docs.title: Placement Result
docs.text:
entries
newCursor
boundaryInteraction
fillerRequirement
presentationEntries
warnings
appliedPolicy
rejectionReason

docs.title: Exact Placement
docs.text: Starts at cursor and uses full scheduling duration.

docs.title: Aligned Placement
docs.text:
Targets:

  • Top of hour
  • Half hour
  • Quarter hour
  • Block start
  • Fixed-event start

Filler may be inserted before aligned content.

docs.title: Trimmed Placement
docs.text:
Only explicitly trim-safe media may be trimmed.

Ordinary movies and episodes are not trim-safe by default.

docs.title: Overrun Placement
docs.text:
Overrun policy defines:

  • Maximum duration
  • Allowed media kinds
  • Boundary types
  • Following-block adjustment
  • Guide behavior
  • Approval warning

docs.title: Carry-In
docs.text:
Carry-In represents content begun before the requested horizon.

It records:

  • Original entry reference
  • Original start
  • Visible start
  • Remaining duration
  • Continuity evidence

docs.title: Carry-Out
docs.text:
Carry-Out extends beyond requested horizon when policy permits.

Full entry interval is retained.

Coverage uses intersection with requested horizon.

docs.title: Boundary Policies
docs.text:
• HARD_STOP
  • MUST_START_AT
  • MUST_END_AT
  • PREFER_START_AT
  • PREFER_END_AT
  • ALLOW_OVERRUN
  • FILL_TO_BOUNDARY
  • IGNORE

docs.title: Hard Stop
docs.text: No ordinary entry crosses the boundary.

docs.title: Must Start At
docs.text:
Target content begins exactly at boundary.

Preceding interval must be filled or explicitly Off-Air.

docs.title: Must End At
docs.text: Selected sequence ends exactly at boundary.

docs.title: Prefer Start or End
docs.text:
Alignment affects score.

Violation records warning.

docs.title: Fill to Boundary
docs.text: Filler or presentation content fills remaining interval.

docs.title: Fixed Events
docs.text:
A Fixed Event may represent:

  • Scheduled movie premiere
  • Imported special
  • Manual event
  • Live-event placeholder
  • Maintenance window
  • Network launch
  • Holiday special

docs.title: Fixed Event Fields
docs.text:
fixedEventId
channelId
startInstant
endInstant
entryDefinition
priority
lockPolicy
conflictPolicy
createdBy
createdAt
revision

docs.title: Fixed Event Conflict
docs.text:
Conflict may:

  • Fail generation
  • Move soft event
  • Backtrack earlier placement
  • Insert filler
  • Require operator resolution

Hard Fixed Events are never silently displaced.

docs.title: Manual Placements
docs.text: Manual placement creates an explicit required entry or locked segment.

docs.title: Lock Types
docs.text:
• Entry lock
  • Interval lock
  • Start-time lock
  • Content lock
  • Sequence lock
  • Boundary lock

docs.title: Lock Preservation
docs.text:
Regeneration preserves locks unless:

  • Actor explicitly unlocks
  • Lock is invalid
  • Lock references missing data and policy allows conflict handling

docs.title: Lock Evidence
docs.text: Plan records lock source and preservation outcome.

docs.title: Filler
docs.text: Filler provides intentional coverage.

docs.title: Filler Kinds
docs.text:
• Shorts
  • Trailers
  • Promos
  • Bumpers
  • Idents
  • Music videos
  • Slates
  • Loopable media
  • Explicit Off-Air

docs.title: Filler Policy
docs.text:
Includes:

  • Eligible selectors
  • Minimum interval
  • Maximum interval
  • Repeat policy
  • Priority
  • Trim behavior
  • Loop behavior
  • Audio policy
  • Guide representation
  • Maximum filler share
  • Failure fallback

docs.title: Filler Selection
docs.text:
Considers:

  • Remaining gap
  • Asset duration
  • Repeat cooldown
  • Presentation role
  • Network identity
  • Exact-fit preference
  • Entry-count limit
  • Trim capability
  • Loop capability

docs.title: Filler Packing
docs.text:
Version 1 may use bounded deterministic heuristics:

  1. Exact fit
  2. Largest valid item leaving fillable remainder
  3. Smallest remainder
  4. Lowest repeat penalty
  5. Stable deterministic tie-break

docs.title: Packing Budget
docs.text: Search depth and candidate count are bounded.

docs.title: Filler Failure
docs.text:
If no fill exists:

  • Backtrack
  • Insert Off-Air if configured
  • Permit overrun if configured
  • Fail interval

docs.title: Explicit Off-Air
docs.text:
Off-Air requires:

  • Start
  • End
  • Guide representation
  • Playout behavior
  • Optional slate
  • Policy or reason

docs.title: Presentation Insertion
docs.text:
Presentation roles may occur:

  • Before program
  • After program
  • Between programs
  • At hour boundary
  • At Block start
  • At Daypart start
  • During maintenance
  • During fallback

docs.title: Presentation Asset Selection
docs.text:
Selection uses:

  • Branding revision
  • Asset assignment
  • Date range
  • Daypart
  • Placement role
  • Cooldown
  • Priority
  • Weight
  • Duration fit
  • Deterministic random stream

docs.title: Presentation Entry Rule
docs.text:
Presentation entries are explicit Schedule Entries.

They are not hidden runtime behavior when editorial timing depends on them.

docs.title: Presentation Duration
docs.text: Use verified media duration.

docs.title: Missing Presentation Asset
docs.text:
Policy may:

  • Skip optional asset
  • Use fallback asset
  • Use slate
  • Fail Block
  • Record warning

docs.title: Bounded Backtracking
docs.text:
Greedy placement may fail even when a valid schedule exists.

Version 1 supports bounded backtracking.

docs.title: Backtracking Checkpoint
docs.text:
A checkpoint may capture:

  • Cursor
  • Entry count
  • Working history
  • Progression state
  • Quota state
  • Candidate exclusions
  • Random stream positions
  • Remaining budget

docs.title: Backtracking Triggers
docs.text:
• Hard boundary cannot be met
  • Fixed Event conflict
  • Unfillable gap
  • Hard quota failure
  • Sequence dead end
  • Progression dead end
  • Filler packing failure

docs.title: Backtracking Limits
docs.text:
Limits include:

  • Maximum depth
  • Maximum branches
  • Maximum elapsed time
  • Maximum candidate evaluations
  • Maximum checkpoint count

docs.title: Backtracking Determinism
docs.text: Branch order is stable and versioned.

docs.title: Terminal Failure
docs.text: When bounded search cannot find a valid plan, generation fails with structured diagnostics.

docs.title: Failure Fields
docs.text:
failureCode
stage
cursor
localContext
activeDayparts
activeBlocks
upcomingBoundaries
candidatePoolSize
hardExclusionSummary
placementFailureSummary
backtrackingAttempts
earliestCheckpoint
budgetUsage
suggestedRemediation

docs.title: Failure Codes
docs.text:
Potential codes:

  • NO_ELIGIBLE_CANDIDATE
  • UNFILLABLE_GAP
  • HARD_BOUNDARY_CONFLICT
  • FIXED_EVENT_CONFLICT
  • LOCK_CONFLICT
  • HARD_QUOTA_IMPOSSIBLE
  • SERIES_PROGRESSION_BLOCKED
  • MISSING_REQUIRED_ASSET
  • INVALID_CONFIGURATION
  • CATALOG_SNAPSHOT_INVALID
  • HISTORY_SNAPSHOT_INVALID
  • BUDGET_EXHAUSTED
  • CANCELLED
  • INTERNAL_ERROR

docs.title: Failure Remediation
docs.text:
Diagnostics may suggest:

  • Add filler
  • Broaden Selector
  • Relax hard constraint
  • Move Fixed Event
  • Unlock entry
  • Permit Off-Air
  • Increase horizon budget
  • Fix missing episode
  • Resolve Catalog availability
  • Correct invalid rule

Suggestions are diagnostic.

They do not mutate configuration.

docs.title: Rule Registry
docs.text: Rule implementations are registered through a typed internal registry.

docs.title: Rule Registration
docs.text:
Includes:

  • Rule type
  • Rule version
  • Classification
  • Parameter schema
  • Evaluator
  • Explanation formatter
  • Cost classification
  • Compatibility range
  • Migration function

docs.title: Unknown Rule
docs.text:
Unknown rule type cannot activate.

Imported unknown rule may remain preserved and disabled.

docs.title: Rule Cost Classification
docs.text:
• CHEAP
  • MODERATE
  • EXPENSIVE
  • HISTORY_HEAVY
  • CANDIDATE_SET_WIDE

docs.title: Rule Evaluation Order
docs.text: The engine should evaluate cheap hard constraints before expensive work.

docs.title: Rule Parameter Security
docs.text:
Rule parameters are untrusted input.

They must not enable:

  • Arbitrary code execution
  • Recursive unbounded expressions
  • Arbitrary SQL
  • Arbitrary file access
  • Arbitrary provider access
  • Secret lookup
  • Unbounded candidate expansion

docs.title: Algorithm Versioning
docs.text:
The plan records:

  • Overall generator version
  • Candidate-query version
  • Constraint version
  • Scoring version
  • Quota version
  • Progression version
  • Randomization version
  • Placement version
  • Filler version
  • Backtracking version
  • Validator version

docs.title: Version Change
docs.text: A version change capable of altering output must be visible in plan metadata.

docs.title: Compatibility Range
docs.text: Rule and generator versions declare supported Programming Configuration Revision ranges.

docs.title: Schedule Validation
docs.text: Validation is separate from generation.

docs.title: Validation Result
docs.text:
validationResultId
schedulePlanId
validatorVersion
planChecksum
state
findings
coverageMetrics
ruleComplianceMetrics
guideCompletenessMetrics
outputCompatibilityMetrics
createdAt

docs.title: Validation States
docs.text:
• VALID
  • VALID_WITH_WARNINGS
  • INVALID
  • ERROR

docs.title: Validation Checks
docs.text:
• Horizon coverage
  • Entry duration
  • Entry order
  • No unintended overlap
  • Gap policy
  • Boundary policy
  • Fixed Event placement
  • Lock preservation
  • Catalog references
  • Availability policy
  • Rule compliance
  • Daypart compliance
  • Block compliance
  • Progression
  • Repeat policy
  • Quotas
  • Guide metadata
  • Presentation assets
  • Output compatibility
  • Time-zone context
  • Checksum
  • Revision existence
  • Staleness

docs.title: Coverage Validation
docs.text:
Required coverage intervals must be occupied by:

  • Program
  • Presentation
  • Filler
  • Slate
  • Off-Air
  • Carry-In
  • Carry-Out intersection

docs.title: Gap Validation
docs.text:
Every gap is classified:

  • Intended Off-Air
  • Allowed gap
  • Invalid gap
  • Publication handoff
  • Outside requested horizon

docs.title: Validation Finding
docs.text:
Fields:

  • Code
  • Severity
  • Entry IDs
  • Interval
  • Rule ID
  • Message
  • Evidence
  • Suggested action
  • Acknowledgement requirement

docs.title: Finding Severity
docs.text:
• INFO
  • WARNING
  • ERROR
  • BLOCKING

docs.title: Validation Determinism
docs.text: Same plan and validator version produce same findings.

docs.title: Validation Checksum
docs.text:
Validation records the plan checksum.

Approval verifies the checksum.

docs.title: Approval
docs.text: Approval is an explicit application command.

docs.title: Approval Record
docs.text:
approvalRecordId
schedulePlanId
planChecksum
validationResultId
approvedBy
approvedAt
approvalMode
warningAcknowledgements
note
expectedProgressionVersions
expectedPublicationRevision

docs.title: Approval Modes
docs.text:
• MANUAL
  • AUTOMATIC_POLICY
  • MIGRATION
  • EMERGENCY_OVERRIDE

docs.title: Approval Preconditions
docs.text:
• Plan status eligible
  • Validation matches checksum
  • No blocking finding
  • Required warnings acknowledged
  • Staleness policy satisfied
  • Expected progression versions match
  • Authorization succeeds
  • Approval mode permitted

docs.title: Automatic Approval
docs.text:
Automatic approval is permitted only by explicit policy.

It still creates Approval Record.

docs.title: Approval Effects
docs.text:
Approval:

  • Marks plan approved through immutable status record or equivalent
  • Commits progression proposals
  • Preserves plan checksum
  • Emits approval event
  • Does not publish automatically unless a separate policy command follows
  • Does not mutate entries

docs.title: Approval Race
docs.text:
Approval verifies:

  • Plan still eligible
  • Validation still current
  • No conflicting approval
  • Progression version
  • Publication precondition
  • Staleness state

docs.title: Rejection
docs.text: A plan may be rejected.

docs.title: Rejection Record
docs.text:
• Plan ID
  • Actor
  • Timestamp
  • Reason
  • Findings
  • Replacement request
  • Audit

Rejected plan remains historical.

docs.title: Publication Separation
docs.text:
Approval does not equal publication.

Milestone 08 activates Schedule Publication.

docs.title: Existing Output Safety
docs.text: Failed generation, failed validation, or rejected approval must not replace the active published plan.

docs.title: Regeneration
docs.text: Regeneration creates a new Plan ID.

docs.title: Regeneration Inputs
docs.text:
• Source Plan ID
  • Selected range
  • Locks
  • New revisions
  • New Catalog Snapshot
  • New seed or preserved seed
  • Reason
  • Actor
  • Policy

docs.title: Full Regeneration
docs.text: Creates an entirely new plan.

docs.title: Range Regeneration
docs.text: Preserves outside entries.

docs.title: Regeneration Freeze Window
docs.text:
A freeze window protects near-term published entries.

Override requires:

  • Permission
  • Reason
  • Audit
  • Acknowledgement
  • Publication coordination

docs.title: Seed Policy During Regeneration
docs.text:
Policy may:

  • Preserve original root seed
  • Derive range seed from original
  • Use new seed
  • Use actor-supplied seed

Actual seed is recorded.

docs.title: Regeneration Lineage
docs.text: New plan records source plan and regenerated interval.

docs.title: Lock Copy
docs.text:
Locks outside range are preserved.

Locks inside range remain unless explicitly removed.

docs.title: Gap Repair
docs.text:
Gap repair creates a new plan with explicit lineage.

It never patches the approved plan in place.

docs.title: Staleness
docs.text: A plan may become stale after generation.

docs.title: Staleness States
docs.text:
• CURRENT
  • CONFIGURATION_STALE
  • CATALOG_STALE
  • AVAILABILITY_STALE
  • BRANDING_STALE
  • OUTPUT_STALE
  • HISTORY_STALE
  • ALGORITHM_STALE
  • MULTIPLE

docs.title: Configuration Stale
docs.text: Relevant active revision changed.

docs.title: Catalog Stale
docs.text: Scheduling-relevant Catalog revision changed after Snapshot.

docs.title: Availability Stale
docs.text: Required Catalog Item or variant eligibility changed.

docs.title: Branding Stale
docs.text: Required Presentation Asset became invalid or unavailable.

docs.title: Output Stale
docs.text: Output compatibility profile changed.

docs.title: History Stale
docs.text: New approved or aired history changes repeat or progression interpretation.

docs.title: Algorithm Stale
docs.text: Generator or rule implementation version changed.

docs.title: Staleness Severity
docs.text:
• Informational
  • Warning
  • Approval-blocking
  • Publication-blocking
  • Runtime-critical

docs.title: Approved Plan Staleness
docs.text:
An approved plan remains immutable.

Staleness may:

  • Trigger regeneration recommendation
  • Block publication
  • Warn operator
  • Permit publication under policy
  • Trigger runtime fallback preparation

docs.title: Plan Comparison
docs.text:
Comparison should identify:

  • Entry additions
  • Entry removals
  • Time changes
  • Content changes
  • Presentation changes
  • Boundary changes
  • Rule explanation changes
  • Filler share
  • Repeat metrics
  • Quota metrics
  • Guide changes
  • Staleness changes

docs.title: Legacy Scheduler Compatibility
docs.text: Inherited Tunarr scheduling remains isolated behind compatibility.

docs.title: Migration Flow
docs.text:
A migrated Channel may:

  1. Retain current operational schedule.
  2. Receive Network and Channel IDs.
  3. Receive Draft Programming Configuration Revision.
  4. Generate preview ChannelForge plan.
  5. Compare legacy and ChannelForge output.
  6. Validate.
  7. Approve.
  8. Publish through later explicit cutover.

docs.title: Legacy Generation Mode
docs.text:
A temporary legacy generation mode may remain.

It must:

  • Be clearly identified
  • Use compatibility adapters
  • Record usage
  • Not define ChannelForge canonical rule model
  • Have removal criteria

docs.title: Legacy Comparison
docs.text:
Comparison may normalize:

  • IDs
  • Guide formatting
  • Known boundary differences
  • Known filler differences
  • Legacy random behavior

docs.title: Legacy Comparison Metrics
docs.text:
• Coverage
  • Entry count
  • Program share
  • Filler share
  • Repeat intervals
  • Series order
  • Daypart compliance
  • Boundary alignment
  • Guide continuity
  • Availability failures

docs.title: Legacy Cutover Gate
docs.text:
Do not switch publication until:

  • Preview generated
  • Validation passes
  • Critical comparison differences understood
  • Required locks preserved
  • Operator approves
  • Rollback exists
  • Last-known-good plan remains

docs.title: Persistence
docs.text:
Scheduling persistence owns:

  • Generation Requests
  • Generation Attempts
  • Schedule Plans
  • Schedule Entries
  • Rule Evidence
  • Validation Results
  • Approval Records
  • Rejection Records
  • Locks
  • Fixed Events
  • Progression proposals
  • Plan lineage
  • Staleness records
  • Metrics summaries

docs.title: Persistence Rule
docs.text: Generation should avoid long write transactions.

docs.title: Plan Persistence
docs.text:
Preferred sequence:

  1. Generate in memory or explicit checkpoint store.
  2. Validate draft representation.
  3. Begin bounded transaction.
  4. Insert Plan metadata.
  5. Insert entries in bounded or optimized form.
  6. Insert evidence references.
  7. Insert validation.
  8. Commit.
  9. Emit completion event.

docs.title: Generation Checkpointing
docs.text:
Long generation may support internal checkpoints.

Checkpoint must not expose partially valid plan as publishable.

docs.title: Immutable Entry Storage
docs.text: Schedule Entries are never updated after plan persistence.

docs.title: Plan Checksum
docs.text:
Checksum covers semantic fields including:

  • Ordered entries
  • Input revision IDs
  • Catalog Snapshot
  • Seed
  • Versions
  • Time zone
  • Horizon
  • Locks
  • Fixed events

docs.title: Evidence Storage
docs.text:
Evidence may be:

  • Per-entry normalized records
  • Compressed structured document
  • Hybrid summary plus diagnostic archive

docs.title: Evidence Retention
docs.text:
Approved-plan evidence must remain sufficient for explanation.

Full rejected-candidate matrices may use bounded retention.

docs.title: Per-Channel Generation Lock
docs.text: Only one publication-changing generation workflow should own a Channel at a time.

docs.title: Preview Concurrency
docs.text: Preview and simulation may run concurrently within resource limits.

docs.title: Configuration Change During Generation
docs.text:
Generation uses immutable revisions.

Later activation does not alter running job.

Result may be stale.

docs.title: Catalog Change During Generation
docs.text: Catalog Snapshot keeps Candidate set stable.

docs.title: Approval Concurrency
docs.text: Approval uses optimistic concurrency.

docs.title: Progression Concurrency
docs.text: Approval commits expected progression versions.

docs.title: Cancellation
docs.text:
A Generation Job accepts cancellation.

Cancellation:

  • Stops candidate loops
  • Stops further backtracking
  • Preserves Attempt diagnostics
  • Does not persist partial valid Plan
  • Releases Channel generation lease
  • Preserves active publication

docs.title: Runtime Budget
docs.text: Generation Request may specify maximum runtime.

docs.title: Candidate Evaluation Budget
docs.text: Generation Request may specify maximum Candidate evaluations.

docs.title: Budget Exhaustion
docs.text:
Produces structured terminal failure.

It does not silently return partial plan as valid.

docs.title: Performance Requirements
docs.text:
Representative targets include:

  • Tens of thousands of Catalog Items
  • Dozens of Channels
  • Horizons of days or weeks
  • Thousands of entries per Channel
  • Multiple Sources
  • Controlled concurrent jobs

docs.title: Performance Principles
docs.text:
• Filter indexed hard constraints first
  • Load bounded history
  • Cache immutable rule inputs during generation
  • Use bounded Candidate Pools
  • Bound backtracking
  • Bound diagnostics
  • Avoid external calls
  • Avoid long write transactions
  • Measure stages
  • Use deterministic fixtures

docs.title: Candidate Query Performance
docs.text:
Required indexes should support:

  • Media kind
  • Availability
  • Duration
  • Series
  • Genre
  • Label
  • Collection
  • Rating
  • Catalog Snapshot membership
  • Stable ID ordering

docs.title: History Query Performance
docs.text: Load only windows required by active repeat and progression rules.

docs.title: Memory Bound

docs.title: Multi-Channel Coordination

  • Stagger time-shift feed

docs.title: Reference Scenario
docs.text:
Example:

  • Horizon: Monday 18:00 to Tuesday 02:00 local
  • Prime Time: 18:00 to 22:00
  • Late Night: 22:00 to 02:00
  • Fixed movie: 20:00
  • Movie duration: 110 minutes
  • Episodes: 42 minutes
  • Bumpers: 30 seconds
  • Filler: 5, 10, and 15 minutes

A valid result may include:

18:00:00  Episode A
18:42:00  Bumper
18:42:30  Episode B
19:24:30  Bumper
19:25:00  15-minute filler
19:40:00  10-minute filler
19:50:00  10-minute filler
20:00:00  Fixed Movie
21:50:00  Bumper
21:50:30  9.5-minute trim-safe filler
22:00:00  Late Night begins

The explanation identifies:

  • Selection reasons
  • Runtime-fit exclusions
  • Filler reasons
  • Fixed-event precedence
  • Boundary alignment
  • Quota impact

docs.text:

  • Duration is known.
  • A supported playable source exists.
  • Rights and Playability Status permit the intended output.
  • Availability is acceptable in the planning snapshot.
  • Network and Channel assignment matches.
  • Content and tag filters pass.
  • Automatic scheduling is explicitly enabled.

docs.title: Plan Rollback

Plans are immutable.

Rollback means selecting another approved plan later through Publication.

Approval is historical.

  • Expected version
  • No incompatible later approval
  • Audit
  • Operator authorization

docs.title: Regeneration Rollback

  • validation
  • cost classification

  • UI distinction
  • tests

  • UI labeling

docs.title: Backtracking Explosion

  • bounded pools
  • checkpoints
  • cost metrics
  • structured failure

  • indexes
  • precomputed summaries

docs.title: Progression Race
docs.text:

docs.title: Snapshot Size

Mitigation:

  • stable paging
  • retention

docs.title: Filler Dead End

Mitigation:

  • backtracking
  • Off-Air
  • diagnostics

docs.title: Fixed Event Conflict
docs.text:

Mitigation:

  • lookahead
  • filler
  • backtracking
  • validation
  • operator remediation

docs.title: Lock Abuse
docs.text:
Too many locks may make regeneration impossible.

Mitigation:

  • visualization
  • permission
  • failure diagnostics

docs.title: Stale Approval
docs.text:
Configuration may change before approval.

Mitigation:

  • staleness policy
  • checksum
  • revision references
  • warnings

docs.title: Legacy Semantic Difference
docs.text:
New Network-first scheduler will not exactly match inherited behavior.

Mitigation:

  • preview
  • comparison
  • operator approval
  • rollback
  • explicit differences

docs.title: Diagnostic Volume
docs.text:
Candidate evidence may be large.

Mitigation:

  • levels
  • summaries
  • bounded retention
  • approved-entry evidence priority

docs.title: SQLite Persistence Cost

Mitigation:

  • optimized transaction
  • batches if safe
  • indexes
  • metrics
  • generation outside transaction
